Sports.title: Manchester United’s infamous 1974 relegation is a warning from history
Sports.content:
In many ways, there are striking parallels between the Manchester United relegated in 1974 and the Manchester United sitting in the relegation zone at this stage of the season for the first time in 40 years. A legendary manager leaves, his shadow remains; with boardroom dithering and uncertainty, his replacements churn and burn as the club slide over several years.

Sir Matt Busby stepped aside as manager of the 1968 European Cup-winning side, but stayed on as a director, just as Sir Alex Ferguson did, watching from the Old Trafford directors’ box as successors tried and failed.

In the six years after being crowned kings of Europe, United turned to Wilf McGuinness, Busby stepped in temporarily to keep them up, then Frank O’Farrell was appointed before they landed on Tommy Docherty, who experienced the ignominy of taking them down.

In the past eight years, United have sacked José Mourinho, Ole Gunnar Solskjær, Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and now Michael Carrick.

View image in fullscreen Tommy Docherty took an old and disjointed Manchester United down to the old Second Division … then back up at the first attempt. Photograph: Robert Stiggins/Getty Images

How did the United of 1974 go down? Most outsiders believed they were too big to fail. Inside the club, though, they sensed the direction of travel. After a heavy defeat at Crystal Palace in December 1972, Busby offered Docherty the job in the Selhurst Park boardroom. “There’s a lot of trouble in the camp,” Busby said. Docherty was doing well as Scotland manager and took a few days to mull it over, but decided he couldn’t turn down the opportunity.

When Busby called him on the Sunday evening, he accepted. “You know it won’t be easy?” Busby said. “It’ll be like turning an oil tanker round, only bigger.” He added: “You might find yourself having to take a step back in order to take a leap forward.” Docherty wrote in his autobiography, The Doc, that at the time he never believed Busby was alluding to relegation.

Docherty was given free rein for a rebuild. The day after his appointment, he signed George Graham from Arsenal for £120,000, a sizeable fee at the time. Alex Forsyth followed from Partick for £100,000 and Docherty pulled off a coup when he persuaded Lou Macari to join bottom-of-the-table United instead of Liverpool for £200,000.

View image in fullscreen George Best made his final appearance for Manchester United against Queens Park Rangers at Loftus Road on New Year’s Day in 1974. Photograph: Wesley/Getty Images

The giants of the previous era were moved on. In February, Bobby Charlton told him that, at 37, it would be his last season. Other big names wanted to stay, but Docherty felt a reset was needed. “The Manchester United team that had won the European Cup in 1968 was without a doubt a great team, but many members of that side had been allowed to grow old together,” he wrote.

“I knew what I had decided would prove very unpopular with many people but it had to be done. I set out my stall to end the United careers of among others Denis Law, Tony Dunne, Pat Crerand and David Sadler.”

George Best, who had retired once but returned under Docherty, played his last game on New Year’s Day 1974 after repeatedly turning up late. The most controversial departure was Law, who was allowed to join Manchester City.

Having taken over with United bottom, Docherty kept them up in his first season and was emboldened to continue his clearout. Thirteen players were released that summer. But halfway through the following season they were facing relegation again and a lack of goals cost them. At one stage, the joint-top scorer was Alex Stepney, with two penalties. He was the goalkeeper.

Relegation was confirmed on the penultimate day as they lost to City, a defeat made all the more painful by Law back-heeling the late winner. Docherty was interviewed on the Old Trafford pitch and asked, in a scene replayed in TNT Sports’ Too Good To Go Down, whether the club would drift into obscurity. “No, there’s no danger,” he said. “We could wash the jerseys here and hang them out to dry and you’d get 15,000 people standing watching them do so.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Despite the bravado, Docherty was expecting the sack when he met Busby a few days later. Instead, Busby handed him a case of champagne, reminded him of the oil tanker and told him to set to work getting them back up.

Docherty’s prediction proved right: the brand was far bigger than the division they played in. In the Second Division, Old Trafford averaged crowds of more than 47,000 – the biggest in the country – and their away support descended on towns and cities and routinely outnumbered the home contingent.

View image in fullscreen Stuart Pearson, who scored 17 goals for United during 1974-75 as they won the Second Division, celebrates against Blackpool on the last day. Photograph: Harry Ormesher/Popperfoto/Getty Images

Docherty bought young and hungry, targeting players with a point to prove, including Steve Coppell from Tranmere, Stuart Pearson from Hull and Jim Holton from Shrewsbury. The direct, attacking football synonymous with United returned and the Scot shaped a fearless 4-2-4 formation.

Crowds grew after they came straight back up and for a while United were on course to become the fifth side to win the First Division after promotion, but finished third and also reached the FA Cup final, losing 1-0 to Southampton. That shows the stark differences between then and now.

The gap between the first and second tiers was narrower. United did not lose a gargantuan broadcast deal when they went down. They were not saddled with debt by their owners. Their wage bill was not tied to Champions League qualification. Players were not on long contracts and were easier to buy and sell. There were no disruptive agents. Fans were more patient.

If lessons of the 1970s are not heeded soon, the fallout could be infinitely more painful.

Sports.title: Veerle Buurman scrambles late WCL winner to push blunt Chelsea past PSG
Sports.content:
Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.

Buurman had stolen the show in Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match, and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.

“She is a top, young talent and is so mature on and off the pitch,” said Sonia Bompastor. “She is a confident player and a really complete player.”

Bompastor’s side were frustrated by Häcken last week, held to a 0-0 draw by the Swedish side and falling out of the top four automatic qualification places. There was a desire to put things right at AFC Wimbledon’s stadium and they did just that, albeit in not the prettiest of encounters.

“Sometimes in football you need to find a way to win and the result tonight was really important for us,” said Bompastor.

Quick Guide WCL roundup: City subs Hemp and Shaw see off Häcken Show Lauren Hemp and Khadija Shaw both scored off the bench to earn Manchester City a 2-0 Women’s Champions League victory over Häcken in Gothenburg. The first half ended goalless with City's best chances coming just before the break. Aoba Fujino was put through on goal but she hit her effort straight at Häcken keeper Jennifer Falk, who made saves from Grace Clinton and Rebecca Knaak to keep the hosts on terms at the interval. Hemp and Shaw were both introduced at half-time by Andrée Jeglertz, and the England winger opened the scoring after 55 minutes. It was a fortuitous breakthrough, with Emma Östlund's clearance ricocheting off Hemp's shin and into the net [pictured]. Mary Fowler appeared to have added a second soon after, but her strike was ruled out for offside against Yui Hasegawa. Soon after Hemp was denied her second goal when her shot hit the post, she turned creator by passing to an onrushing Shaw, who tucked home for City's second in the 77th minute. The visitors could have had a third, but Falk saved Fowler's stoppage-time penalty after a VAR intervention. Signe Bruun also made the difference off the bench on Wednesday, scoring two late goals as Real Madrid wore down 10-woman Internazionale to win 3-1. The Danish forward put Madrid ahead five minutes of time before adding a late penalty to secure all three points. Lineth Beerensteyn got the hosts off the mark in Madrid after 28 minutes, and Inter faced an uphill battle after Karolina Vilhjalmsdottir was sent off three minutes before the break. The visitors got an unexpected equaliser when Michela Cambiaghi headed in from a corner, and held on until Bruun's late double. City and Real Madrid are both unbeaten after five league phase games, winning two and drawing three matches each as they bid to finish in the top four and avoid the playoffs. Juventus join them on nine points after late goals from Annamaria Serturini and Matilde Pavan earned a 2-0 home win over Leuven. PA and Guardian sport Photograph: Declan Lloyd/Manchester City FC Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

PSG had lost 2-1 at home to Bayern Munich after three draws and one win in the competition before their trip to London. Denied a point late on, they remain 10th and dangerously close to slipping out of the playoff places with one game to play.

Chelsea had been thrillingly gutsy and diligent in their 1-0 win over City on Saturday and against PSG they were similarly solid at the back, but they lacked spark in attack. Ellie Carpenter became the focal point of their forward play from the right, with the striker Melvine Malard injured in the game against City.

PSG nullifying the threat of Carpenter blunted Chelsea, and despite their dominance of the ball, amassing 64% possession in the first half, Chelsea struggled to carve a way through the visitors’ backline. They had seven attempts on goal to PSG’s six at the break, despite 33 attacks to 10.

Chelsea have historically performed well against PSG, winning three of their four Champions League meetings prior to this penultimate fixture of their league phase campaign. In the 2018-19 quarter-finals they earned a 2-0 home win and, after a 2-1 away defeat, progressed to the semi-finals; in the 2022-23 season they won both group meetings with an overall score of 4-0.

The visiting team’s first attempt on target arrived after the break, with Merveille Kanjinga forcing a near-post save from Hannah Hampton. While Chelsea still dominated, PSG had more forays forward in the second half.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Aggie Beever-Jones is beaten to a header by her Chelsea teammate Wieke Kaptein (right) in what was a close game against PSG. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

Erin Cuthbert, Maika Hamano and Lucy Bronze arrived at the hour mark as the home team sought to deal the killer blow their dominance required. It increasingly felt like it would take something special to break the deadlock, akin to the sublime effort that Sandy Baltimore had delivered against City.

Aggie Beever-Jones was replaced by Sjoeke Nüsken late on and the German instantly made a difference, forcing a sublime save from Katarzyna Kiedrzynek. The breakthrough came from the resulting corner, and it was far less sublime than Saturday’s effort, Buurman somehow squeezing the ball in at the near post after PSG failed to clear Cuthbert’s ball in.

“The main feeling is one of frustration,” said the PSG manager, Paulo César. “We defended well, we just lacked a bit of clarity on the transition and I have mixed feelings. I’m proud of my team but it shows that there are very fine margins that we need to rival a big team like Chelsea.”

Ultimately, the goal was the bit of luck Chelsea needed and they look increasingly formidable.

Sports.title: Leicester part ways with BC Game after sponsor’s partnership with porn actor
Sports.content:
Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt sponsor, BC Game, after the cryptocurrency casino’s partnership with a porn actor sparked a fan backlash. BC Game, an offshore company registered in Belize that is unlicensed to operate in the UK, had been Leicester’s main sponsor since 2024.

This month BC Game named Eva Elfie a brand ambassador, leading the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, to highlight the “devastating impacts” caused by gambling and pornography. On Wednesday the club said they prematurely ended their agreement with the online betting firm after they “recognised our differing commercial priorities”.

It is understood Leicester directly raised concerns with BC Game about the implications of their deal with Elfie, a Russian porn actor who BC Game said had “an established presence in gaming communities”. Leicester’s deal with BC Game, which began in July 2024, was due to run until the end of the season.

The trust had previously outlined concerns about the club’s partnership with BC Game. In a statement responding to the partnership this month, they said: “From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company we felt Leicester City were ditching its values.

“Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content. Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?”

Leicester, who visit Huddersfield in League One on Saturday, said supporters who purchased a shirt featuring BC Game branding within the past 28 days are able to exchange the shirt or are eligible for a full refund. The club added they would pay for the postage of returns via standard delivery.

Leicester remain for sale, with the club’s Thai owners, King Power, also seeking to sell their stadium, training base and women’s team.

In an unrelated development, the former Chelsea technical director Michael Emenalo is working as an adviser to the club, who are 11th in the third tier. Emenalo is among a team of Deloitte consultants Leicester say they have enlisted to “assess its current operations and inform its future strategic planning”.

Sports.title: Emma Hayes to assist in US Soccer hiring process for next USMNT coach
Sports.content:
The US women’s national team head coach, Emma Hayes, said she was “confident in the group that is being put together” to select her next counterpart for the men’s team – a group that includes her.

Speaking after announcing her team’s squad for the ­Concacaf championship and World Cup qualifier, Hayes shed light for the first time on her role in searching for Mauricio Pochettino’s replacement after the Argentinian decamped to Manchester United. US Soccer had previously said Hayes – alongside the federation CEO, JT Batson, the chief operating officer, Dan Helfrich, and Oguchi Onyewu, the vice-president of sporting – would assist with the search.

“Listen, I’m very embedded into the federation, and I work really closely with JT, in particular, and even more so with Dan as we’re growing to develop the American soccer movement,” Hayes said. “And you know, JT asked if I would be involved as a technical voice to be involved with the process. And I feel confident in the group of people that have been put together to create a thorough process to select the next men’s national team coach – my role is merely to support that through a technical lens, knowing I do this job … albeit with the women’s team, and that I’ve coached for a number of years, and can offer some of that insight into the application of what to look for and why.”

Hayes résumé spans 25 years and is distinguished, having coached at the very highest level for club and country alike. The Englishwoman, who took over the US team in 2024, moved from being the assistant coach at Arsenal to taking charge of the Chicago Red Stars in Women’s Professional Soccer in 2008, and later moved to Chelsea, winning the Women’s Super League seven times. Since accepting the US job, she has guided the women to an Olympic gold medal and taken on an expansive role at the federation as it looks to overhaul and grow the women’s game.

“I think it will be a very thorough process,” Hayes said. “I think that’s the most important part of it. I feel very embedded in what we’re doing with the federation, so it doesn’t feel unusual to me [to help with the search]. So, like I’ve said many times, let’s build off the good work that Mauricio has done. I think that’s the important part, and let’s get it right.”

Hayes offered a heartfelt goodbye to Pochettino on the TNT broadcast of the his final match with the USMNT on Tuesday night, a 2-0 victory over Haiti in their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final. “I just want to say thank you on behalf of all of us at US Soccer, it’s been a privilege to work with you here, see the amazing work you’ve done with the team,” she said. “I think you’ve left an amazing foundation for someone to come in and build on that great work and the good feeling and certainly the good habits you’ve left with the team. You’ve left a lasting impression on the American people.

Pochettino replied on the broadcast, saying: “I admire a lot Emma. She is a wonderful coach, and a wonderful person. It was an honor to share [this experience] with her.”

Sports.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
Sports.content:
The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.

Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.

There also appears to be a clear frontrunner. “I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes,” one experienced media rights buyer told the Guardian.

Multiple sources have confirmed that Netflix would submit a bid before Thursday’s deadline for first-round offers, along with their fellow streamers Apple TV, Disney, Amazon, YouTube and Dazn, as well as the traditional broadcasting heavyweights, Fox, ESPN, NBC Universal and Skydance, although the last of these may find itself constrained by the budget cuts being made after its $110bn acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. Netflix has already bought exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cups.

“There’s a huge range of buyers and therefore a broad range of possible outcomes,” one broadcasting veteran says. “All the media companies and streamers will bid. Fox will find it very challenging to retain the rights.”

In a significant change, Fifa is selling the English and Spanish rights together for the first time, a move that indicates it is seeking a single exclusive rights holder, which would suit the streaming companies. With Fox having paid $485m for exclusive English-language rights to the 2026 World Cup, and NBC Universal’s Telemundo paying $600m for the Spanish-language rights, the only certainty is that the 2030 price will be far higher, despite less attractive kick-off times for a US audience as the tournament is in Morocco, Spain and Portugal.

The impact of the time difference is hard to price, but may not prove to be that significant given the seemingly insatiable demand. NBC paid about $1.5bn for exclusive rights for the 2024 Paris Olympics and were rewarded with average daily viewing figures of more than 30 million, albeit with far more variation in programming than a World Cup.

Fifa awarded non-competitive extensions to Fox and Telemundo in 2015 as compensation for moving the 2022 Qatar World Cup to winter, a perspective that was strengthened on the back of this year’s record-breaking tournament. Fox’s live coverage of Spain’s extra-time victory over Argentina in the final was the most-watched soccer telecast in US history, with a peak audience of 51.685 million; five World Cup games brought in average audiences of more than 20 million; and the average viewing figure across all 104 matches was 7.7 million, twice the figure in Qatar four years earlier.

Telemundo’s coverage, available through NBC’s streaming platform Peacock, averaged a total audience of 6 million viewers per game, with Spain v Argentina and Mexico v England attracting peak audiences of more than 23 million, the highest-ever for Spanish-language broadcasts in the US.

The bumper audiences were extremely lucrative for the broadcasters, with figures from the advertising sales analysts Guideline showing that Fox and Telemundo generated a combined $1.19bn in advertising revenue alone during the tournament, almost three times the figure from Qatar four years earlier and more than their original rights investment.

Fox alone brought in $835m from World Cup advertising, with 30-second slots costing between $200,000 and $750,000 according to the Hollywood Reporter, and the six-minute hydration breaks generating between $2m and $9m per game.

View image in fullscreen The 2026 World Cup final was the most-watched soccer telecast in US history. Photograph: Lars Baron/Getty Images

Having left a considerable amount of money on the table because of the circumstances of the 2026 process, Fifa is determined to cash in this time around. Holding the auction only four months after the US hosted the World Cup appears a clear attempt to capitalise on the success of the previous tournament, which contributed the vast majority of Fifa’s $4bn media revenues over the four-year cycle to 2026.

The addition of hydration breaks will give bidders such as Fox more revenue to play with, although Fifa will expect the option for extra adverts to drive up the price and take its own cut this time around, having missed out in the summer. The two three-minute breaks in each half were only finalised last year and did not feature in the 2026 tender documents.

“Sports advertising is much more valuable than entertainment programming as it has a broader reach,” says François Godard, an independent media analyst. “And one-off events such as World Cups do not generally do particularly well for subscription services, who want year-round content.

“Fox in particular needs the World Cup and is heavily associated with it. They are the smallest of the legacy broadcasters and are reliant on sport, as well as news. Having said that, the market for sport amongst streamers is far more competitive in the US than in Europe. Netflix, Amazon and YouTube have all bought NFL rights, while Apple is investing heavily in Formula One, so I wouldn’t rule any of them out.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Adam Kelly, president of the global sports marketing agency IMG, has a seat at the table at many rights negotiations and has long predicted the rise of the streamers, viewing the 2030 World Cup as the potential tipping point when a premium event could be exclusively bought in a major market by a streaming service for the first time. IMG has the rights to sell more than 70 global sports organisations, including the Premier League, World Rugby and Wimbledon.

In addition to the exclusive rights in the US for the 2027 and 2031 Women’s World Cups, Netflix has secured exclusive 2030 World Cup rights in Spain. It must sublicense all of the Spanish national team’s matches, both semi-finals and final and at least one match per day to a domestic free-to-air broadcaster to comply with government regulations.

“These entities are the future of broadcasting, as they are the best companies in the world at turning attention into earnings,” Kelly says of the streamers. “Their model allows them to monetise better than their rivals due to their size, scale and the high consumption levels of their customers.

“Netflix in particular has built a sophisticated and lucrative advertising platform. They have the back-office capability and 2027 would provide a perfect test run. If they’re successful in the tender for the World Cup it shows they are potentially the future of sports broadcasting.”

Netflix’s diversification into an advertising business, which brought in $1.5bn last year with projections of $2.7bn this year, puts it ahead of Apple TV and Amazon and well placed to make a profit from an undertaking as large as broadcasting a men’s World Cup. The lack of stipulations in the US for free-to-air coverage makes this tender particularly attractive to Netflix, although if successful it could make some matches available to non-subscribers for promotional purposes, as Apple TV has done with Major League Soccer.

“As a company, Netflix’s unique offering is exclusivity, so why would they hand that to their rivals?” another broadcast source said. “There are no regulations in the US preventing exclusivity so I would expect Netflix to bid for and retain every game if they win.”

Given recent reports that Netflix is exploring tabling an offer for NBC Universal after withdrawing its $85bn bid for Warner Bros last year, a future partnership with a linear network cannot be ruled out if it is successful. Some sources have even suggested that the tender has been timed deliberately to attract a competitive bid from Netflix, as the streamer is short of sports content to promote during the 2027 Women’s World Cup. Others argue that Fifa would have been better advised waiting to build further on the interest created by that tournament.

The NFL’s decision to pause its media rights process as it seeks an early renegotiation of contracts that are due to run to 2034 is likely to have played a part in the timing, creating a window of opportunity for Fifa to go to market. While a second round of bidding is possible after Thursday’s opening round, the outcome is expected to be known within the next few weeks and could present a bounce for Gianni Infantino as he continues his presidential re-election campaign.

Sports.title: ‘An honour’: Pochettino up for challenge of leading Manchester United revival
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino said it was “an honour” and “a privilege” to be the new Manchester United head coach after arriving in England on Wednesday.

Pochettino flew from Cincinnati to Manchester overnight after overseeing the USA beating Haiti in his final game in charge. Members of Pochettino’s staff landed earlier in the week to begin work at Carrington, laying the foundations as United seek to turn their season around. His right-hand man, Jesús Pérez, the goalkeeping coach Toni Jiménez and the fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino, who continues to work with his father, have already taken training with those not on international duty.

Those away with their national teams will return to the club on Thursday, when they are expected to meet Pochettino for the first time and hold meetings. Conversations have also been held with various departments within the club, as Pochettino sought to learn about the squad’s health as he seeks areas of improvement.

Pochettino’s first challenge will be at Anfield on Sunday, when 18th-placed United take on Liverpool. The 54-year-old has his eyes set on rattling Manchester City after being told on TNT Sports that “Manchester’s blue and always will be blue” by DaMarcus Beasley, who once had a loan spell with City. Pochettino responded: “No way. You will see. Give me time … give me time and that is going to start to change.”

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino arrives at Carrington for his first day as Manchester United’s new head coach. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

Speaking about joining United, Pochettino said: “It’s a big challenge but at the same time, it’s adrenaline that you want to feel because I think we are going to have a different job. But I think one of the things that is important is that we have the experience to deal with that, and I think we need to add our common sense and the way we are going to approach all the things.

“We know that the situation is not a situation that a club like Manchester United deserves,” Pochettino added. “The fanbase is amazing and after we signed here in America, of every 10 people I crossed in the street, nine are Manchester United fans. It’s amazing.”

Pochettino is also reunited with the strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya, the analyst Alec Scott and his long-term assistant, Miki D’Agostino, at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Fifa’s World Cup TV rights documents indicate hydration breaks to stay in 2030
Sports.content:
Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup include a provision for broadcasters to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication the controversial ­stoppages will be retained.

A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.

Fifa insists it has yet to decide whether hydration breaks will be used at the 2030 tournament, which will take place largely in Morocco, Spain and Portugal but will also feature three matches in South America, but the Guardian has learned the possibility and potential commercial benefits are flagged to broadcasters in the tender documents.

The global governing body has awarded World Cup rights to ­Netflix in Spain and to the public service broadcaster SBS in Australia, and the sales process for the US and Puerto Rico is continuing, with Thursday the deadline to bid.

The tender documents are also understood to reference cooling breaks, a welfare mechanism used by Uefa whereby play is stopped for between 90 seconds and three minutes if the on-field temperature reaches 28C.

Fifa sources told the Guardian the tenders were designed to cover all potential options.

Fifa used cooling breaks on an ad hoc basis before triggering the wholesale adoption of hydration breaks for the 2026 World Cup, despite 31 of the 104 games being played in climate-controlled stadiums, after high temperatures led to stoppages in about 60% of matches at the 2025 Club World Cup in the US. Fifa said the move was to protect the integrity of the World Cup by ensuring all matches were played in the same conditions, although there were also major commercial benefits for broadcasters.

The Hollywood Reporter reported last summer that hydration breaks were generating between $2m and $9m in advertising revenue a game, leading to claims that Fox brought in an estimated $250m.

Fox’s overall advertising yield from the tournament was $835m according to the media sales analyst Guideline, almost double the $485m rights fee paid to Fifa.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Fifa did not benefit financially last summer but the expectation of hydration breaks being included could drive up prices for 2030. The US rights are expected to fetch between $1.5bn and $2bn (£1.14bn-£1.52bn) in an auction that will feature bids from Netflix and all of the streaming services alongside traditional broadcasters.

Fifa declined to comment.

Mandatory hydration breaks will not be used at next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil, where temperatures are forecast to be cooler than they were in many cities at this year’s men’s tournament.

Sports.title: Overlap, underlap or sit back? How Premier League teams use their full-backs
Sports.content:
Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.

Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”

Between them, White and Calafiori have contributed to six goals for Arsenal already in the Premier League this season (White: three assists; Calafiori: one goal, two assists). No other defender has registered more than three goal involvements so far. The Arsenal duo are a great illustration of the impact full-backs can have. But, with the position more demanding than ever before, how does each Premier League team deploy theirs?

Where do full-backs take their touches?

The graphic below shows the average height and width of the touches of each Premier League team’s full-backs, sorted from highest average position to lowest. The most obvious takeaway is that Arsenal’s full-backs have the highest average touch location of any Premier League side this season, coming 58.2 metres from their own goal.

That is a reflection not only of Arsenal’s territorial dominance, but also the license White and Calafiori are given to push into the attacking line. White averages 3.4 touches in the opposition box per 90 minutes, the most of any full-back or wing-back in the division. Calafiori ranks third, with 2.9.

Arsenal’s full-backs also have the narrowest average touch locations of any team, emphasising how far they have moved away from the traditional full-back role of maintaining width. Instead, they are encouraged to drift inside and operate in central areas.

Tottenham also deploy their full-backs extremely high up the pitch. For most of the campaign, that has been Archie Gray at right-back and Andy Robertson on the left. Of course, analysing a player’s influence is not limited to what they do on the ball. Thanks to Opta Vision, we can also track what they do without it.

Gray is particularly noteworthy, given his exceptional work rate. He ranks first among Premier League full-backs for underlapping runs, both in total (23) and per 90 minutes (2.9), and also ranks fourth for overlapping runs per 90 (1.8). That shows the benefit of deploying an attack-minded player at full-back, with Gray showing energy and an ability to get beyond the ball and offer another option in the final third.

Robertson is no slouch on the opposite flank, either. The 32-year-old ranks seventh for underlapping runs per 90 minutes (1.4) and sits inside the top 20 for overlapping runs per 90 (1.1). He has also received more passes ending in the final third (159) than any other full-back.

It might be more of a surprise to see Coventry’s full-backs play so high, given they have not dominated the ball at all (39.1% possession, second-lowest) and they start their attacks from deep (40.2m away from goal, sixth-lowest). It is, however, something they did to good effect in the Championship last season (average height of 56.8m, sixth-highest).

Frank Lampard has also used a back five at times, which means his wing-backs naturally play higher up, but he has been brave with pushing his defensive line up in general. Coventry have provoked the second-most offsides of any team so far (30).

That has allowed Milan van Ewijk and Jay Dasilva to push forward on the flanks. The pair have each created eight chances, with only Jack Rudoni (12) creating more for the Sky Blues.

Dasilva is a particularly important outlet down the left. He takes his touches higher up the pitch than any other full-back in the division, and Coventry have created 42.2% of their open-play chances down his side, the highest proportion of any Premier League team.

Wing-backs v full-backs?

It makes sense that Nottingham Forest and Leeds also see their full-backs touch the ball high up the pitch, given they are two of the biggest users of wing-backs. That pair are two of just four teams that predominantly play with wing-backs, with the back three/five becoming a rare breed in the modern Premier League.

For Leeds, Jayden Bogle has been particularly influential going forwards. He has made more runs ending in the opposition box than any other full-back this season. They’ve come at an average of 3.9 per 90 minutes, the second-highest rate in the division, behind only Nico O’Reilly, who has played just 54.3% of his minutes at full-back.

Crystal Palace, meanwhile, are feeling the effects of losing the influential Daniel Muñoz. Despite playing solely with wing-backs, they have gone from having the highest average full-back positioning in the Premier League in 2025-26 to sitting below the league average this season. Muñoz was relentless in his work up and down the right flank last term, and his absence has clearly affected the extent to which Palace are able to push their right-sided wing-back up in those wide areas.

The Colombian is now at Nottingham Forest with his former manager Oliver Glasner. They have gone from having the fifth-lowest average touch location for their full-backs to the fourth-highest. That is not only down to Muñoz, but having someone who is able to put in consistent lung-busting runs – he is behind only Ipswich Town’s Leif Davis for the average length of his off-ball runs – helps a lot.

We can’t talk about the league’s most energetic full-backs without mentioning Adrien Truffert, who has continued where he left off last season. The Frenchman is the overlapping king, making more of those runs than any other full-back in the division (23). That comes after he made almost twice as many overlapping runs as any other player across the entire league last season. His manager, Andoni Iraola, may be gone, but he’s clearly got the same license to bomb on from Bournemouth’s new head coach, Marco Rose.

Continuity or change?

Iraola is now at Liverpool, and his full-backs are one of the most asymmetric duos in the league. Milos Kerkez – just as he did at Bournemouth under Iraola – has freedom to push forward and is one of the biggest overlappers in the league, completing 15 such runs thus far. On the other side, Ronald Araújo – who is more of a converted centre-back – plays a far more reserved role.

Manchester City are a curious case. Despite averaging the most possession in the division (65.4%), completing the most passes per game (566) and recording the highest territorial dominance, as measured by field tilt, Enzo Maresca’s team do not use their full-backs in advanced areas to exert that dominance.

Their average full-back touch location is 53.1 metres from goal, making them the fourth-deepest team in the division. That is a huge contrast from Pep Guardiola’s last season, when City ranked third-highest for average full-back positioning. There are plenty of ways to play full-back in the Premier League, but the growing importance of the position is the same for every team.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Mykhailo Mudryk not ruling out Chelsea renaissance as he names three clubs he held talks with before Tottenham loan
Sports.content:
Mykhailo Mudryk not ruling out Chelsea renaissance as he names three clubs he held talks with before Tottenham loan

Mykhailo Mudryk has revealed he held talks with Brighton, Brentford and Leeds before joining Tottenham from Chelsea.

The 25-year-old sealed a season-long loan deal with Spurs in August in a move that contains an option to buy worth £75million.



3 Mudryk was shipped off on loan to Spurs from Chelsea after his doping case was resolved Credit: Getty

Having not featured for the Blues in a competitive game since December 2024 due to a failed drugs test, Mudryk had been slapped with a four-year ban by FIFA.

But all charges against him were dropped in July, allowing him to instantly resume his football career.

Having featured under new Blues boss Xabi Alonso in pre-season, the west London outfit allowed him to depart in the summer with the Ukrainian seeking regular football.



talkSPORT reported how Leeds were the subject of two failed loan approaches for the pacey winger.

Brentford were another club looking to secure his services.

But in the end, Mudryk elected to reunite with his former Shakhtar Donetsk boss Roberto De Zerbi at Tottenham.



And during his appearance on Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk has revealed the Seagulls were another possible destination.

Discussing which clubs were interested in prising him away from Stamford Bridge, he confirmed he held talks with Brighton, Brentford and Leeds.



All three clubs he rejected currently sit above 11th-placed Spurs in the table.

How has Mudryk fared at Tottenham?

As it stands, his switch to north London hasn't gone to plan, having been limited to just 16 minutes of Premier League football this term.

3 Mudryk has scored ten goals in 73 games for the Blues across all competitions Credit: Getty

Mudryk's only outing this term has been his cameo off the bench in the 0-0 draw away at Nottingham Forest on September 5, with the forward picking up an ankle knock shortly after in training.



Though he could be available for selection in Spurs' home tie against Ipswich Town on Saturday.

What has Mudryk said about his Chelsea future?

Despite Spurs having an option to turn his temporary stay into a permanent switch, Mudryk has revealed a return to Chelsea remains in the pipeline.

Commenting on a discussion he had with Alonso before his exit, he claimed that the Spaniard is hopeful of having him in his squad next year

Mudyk said: "[Alonso] told me straight up to my face, ‘You better go and play and get some minutes,’ then come back.



"I am counting on you."

3 Mudryk will be hoping to win his place back in Ukraine's side in the March international break Credit: Getty

What has Mudryk said about his doping case?

In a stinging blast towards his home nation, Mudryk has claimed that he felt let down by a lack of support from the Ukrainian FA during his ban.

Having insisted that they 'offered no help,' he also stated: "They created more problems than they solved.

"When I needed the help the most, they turned their back."

And he also believes he consumed the banned substance meldonium while on international duty.



Mudryk remarked: "I had never of heard of a drug like meldonium, it is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe, it could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England."

Before adding: "The Ukrainian national team has absolutely no security system.

"At clubs, when you travel to an away game, there are always people responsible for what happens on the hotel floors and in the team. There are people who keep an eye on it.

"On the Ukrainian national team, we have a nutritionist who hands us pills, every couple of days before games, he brings us a little cup, everyone has to take the pills that are in that cup."

Sports.title: Luke Littler’s opponent breaks down in tears as he sends reigning champion crashing out
Sports.content:
Luke Littler’s opponent breaks down in tears as he sends reigning champion crashing out

Luke Littler's dream of winning a third successive Grand Slam of Darts title is over having lost to Jermaine Wattimena in the last-16.

The world no.1 was defeated 10-8 by his Dutch opponent in an epic thriller on Wednesday night - resulting in tears of joy from 'The Machine Gun'.

3 Littler was the favourite to win the title for a third time, but he was outclassed by Wattimena Credit: Getty

3 Wattimena was overcome with emotion following the 18-leg thriller

It is the first time in the 19-year-old's career so far that he has ever lost a knockout match in the PDC major event held in Wolverhampton.

Littler, who qualified top of Group A, exits the tournament having won only one match.

His only victory came in his opener against Beau Greaves, with the teenager then losing to Niels Zonneveld in his second group match.

At one stage against Wattimena, he trailed 7-2, before threatening to produce an incredible comeback.

Wattimena eventually found himself 9-6 up, only for Littler to win the next two legs.

And with Littler hot on his tails of winning another break of throw, the 38-year-old checked out 77 to advance into the quarter-finals for just the second time in his career.

For Littler, he will now not be in action until the PDC World Championship next month having failed to qualify for the Players Championship Finals.

How did Jermaine Wattimena react to his win?

Wattimena was overcome with emotion following just a second career win over Littler as he burst into tears in his post-match interview with Sky Sports.

Through tears, he said: "It feels emotional, absolutely incredible.

"I saved my best game for this stage and I'm really proud of it.

"I was 7-2 ahead and missed three darts to go 8-2 up.

"He then started playing well again.

"But in the last leg, one dart for the match - it feels amazing."

Wattimena has now won all three of his Grand Slam matches in 2026 having triumphed over Lisa Ashton and Alan Soutar in Group B.

And he produced his best performance of the tournament so far against Littler having averaged 101.70.

While Littler wasn't far off with 101.38, it was his lowest of the tournament.

3 Dutch star Wattimena is now looking to advance into the Grand Slam semi-finals for the first time in his career

Wattimena will now face Kevin Doets for a place in the last four.

Littler's PDC major struggles continue

Littler had been on course midway through the year to complete a clean sweet of PDC singles majors having won the first five - in addition to triumphing in the World Cup with England teammate Luke Humphries.

But he has now failed to go beyond the quarter-final in the four majors since coming out on top at the World Matchplay in July.

Along with the Grand Slam, the World Series Finals, World Grand Prix and European Championship have all eluded him.

And he will not be present at this month's Players Championship Finals in Minehead later this month to defend his title having missed too many events.

But despite his recent setbacks, Littler will be among the foremost favourites to win the 2027 World Championship at Alexandra Palace having reached the last three finals - winning the last two.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s £50million Vinicius Jr alternative will be an absolute superstar with Gunners transfer
Sports.content:
RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa will become a superstar if he completes a move to Arsenal.

This is the view of European football broadcaster Andy Brassell, who believes the Premier League and the Emirates Stadium are the perfect platforms for the Norway winger to take his game to the next level.



5 Nusa has made an impressive start to the season with 14 goal involvements in 15 games for RB Leipzig, including a goal in the Champions League against Manchester City Credit: Getty

Despite holding a five-point lead at the top of the Premier League, Arsenal are said to be interested in expanding their stacked squad.

It's reported the Gunners are keen on Nusa, dubbed the 'Norwegian Neymar', along with other Premier League clubs.

The 21-year-old, who has six goals and eight assists for Leipzig this term, could would represent a younger and cheaper alternative to Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior.



Vinicius Jr who was linked with a move to Arsenal before signing a new long-term contract at the Bernabeu in the summer, however, a bad start to the season has led to suggestions his future in the Spanish capital could be in doubt again.

And Brassell argues that while there's no great urgency for Arsenal to get a deal for Nusa done in January, it's a move that would suit both player and club down to the ground.



Brassell: Nusa will become a superstar at Arsenal

"It feels a very Arsenal-y type of signing," Brassell told talkSPORT.com. "We know it's an area in which they would probably like to reinforce.

"Although, I have to say, I think [Christos] Tzolis has been pretty good so far, and I think he can get even better. For me, the urgency to fill that left-wing role is maybe not as great as it was six months ago.



"But maybe this is why that feels more like an Arsenal signing than Vinny Jr. If Vinny Jr becomes available, I definitely think Arsenal should throw the hat in the ring all over again. I don't see why not.

"His below par form is better than 99 per cent of players playing professional football at this level. But if you can get him back to his 2024 form, wow, that would be really something for Arsenal.

"Having said that, their thing over the years tends to be to get on ground level or near a ground level and then build that player into a superstar. A little bit like Liverpool have done over the years.

5 Nusa scored in Norway's 3-1 win over Wales in the Nations League last weekend Credit: AFP



5 The ex-Club Brugge winger could be set for a big move in 2027

"I think that's fine, by the way. Even someone like Declan Rice, who cost a heck of a lot of money and was already an established Premier League player, he becomes an absolute elite performer at Arsenal.

"That, to me, seems like a reasonable model. That would be what they're doing with Antonio Nusa.

"Bear in mind that there's a big question mark over Nusa coming into this season. He is a player that, since he's about 13 or 14, people have known exactly how good he could be.



"He got himself into the professional game, excelled in Belgium, Premier League interest. Tottenham were fairly close to signing him at one point.

"Then he's gone to Leipzig. There was just a sense that we know the talent is there, but where's the next level?

"That was reinforced by the World Cup. He didn't play terribly in the World Cup, but every time they brought on Andreas Schjelderup for him, Norway were a better team.

5 Nusa joined Leipzig from Club Brugge in 2024 Credit: Getty



"Interestingly, over this international break, and particularly the game against Wales, I think Nusa and Schjelderup showed they could play pretty well together.

"What we've really seen from Nusa so far this season is what we needed to see from Nusa. More production in terms of goals and assists. To go with the verve and end product.

"I think the physical side of it is clear. I think he would thrive in the Premier League as well. He's someone who I think could go on to score a lot of goals on a regular basis, if he carries on on the trajectory in which he's on at the moment. I think Arsenal would absolutely be the right team for him.

"Honestly, I think he could become an absolute world superstar there. With the sort of talent he's got, that's what he should be aiming at. I think the price pinch is probably about right as well.



"Because at the top of this season, they're looking for €55-60 million [£46m-£50m], somewhere around that mark.

"Maybe it's a little more if he continues to have the season that he looks like having in the first couple of months of this season.

5 It remains to be seen whether Arsenal will formalise any interest in Nusa in the winter transfer window Credit: Getty

"If he produces a complete performance over this season. Remember he scored against Manchester City in the Champions League as well. So, I think he's exactly where Arsenal should be aiming at."



What has Nusa said about his links to Arsenal?

Nusa is contracted at Leipzig until the summer of 2029, meaning any potential suitors would have to stump up to prise him away from the Bundesliga outfit.

And the player hasn't given much away regarding his future, saying last week: "I try to take a step back from that. There's a lot going on at the same time now. I try not to open my phone too often, because there's always something going on there, he says, laughing."

On what appears on his phone, Nusa added: "I see everything, then! Whatever comes. I'm not blind, so I get it.

"That's why I try to take a step back. I have good people around me. There's no stress. I just try to enjoy the everyday life I have in Leipzig. It's a fantastic team with a fantastic coach (Martin Demichelis).



"Next to that I have an agent who works with all the other parts and just lets me focus on the football. That's the most important thing for me."

Sports.title: Netflix set to face $2bn World Cup bidding war that could change sport forever
Sports.content:
Netflix set to face $2bn World Cup bidding war that could change sport forever

FIFA could reportedly auction 2030 World Cup broadcasting rights in the United States for up to $2billion to Netflix.

Given the tournament is regarded to be the biggest across sport, rights to cover matches are incredibly lucrative for broadcasters.



2 Netflix are looking to expand their sport streaming portfolio by landing broadcast rights for the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

FOX Sports are the existing holders and transmitted fixtures during this summer's tournament as Spain went all the way to win their second title.

However, there could be a landmark change in coverage of the sport in the US ahead of the next World Cup.

Netflix eye up World Cup rights

Streaming giants Netflix are interested in bidding, say The Guardian, and the rights could be worth between $1.5bn (£1.1bn) and $2bn (£1.5bn).



"I would put money on Netflix to win – they will pay whatever it takes," a media rights buyer told the outlet.

Netflix are set to submit a first round bid before the Thursday deadline.



Apple TV, Disney, Amazon, YouTube and DAZN are expected to do the same as streaming platforms look towards sport coverage.

FOX, ESPN, NBC Universal and Skydance, all of whom are traditional US broadcasters, will also place bids.



"There's a huge range of buyers and therefore a broad range of possible outcomes," another source told The Guardian.

"All the media companies and streamers will bid. Fox will find it very challenging to retain the rights."

Netflix has already landed 2030 World Cup broadcasting rights for all 104 matches in both Spain and Andorra.

2 The current rights holders in the US, FOX, are among a number of broadcasters and platforms who are set to bid Credit: Getty



The former country are one of the co-hosts of the next edition alongside Portugal and Morocco.

As part of the agreement, Netflix will make every Spain match, the semi-finals and final free-to-air on a national broadcaster.

Those in Andorra will also be able to watch one game per matchday on the platform for free.

Other countries have already had their broadcasters confirmed, such as Ireland with RTE.



Both the BBC and ITV will remain as the television networks for fans in the United Kingdom.

The 2030 World Cup begins on June 8, with the final scheduled to be played on July 21.

Sports.title: Leicester end partnership with BC Game after porn star becomes ambassador for shirt sponsor
Sports.content:
Leicester end partnership with BC Game after porn star becomes ambassador for shirt sponsor

Leicester has ended its partnership with main shirt sponsor BC Game after the cryptocurrency platform appointed a porn star as an ambassador.

BC Game had been the Foxes' front-of-shirt sponsor since 2024, and announced a partnership with Russian adult content creator Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador on November 3.

4 Leicester will no longer have BC Game as their front of shirt sponsor Credit: Getty

With BC Game an unlicensed online cryptocurrency gaming platform, their partnership with the League One side has already proved controversial among some supporters.

However, the sponsor drew yet more controversy when it revealed it would be teaming up with porn star Elfie earlier this month.

And the decision has been taken that Leicester will end all ties with BC Game, with supporters who bought a replica shirt with the BC Game branding through official club retail channels over the last 28 days being entitled to a full refund.

Leicester end sponsorship deal with BC Game

Leicester City Football Club and BC GAME have reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect," a club statement on Wednesday read.

"The decision follows constructive discussions between both parties in recent days, during which we recognised our differing commercial priorities moving forward.

"We would like to thank BC GAME for its support throughout its two-and-a-half-year association with Leicester City and for the constructive approach taken in reaching this agreement.

"Supporters who have purchased a BC GAME-branded replica shirt through official LCFC retail channels within the last 28 days (since 21 October, 2026) can return it for a full refund or exchange (subject to availability) by Wednesday 2 December. Proof of purchase will be required.

"This enhanced returns policy includes shirts that have been worn or personalised, which would not ordinarily qualify under our standard returns policy.

"Returns can be in-person at the Foxes Fanstore at King Power Stadium or via post. If supporters return their items via Royal Mail standard delivery, the cost of the return postage will be refunded by the club via the payment method used for the original purchase."

Controversial promo video

Announcing the partnership, the online gambling company posted a suggestive video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media.

4 In a promotional clip announcing the partnership, Elfie grabs a delivery driver by the shirt and pulls him inside the room Credit: @bcgame

4 Elfie then poses with her BC Game contract

The innuendo-laden promotional clip shows the adult actress accepting her BC Game contract, and has already been viewed over 6 million times on X.

The post was accompanied by the caption: “Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin.”

This quickly sparked backlash among BC Game's eSports fanbase, as well as Leicester supporters, particularly fan group The Foxes Trust.

In a lengthy statement, the supporters' group said: "Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City."

'Ditching its values'

Leicester's decision to end the partnership comes amid renewed pressure from the Foxes Trust for their association with BC Game.

The group previously accused the club of 'ditching its values' over their sponsorship deal with the company, which is based out of Curacao and unlicensed in the United Kingdom.

4 BC Game was Leicester's main shirt sponsor in their last Premier League campaign Credit: Getty

Earlier this month, the Foxes Trust said: “Most Leicester City supporters will know by now the trust’s dismay and discontent with BC Game being our front of shirt sponsor.

“BC Game have now announced a new partnership with ‘international content creator and esports personality’ Eva Elfie… who just happens to be an international porn star.

“From the moment the club decided to take sponsorship from a betting company we felt Leicester City were ditching its values.

“Now throw into the mix that BC Game have entered into a partnership with someone who continues to make their name via adult content.

“Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people’s lives, in particular young people.

“Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?”

Leicester's partnership with BC Game coincided with a challenging spell for the club on the pitch.

Their first season together - the 2024/25 campaign - saw the Foxes relegated from the Premier League, before they dropped another division to League One last term.

Now managed by Russell Martin, the 2016 English champions have had a mixed start to life in the third tier - initially struggling with just one win in five to pile pressure on their coach, but have since steadied the ship.

Had they stayed in the Premier League two seasons ago, then the partnership with BC Game - which lost its licence to operate in the UK in December 2024 - would no longer be allowed.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire theory rubbished as Man United warned over ‘huge problem’
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire has been told his ex-England teammate should serve as a blueprint for how he can thrive under Mauricio Pochettino.

The former Manchester United captain is set to play under his eighth different manager - fifth permanent - since joining the club in 2019.



3 Maguire has started all 10 of Man United's Premier League games this season Credit: Getty

During that period, Maguire, who named himself one of the world's best defenders in both boxes this year, has divided opinions among fans.

The 33-year-old, who has made over 260 appearances for the club, was appointed Man United captain just five months after his arrival.

However, a downturn in form led to criticism of his continued selection under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and his interim successor Ralf Rangnick.



After falling out of favour under Erik ten Hag, Maguire was stripped of the Red Devils captaincy in 2023 and looked to be on his way out.

A proposed transfer to West Ham broke down that summer, and the England star worked his way back into favour under Michael Carrick.



Maguire, described by Steve Bruce as the Premier League's most underrated player, has started every top flight game this season.

Pochettino's arrival has called into question his future once again, due to the Argentine's favoured high-pressing, high energy set-up.



Maguire 'could still be pretty useful' under Pochettino

Micah Richards has claimed that Maguire won't fit into the ex-Chelsea and Tottenham gaffer's plans at Old Trafford, but European football expert Andy Brassell has explained why it's not all doom and gloom.

When asked which current Man United players won't suit Pochettino, he told talkSPORT: "Well, I guess a lot of people would say Harry Maguire, but I don't know."

3 Eric Dier - who is now at Monaco - is fourth on Pochettino's all-time list of most-used players across his managerial career Credit: Getty

"I think Maguire could still be pretty useful to them," Brassell continued.



"You bear in mind someone like Eric Dier, who's not exactly the same player, but he's a player who's good on the ball, tactically intelligent and not the fastest and never has been.

"I guess at least some of those characteristics pertain to Harry Maguire as well.

"So, look, I think he'll be really open-minded. Look, United have a huge problem, not just in terms of this cycle of failure, but the fact that this cycle of failure or this cycle of underachievement, what it has led to is the fact that they are no longer in a position to go out and get the biggest stars in the game. There's still a huge name, there's no doubt about that.

"There's still a huge pull, Manchester United. But I don't think they're a huge pull for the absolute elite players in the game.



"And if we're talking about anything other than a gradual rebuild, that presents a real problem for them, really."

3 Pochettino is set to oversee his first Man United game on Sunday Credit: Getty

Pochettino is in for a baptism of fire when his reign begins against Liverpool on Sunday, with the 52-year-old only taking charge of his first training session on Wednesday.

Brassell added: "What is clear at the moment is that even if they don't have those absolute elite-level stars, there's a heck of a lot of talent in the building.



"But the squad is a mess. It needs organising, it needs restructuring. I think in terms of moving to a very athletic, press-heavy model, I mean, that's hard mid-season.

"I think Pochettino is going to need time. He's going to need to work in increments, make them more competitive, make them more clinical, as you said before, and then build to the next stage.

"A bit like how Xabi Alonso talked about how he did things at [Bayer] Leverkusen, really.

"You can't go in and impose your idea from minute one if what you're inheriting is nowhere near what you're aiming to produce eventually.



"So that will take time. But even regardless of transfers, he has got plenty of quality to work with there, I think."

Sports.title: Four-cap England international named ideal Bernardo Silva successor at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Real Madrid have been told that Adam Wharton would be brilliant as the successor to Bernardo Silva in midfield.

Los Blancos are one of several European giants keeping tabs on the Crystal Palace star, having sent scouts to watch him last year.



4 Wharton has been linked with a move away from Palace for a number of years Credit: Getty

The 22-year-old was thought to be one of the hottest properties on the market towards the end of last season.

Palace, who have sold many of their star players in recent seasons, slapped a price tag of over £80million to ward suitors off Wharton.

The club's No.20 earned the player of the match award in the UEFA Conference League final triumph over Rayo Vallecano in May.



However, Wharton was not included in Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the World Cup this summer.

The former Blackburn star has since been hampered in his attempts for an international recall by Palace's poor start to the season.



Pierre Sage has now been sacked, with Thomas Frank named as the Eagles' new manager on a two-and-a-half-year deal.

Wharton will be among those with a point to prove to his new boss, having also been omitted once again from Tuchel's England squad.



"He's got fewer than ten caps which, frankly, is a travesty," European football expert Andy Brassell stated to talkSPORT.com.

"He's a brilliant midfield player, so good at controlling and creating, and every time I see Palace in the flesh, he just looks unbelievable."

On Frank's immediate tasks at Selhurst Park, Brassell added: "Obviously he has to do stuff like get Adam Wharton back to his absolute best form, which has seen him link to some of the best clubs in Europe."

4 Wharton has helped Palace win three trophies in two years Credit: Getty



Adam Wharton transfer latest

The four-cap England international has played the most minutes of any Palace player across all competitions after Chris Richards.

His importance to the south Londoners was further underlined by Wharton taking over the captaincy in Dean Henderson’s absence.

But as confirmed by Palace chief Steve Parish, live on talkSPORT in October 2025, Wharton will want to play Champions League football.

Discussing the potential clubs interested in him, Brassell argued that a move overseas over staying in England might be the best option.



England captain Harry Kane, Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon have all snubbed Premier League interest to become stars abroad.

Brassell continued: "In the medium term, I do wonder, with the midfield options that some of the other big teams in the Premier League have got, whether that interest from a Real Madrid or a Bayern Munich is something that could bear fruit.

4 England's two best players, Bellingham and Kane, have made their homes abroad Credit: Getty

"You look at Bayern, I think he'd be great next to Pavlovic - Pavlovic is the energy, the tackler, the up and down.



"Wharton's the one you give the keys to."

Adam Wharton to Real Madrid

"And also, I think this season, what has been clear to anyone since the back half of September is that Real Madrid are miles better with Bernardo Silva in the centre of midfield.

"But I also get the feeling he's not going to be there forever, and they can't rely on him to play all those games every game in a season.

"Who would fit in that spot really well? I think it's obvious.

4 Mourinho's Madrid have won all six LaLiga games where Bernardo Silva has started, including El Clasico Credit: Getty

"I think a Wharton would be brilliant for Real Madrid in that very spot.



"And I like the idea of there being some sort of relief locum slash extended handover between Bernardo Silva and Adam Wharton in the centre of midfield."

Sports.title: Manchester United quietly axe five coaches including Champions League winner as Mauricio Pochettino era officially begins
Sports.content:
Manchester United have announced five coaches have followed sacked manager Michael Carrick out the door.

The Red Devils wielded the axe on club legend Carrick last week with United sitting in the relegation zone after the opening ten Premier League games.



2 Pochettino's first game for United will be away at Liverpool on Sunday Credit: Getty

Former Tottenham and Chelsea manager Mauricio Pochettino has subsequently been whisked in as his replacement.

Having overseen his final two matches in charge of the United States' national team during the international break, the Argentine has now arrived in England.

With the Pochettino era officially underway, he will now be looking to guide United to a first top-flight win since August when his side face rivals Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.



And he has brought his own staff with him in his quest to get United up the table and away from a relegation battle.

Along with his son Sebastiano, Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez and Alec Scot have linked up with Pochettino at United.



Though Pochettino will not be working with United cult hero Jonny Evans, who won 12 major honours across his two spells as a player - including the Champions League.

Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate are two other notable coaches from Carrick's staff that have been moved on.



What did United say in their club statement?

United announced the news relating to their coaching staff when highlighting Pochettino's arrival to their Carrington training ground on Wednesday.

Burying the update at the bottom of the article, a statement read: "The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

"We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future."

2 United cult hero Evans became part of the club's first team coaching staff in January Credit: Getty



Evans initially joined United's first team coaching staff under Darren Fletcher's caretaker role in January, with Carrick keeping him on.

The same month, Carrick brought in ex-England coach Holland to the Theatre of Dreams, along with former Tottenham and Real Madrid centre-back Woodgate, who worked alongside side him at Middlesbrough.

The trio have lasted just 11 months in their assistant coaching positions.

As for Craig Mawson, the former Burnley shot-stopper has left his role as goalkeeping coach, having worked in the tole under ever manager since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.



Meanwhile Binnion, who previously coached both United's Under-18s and U21s before stepping up to first team duties, leaves having spent five years at the club.

Despite the changes at United, Pochettino has expressed his excitement at beign given the keys to the club.

Speaking for the first time after officially starting work, he said: "Very excited to be here.

"It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club.

"Looking forward to starting work."

Sports.title: Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington
Sports.content:
Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

The club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but quickly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

They are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

‘You can’t be yourself,’ says Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’

Like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady said that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction

Intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

City have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

He utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

The format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson says, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

‘You're having the same conversations again. It was like, "Hang on a minute. I've had this conversation before". The previous people knew about it. They have the footage from earlier seasons – so do your homework, like we all do with our jobs. It almost felt like a bit of a lack of respect at times.’

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum

These are the challenges that Amazon face with United, somehow attempting to earn trust or forging relationships in a matter of months before they pack up and leave. The film crew will be seen as outsiders.

There is intrigue within the industry as to exactly how granular Amazon can go amid the United chaos and whether they use fly-on-the-wall cameras, as was the case with Arsenal (in 2021–22) and Tottenham (in 2019-20).

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

Unlike Mourinho, Pochettino – his predecessor, sacked in November 2019 – had banned them from his office. He was never keen on the idea of the documentary and hardly features in the series, his dismissal coming early in Episode One – a sign perhaps that the film-makers got little out of him.
