Structure does not mean that governors own voters or that citizens will automatically vote according to the instructions of a governor. Nigerians are not political robots. Voters can reject candidates, ignore political directives and vote according to their conscience. But political structure creates the machinery through which a political party reaches voters, communicates its message, organises campaigns, mobilises supporters and deploys its agents to polling units.

The APC’s current geographical and political advantage is therefore not something that should be dismissed. Recent reporting indicates that the ruling party has governments in 32 of Nigeria’s 36 states, while only Oyo, Bauchi, Osun and Anambra are officially outside APC control. Even more significantly, political movements have continued across party lines, with some governors and influential politicians who are not formally APC members openly supporting President Bola Tinubu’s second-term bid.

What does this mean politically? It means that the APC enters the 2027 election with an extraordinary network of governors, commissioners, senators, members of the House of Representatives, state legislators, local government leaders, party executives, ward leaders, political associates and grassroots mobilisers. These people do not own the votes of Nigerians, but they constitute a political infrastructure capable of reaching millions of voters.

That infrastructure cannot simply be wished away by social-media popularity or angry supporters of opposition candidates. For the opposition to overcome the ruling party’s existing structure, it would need not merely a popular candidate but a candidate with an exceptionally powerful personal following capable of cutting across party structures and geographical boundaries. In other words, the candidate would need a political force almost cult-like in its intensity and national reach—one capable of making millions of voters disregard established political networks and vote overwhelmingly for a new political vehicle. At the moment, it is difficult to identify an opposition candidate who clearly possesses that level of nationwide political following.

The current administration inherited serious economic problems and responded with reforms that were politically difficult, particularly the removal of petrol subsidy and changes to the foreign-exchange regime. These policies imposed substantial costs on households and businesses, and the administration has faced intense criticism over the resulting cost-of-living pressures. That criticism cannot simply be dismissed.

However, the economic picture is no longer the same as it was at the beginning of the administration. This is precisely why government performance could become the second major pillar of President Tinubu’s 2027 campaign after political structure. The administration can point to stronger GDP growth, moderating inflation, improved oil production, stronger external reserves and continuing investment in infrastructure. The government’s argument will be that difficult reforms were necessary to move Nigeria away from an unsustainable economic path and establish the foundation for longer-term growth. There has also been commendable progress in the fight against insecurity, although significant security challenges remain and Nigerians continue to demand greater protection of lives and property.

Its opponents, naturally, will present a different interpretation. They will argue that economic growth means little if food remains expensive, unemployment remains a concern and households continue to struggle. They will also point to the fact that kidnapping and other security challenges have not disappeared. Ultimately, voters will decide which argument they believe. But this is where the politics of 2027 becomes more complicated than viral videos of booing or stone-pelting suggest.

Of course, the APC must not become complacent. Political structures can collapse when voters become sufficiently dissatisfied. Governors can lose influence. Political alliances can change. Candidates can make strategic mistakes. And no amount of party machinery can permanently protect a government that completely loses the confidence of the electorate. But as things stand, it would be difficult to argue that Tinubu and the APC are entering 2027 from a position of weakness.

Stone-pelting and booing do not win elections. Political structure does not guarantee victory either. But when structure, incumbency, national political experience, organised mobilisation, improving economic conditions, infrastructure development, increased public investment and progress in tackling insecurity come together, the burden of proof lies heavily on the opposition.

For the APC to lose in 2027, therefore, it may take far more than the political noise currently dominating the public space. It may take a dramatic realignment of voters, a powerful opposition coalition, a candidate with extraordinary national appeal and a significant deterioration in the government’s performance.

Until such a combination emerges, the argument that Tinubu and the APC have the upper hand in 2027 is not political propaganda. It is a reasonable assessment of the balance of political forces presently visible in Nigeria.

Kenechukwu Aguolu, FCA, FCIA, ACTI,

Project Manager, Business Analyst

World.title: THAT YARI’S COMMENT ON HUNGER
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

The thoughtlessness and inability of Nigerian leaders to empathise with the people must end soon, writes MONDAY PHILIPS EKPE

The Director-General of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdul’aziz Abubakar Yari was widely reported some days ago to have drawn a link between the increasing inaccessibility of many Nigerians to food and their lack of hard work. “If there is no food in the market, that is what we are calling hunger. But anyone who is not a lazy person, definitely he will have food on his table,” the APC senator representing Zamfara West and former governor of the state was quote to have declared at the Uyo, Akwa Ibom APC presidential rally.

Not surprisingly, a group called Senator Yari National Unity Project for Tinubu 2027 (SYNUP 4 Tinubu 2027) later dismissed the stories as misrepresentations of what their leader meant; that he never made any direct reference to Nigerian youths. “What was actually said was a statement on the dignity of work, made by a man who had just acknowledged that hunger exists. To turn that into the headline, ‘Yari calls youths lazy’, is not reporting. It is spin,” it said. The writers who joined “youth” and “lazy” together probably did so with a similar situation in mind. While on a foreign trip, the late President Muhammadu Buhari openly blamed the socio-economic plight of young Nigerians on their laziness.

But not many people would buy SYNUP’s defence or clarification. Those who have been following the Nigerian political scene especially in the present dispensation could well take Senator Yari’s Freudian slip as representative of the thought processes of majority of the members of his privileged class. A man or woman gets into public office and is soon bitten by a bug which numbs him/her from the humane understanding of his/her surroundings. Does it require advanced semantics to know the differences between availability of anything and its affordability? As someone who should know why even his own banditry-ravaged state can’t take the abundance of foodstuff for granted, it’s unfortunate indeed that Yari voiced out the contentious blunder in front of that hapless crowd.

It’s difficult to say what many of those in authority in Nigeria eat or drink. Or smoke. On a good day, odious statements that suggest or peddle the complicity of citizens in the face of obvious governmental inadequacies ought to result in the resignation or removal of the speaker. Yari was there to solicit the votes that would grant President Bola Tinubu a second term in office, after all. But he dared to deny food shortage and blame the victims of Nigeria’s hugely diminished purchasing power in the same breath. Who does that without consequences? How much longer will it take Nigerians to realise that the gulf between the ruling elite and the masses may have now further widened without remedies in sight?

Our politicians are among the luckiest on earth, you know. We shouldn’t single out Yari for condemnation. There’s no way the wanton display of unexplained wealth by a little percentage of the citizenry can coexist with empathy for the down-trodden. Only very few vocations and professions can compete favourably with holding government positions as pathways to riches untold. Better still for them, the machineries designed to checkmate such excesses aren’t showing any signs of genuine operations at the moment. Even more pathetic is the fact that the populace, particularly younger ones, who should demand accountability, are heavily distracted. Many of them are trapped by the social media in pursuit of the soft life. Even when they attempt to engage politically, they propagate and deepen the primordial inanities that have kept the country divided for long.

The line between the oppressors and the oppressed must worry everyone. If the repercussions aren’t apparent now, they will be at some point. A September 2026 report of the United Nations Trade and Development (UNCTAD) titled “Deconstructing Poverty and Inequality in Nigeria” asserts that poverty is concentrated in the north and rural areas. It affirms thus: “Poverty remains widespread in Nigeria despite the country’s considerable economic potential. Inequality has declined over time, but poverty has risen in recent years… The multidimensional poverty index, which measures deprivation across four dimensions – health, education, living standards and work and shocks – indicates that 62.9% of Nigerians, or about 133 million people, were multidimensionally poor in 2022.

“The north-east and north-west recorded the highest multidimensional poverty index scores, while the incidence reached 91% in Sokoto. The report links these differences to economic activities, household size, education, infrastructure, urbanization, fiscal capacity, insecurity and conflict.” These figures have since worsened, unfortunately. Interestingly, Yari’s backyard hosts a chunk of this despicable profile. Come to think of it, can he reproduce his goof in Gusau, Zamfara’s capital, without instant judgment? Most likely never!

Yari is not alone in his failure to connect with the despondent conditions of most Nigerians today, however. Many of his colleagues also have only an academic knowledge about the sufferings of the people they claim to lead. Each time President Tinubu assures in his speeches and elsewhere that he knows what the citizens feel, I don’t receive it well. I sincerely think he doesn’t. Hardship in the country is now unprecedented. Let’s hope our leaders come to terms with this ugly truth quickly.

My colleague and editor of THISDAY Lawyer, Onikepo Braithwaite, put this succinctly in her compelling article, “Hunger and Yari’s Poverty of Thought”, published in THISDAY on November 17, 2026: “Hunger in contemporary Nigeria is primarily a question of non-affordability, produced by policy choices, insecurity that keeps farmers off the land, and a wage structure that leaves even full-time workers unable to meet basic needs. The student-devised (meal-rationing) equation of 1-0-0, 0-0-1 or 0-0-0 is simply the arithmetic expression of that reality.

“Until those who have held high office can demonstrate that they used the resources and authority available to them to reduce, rather than preside over widespread poverty, statements that shift blame onto the governed will continue to ring hollow and sound offensive. Public office carries a duty of care; when that duty is unmet, it is not just a falsehood but disparaging, to re-describe the people’s resulting hunger as laziness and/or the fault of the hungry.” And may these high-level indifference, insensitivity and provocation not lead to uncontrollable angst. Progressive Nigerians should work towards when the people would get rid of ethnic, religious and regional demarcations and act as one. Then, the opportunism, uncharity and unwisdom of those who preside over them and their resources would be decisively challenged.

Dr Ekpe is a member of THISDAY Editorial Board

X: @monday_ekpe2

World.title: Stock Market Drops by N642bn to Sustain Downward Trend
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Kayode Tokede

The stock market section of the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), yesterday dropped by N642billion as cautious sentiment continued for the second consecutive trading session this week.

The NGX All-Share Index declined by 989.00 basis points or 0.40 per cent to close at 248,329.65 basis points.

Consequently, market capitalisation lost N642 billion to close at N161.238 trillion.

The downturn was driven by price depreciation in large and medium capitalised stocks amongst which are; Aradel Holdings, Zenith Bank, eTranzact International, Meyer and Champion Breweries.

Despite the bearish close, market sentiment remained marginally positive, with 26 advancers, outweighing 25 decliners. Critical Minerals Financing Corporation (CMFC) and McNichols emerged the highest price gainer of 10 per cent each to close at N3.52 and N4.95 respectively, while Chellaram followed with a gain of 9.79 per cent to close at N10.65, per share.

Living Trust Mortgage Bank rose by 9.77 per cent to close at N2.81, while Veritas Kapital Assurance appreciated by 9.71 per cent to close at N1.13, per share.

On the other side, Aradel Holdings led others on the losers’ chart with 10 per cent to close at N1,166.40, per share. eTranzact International followed with a decline of 9.86 per cent to close at N15.55, while Transnational Express shed 9.26 per cent to close at N2.45, per share.

Meyer went down by 8.86 per cent to close at N15.95, while Champion Breweries depreciated by 8.85 per cent to close at N11.85, per share.

The total volume traded declined by 20.02 per cent to 451.14 million units, valued at N26.61 billion, and exchanged in 32,572 deals.

Transactions in the shares of First Holdco led the activity with 62.650 million shares worth N6.671 billion. Access Holdings followed with account of 42.467 million shares valued at N1.138 billion, while Zenith Bank traded 33.155 million shares valued at N3.780 billion.

Fidelity Bank traded 23.748 million shares worth N540.846 million, while Nigerian Breweries traded 23.083 million shares worth N1.616 billion.

Looking ahead, Cowry Assets Management Limited said, “sustained profit-taking in heavyweight counters and sectoral weakness could constrain near-term recovery, although selective bargain-hunting and marginally positive market breadth may provide some support.”

World.title: Dozi breaks silence on cancer rumours
World.content:
Dozi has denied rumours he has cancer. Image via Facebook

Afrikaans singer Dozi, real name Hendrick Opperman, has rubbished social media rumours that he is dying from cancer.

The veteran entertainer – known for hit songs like Ou Ryperd, Maybe, My Baby, and Tussen My en Jou – recently underwent surgery to remove growths on his vocal cords.

DOZI NOT DYING OF CANCER

In recent days, social media users have been circulating rumours about Dozi’s dire diagnosis, including claims he has developed cancer of the vocal cords.



The claims were rubbished by the singer’s publicist, Alishia van Deventer, who accused individuals of altering images of Dozi to appear frail and thin.

Dozi himself has called out the trolls in a Facebook video, in which he says: “You have to wake up one morning and hear you have a disease… cancer.

“I don’t have cancer, ladies and gentlemen, I’m very sorry. I’ve worked hard, and I’m keeping myself busy. I’m so happy to see so many people still love me and care. You’re not going to believe this, but I’m healthy.”

He added: “We can’t stop fake news from being created, but we can stop sharing it.”

Earlier this month, Dozi underwent surgery to remove polyps on his vocal cord.

BACKABUDDY CAMPAIGN

Meanwhile, a BackaBuddy campaign has been set up to help Dozi cover the costs of his recent surgery.



According to the crowdfunding initiative, which has raised over R80 000, the veteran entertainer could be out of action for several months as he recovers.

“We therefore want to help alleviate the financial pressure of his medical expenses, recovery period and essential living expenses”, it reads.

Ahead of his surgery, industry colleagues hosted a fundraising concert called Dozi JAM – Back Our Buddy, in Hartbeespoort.

World.title: Anele Mdoda’s sister claims friends ‘didn’t trust’ her husband, Buzza
World.content:
Zamalisa Mdoda, the younger sister of Anele Mgudlwa (née Mdoda), came out guns blazing, claiming that two of Anele’s friends did not trust her husband, Bonelela “Buzza” Mgudlwa.

ZAMALISA MDODA CLAIMS ANELE’S FRIENDS ‘DIDN’T TRUST’ BUZZA

In a tweet posted on 15 November 2026, Zamalisa alleged that two of Anele’s “long-time friends” had approached their father, asking him to persuade Anele to sign a prenuptial agreement because they did not trust her husband.

She further alleged that Anele had ignored warnings about Buzza and that he might “turn on her.”



2 of @Anele’s long-time friends went to our father asking him to get Anele to sign a pre-nup because they didn’t trust @BonelelaM. Did she listen? No. She had multiple warnings about him but she wanted her Netflix wedding. When he does turn on her, remember that she chose this. — Zamalisa (@Zamedyzamzam) November 15, 2026

FANS DEFEND ANELE

Judging by their reactions to Zamalisa’s allegations, Anele’s fans are clearly in her corner. They defended her fiercely amid the buzz surrounding her Netflix wedding special.

Ziminaphakade: I guess Anele was right when she said you 3 sisters couldn’t state clearly what the problem was between her and you guys; instead, you fought amongst yourselves. You’ve been talking for 2 weeks now, and we still can’t make out what the problem is.



SouthAfricansFirst🇿🇦@_SAFirst_: Reading all your tweets, you are trying everything to humiliate your sister, and it is sad. Pathetic actually. The things you are saying about Anele say A LOT about who you are & less about her.

veve@Leveve18: It’s now clear that Anele’s sister is a bully, and she is hurting that they can no longer control her It’s good that Anele isn’t giving this fire any oxygen. This one needs to heal shem.

MORE ALLEGATIONS MADE BY ZAMALISA MDODA

The allegations involving Anele’s friends are among multiple claims made by Zamalisa.



The Mdoda family drama unfolded when Zamalisa dished out a heated response to a tweet in which Anele shared her thoughts on firstborns.

Zamalisa interpreted the tweet as a reference to their family dynamics, writing:

“This girl has used her platform to harass and lie about our family for YEARS! @947, is this how your hosts conduct themselves? Using personal vendettas as topics of discussion?”



Without delving into their family drama, Zamalisa alleged that Anele had been a topic of discussion during family meetings over the years. She also insinuated that Anele was involved in witchcraft.

@Anele I told your father a touch is a move. So since you wanna touch, here is my move. That meeting was about YOUR broom activities. And while we’re here, bring back our photo albums or did you leave them at umhlaba uyalingana? — Zamalisa (@Zamedyzamzam) November 13, 2026

Zamalisa also accused Buzza of failing to pay her cousin for the alcohol she supplied at his wedding.



She paired the tweet with a post referencing the allegations of corruption involving COVID-19 PPE tenders.

She also alleged that Buzza only married her sister for financial gain.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs suffer defensive blow ahead of Sundowns semi-final
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs defender Inacio Miguel has been ruled out of the highly anticipated clash against Mamelodi Sundowns at Loftus Versfeld Stadium this weekend.

Amakhosi face the Brazilians in the semi-final of the Carling Knockout Cup on Sunday afternoon.

Miguel, who serves as Chiefs’ vice-captain, is currently completing a two-match suspension following a straight red card in the heated 2-1 Soweto Derby defeat to Orlando Pirates last month.



His absence leaves a significant void in the heart of the Kaizer Chiefs defence, particularly if the team suffers an injury during the encounter.

In recent matches, Amakhosi head coach Fernando Da Cruz has opted to partner Rushwin Dortley and Thabo Moloisane in central defence. The duo have been impressive so far and will likely continue their partnership against Sundowns.

Kaizer Chiefs need a strong defence on Sunday

Chiefs will need to remain defensively solid, especially against a Sundowns side boasting one of the strongest attacking forces in the PSL and across the continent.



The last meeting between the two sides ended in a 1-1 draw in August. Da Cruz will take encouragement from the fact that Amakhosi have avoided defeat in their last four meetings against the Brazilians.

Kaizer Chiefs have not reached a final since winning the Nedbank Cup. Ironically, they played Downs in the semi-final, where they won 2-1. At the time, they were coached by Tunisian tactician Nasreddine Nabi, who ended their 10-year trophyless drought.

Do you think Miguel missing Sunday’s match will help Chiefs?

World.title: Rassie’s ‘cousin’ claps back at critics
World.content:
Rassie Erasmus has been praised by a relative. Image via IG

Rassie Erasmus’s reported cousin has spoken out in his defence following his six-match suspension by World Rugby this week. This follows comments by the Springbok coach, who implied that match officials may have deliberately ignored 17 dangerous tackles by the French against South African players.

RASSIE ERASMUS’S COUSIN COMES TO HIS DEFENCE

In an Instagram post, Gerhard Boshoff, who claims to be Rassie Erasmus’s cousin, showed his public support for the Springbok coach.

He also praised the rugby hero for his bold comments questioning the television match official (TMO)’s lack of intervention in several tackles he believed were dangerous. 

Gerhard, a fitness coach, posted: “When protecting the game of rugby matters more than protecting yourself. That’s leadership!”

He added: “Proud of you for speaking up, cuz!”

Gerard added that Rassie was a “leader and innovator” who is “not scared of the truth”.



In the comments section, Gerhard continued to defend Rassie against critics who accused the latter of selective outrage.

He clapped back: “He is living rent-free in your head, and I understand that can be hard to swallow”

He added: “He took one for World Rugby, as we all know it’s rotten on the top”



DAUGHTER HINTS AT DOUBLE STANDARDS

Meanwhile, Rassie’s daughter, Nikki Erasmus, has indirectly reacted to her father’s si-match suspension.

The netball star – the twin sister of Carli – made a subtle hint at double standards after she posted an IG Story about Irish player Sam Prendergast, who has been cleared to play against the Springboks, despite being cited for a dangerous tackle.



Over the weekend, Prendergast was involved in a hip-drop tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato, who was forced off the field due to injury.

Just weeks earlier, World Rugby outlawed the dangerous technique under its updated laws.

In his comments, Rassie predicted that Predergast suggested that Prendergast would escape punishment because of a technicality.



This comes just days ahead of the Springboks match against Ireland on Saturday, 21 November, at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

World.title: Dladla leaves Yanga as Fadlu Davids reshuffles backroom staff
World.content:
Former Durban City head coach Simo Dladla has reportedly parted ways with Tanzanian giants Yanga SC.

Dladla had joined Yanga SC as one of Manqoba Mngqithi’s assistants at the start of the season.

Mngqithi was let go after 13 games alongside some of the technical members he came with but Dladla remained behind as caretaker coach.



Now, according to FARpost, Dladla has now left Yanga SC who recently appointed Fadlu Davids as Mngqithi’s permanent successor.

The publication further reports that Dladla will be returning to Richards Bay FC who sacked Dimitar Pantev two weeks ago.

Dladla coached the Natal Rich Boyz between 2020 and 2021, the management believes he can help them steer the ship in the right direction.

Richards Bay FC are winless in their last 10 competitive games, and they are early candidates for relegation.

DLADLA LEAVES YANGA SC TO REUNITE WITH RICHARDS BAY FC – REPORT

“Simo Dladla and Tanzanian champions Young Africans SC have parted ways by mutual agreement, with the South African coach set to return to Richards Bay FC after agreeing terms with the Betway Premiership club, FARPost has learnt,” reads part of the report.

IS HE THE RIGHT MAN TO LEAD RICHARDS BAY FC?

World.title: ‘Disgusting’: South Africans fume over R2 400 SASSA grant update
World.content:
South Africans are venting their anger at the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), with many saying the R2 400 SASSA grant is not enough for vulnerable recipients to survive.

The Older Persons Grant is R2 400 per month for beneficiaries aged 60 and older, amounts that took effect from 1 April 2026. The Disability Grant and Care Dependency Grant also rose from R2 315 to R2 400.

Grant recipients and their families shared their frustrations in the comments on The South African’s Facebook page.



Grant recipients accuse SASSA of ‘games’

Several commenters said they felt SASSA was toying with people who depend on their R2 400 SASSA grants.

“What waiting game,” Liz Zugloi wrote.

Letitia Cullen was among the most outspoken. She questioned how recipients are expected to cope.

“How cruel can SASSA be? How must we survive now? You want to play games?” Cullen wrote.

She said elderly South Africans are the hardest hit, adding that “there are thousands of old people suffering, sick and even dying.”

Long days at SASSA offices

Others turned their frustration to the service recipients receive at SASSA offices.



Isaiah Oupa said people in Soshanguve often spend the entire day at the local office without getting help.

“Sometimes in SA you will hate the way our government works, especially in SASSA Soshanguve, most people go there without help, stay there the whole day without help,” Oupa wrote.

One word sums up the mood

For some South Africans, a single word was enough to express how they felt.

“Disgusting,” Dina Chorn wrote.

The reactions reflect growing frustration among grant recipients, particularly pensioners, who rely on their monthly payments to cover food, electricity, transport and medical costs.

Many older South Africans also support children and grandchildren in their homes, which means a single grant often has to feed an entire household.

For them, any change, delay or uncertainty around their grants can mean the difference between getting by and going without.

The comments also show how many recipients feel unheard by SASSA, both in decisions about their payments and in the service they receive at local offices.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Thabang Matuludi named Sundowns’ best player for October
World.content:
Thabang Matuludi is Sundowns' best player for October. Image: Mamelodi Sundowns WhatsApp Channel.

Mamelodi Sundowns right-back Thabang Matuludi has been named the club’s best player for the month of October.

Signed in September from Polokwane City, Matuludi needed no introduction from the majority of Sundowns fans.

And he fitted like a hand in a glove after taking over from the injured Khuliso Mudau, cementing his place in the Sundowns team.



In October, the right-footed defender featured in all five competitive matches for the Brazilians.

Matuludi, despite being a defender, scored two goals in those five games and helped the team win the MTN8 final.

As a result, he won the Cherry Player of Month award where he will be handed the vehicle and get to drive it for a month.



Matuludi was nominated alongside the Fawaaz Basadien, Iqraam Rayners, Ronwen Williams and Teboho Mokoena.

He becomes the third Sundowns player to win the Cherry Player of the Month award this season after Marcelo Allende (August) and Siyanda Ndlovu (September).

The 27-year-old was instrumental as Bafana Bafana recently collected four points off Kenya in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifiers.



Pitso Mosimane’s men played to a 2-2 draw with Kenya in the first leg which played at Orlando Amstel Arena before beating the same opponents 2-1 on Tuesday.

As reported by The South African, Bafana Bafana have since returned to the country from Nairobi, Kenya.

World.title: R100m mandrax laboratory bust in KZN
World.content:
DURBAN – Police have uncovered a mandrax manufacturing laboratory worth an estimated R100 million in Umvoti, KwaZulu-Natal, following a joint operation by the Hawks and the South African Police Service (SAPS).

The operation led to the discovery of illicit drugs, chemicals and specialised equipment allegedly used in the manufacturing of mandrax.

A 31-year-old suspect has been arrested in connection with the alleged drug manufacturing operation.

The suspect is expected to appear before the Kranskop Magistrate’s Court on Friday, where he will face charges under the Drugs and Drug Trafficking Act, including the alleged manufacturing of illicit drugs.

World.title: F1 hits Vegas with titles settled, podiums up for grabs
World.content:
LAS VEGAS - With Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes already crowned as this year's champions, F1 descends on Las Vegas this weekend with the rest of the podium spots still up for grabs, as five drivers vie for second place.

For a fourth year running, Nevada's gambling metropolis will transform its famous 'Strip' into a nighttime racing circuit flanked by giant, illuminated casinos, from Thursday through Saturday.

While Antonelli, confirmed as the youngest world champion in F1 history, can soak up the adulation, his teammate George Russell will jostle for points with multiple-time world champions Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, in the 21st of 23 rounds this season.

"Winning both world championships was an incredible achievement and we have taken the time to celebrate that," said Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff.

But Wolff insisted it was "back to work," with the team goals of "helping George finish as high as possible in the drivers' championship, ending the year with momentum, and continuing to unlock more performance from the car."

Russell has endured a challenging season. The British driver has won only three Grand Prix races, totally overshadowed by his 20-year-old Italian prodigy teammate.

Russell sits third in the rankings on 262 points, trailing Red Bull's Verstappen, who is enjoying a stellar end to the season, by 17, and leading Ferrari's Hamilton by a single point.

While Verstappen and Hamilton, with 11 world titles between them, are unlikely to be too preoccupied by the goal of finishing the season in second place, two other men could yet storm up the rankings.

Hamilton's Monegasque teammate Charles Leclerc, on 249 points, and 2025 world champion Lando Norris of McLaren, on 246, can also grab the runner-up slot, with season-capping races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi still on the calendar.

Organizers say those rounds, set for late November and early December respectively, will go ahead despite the uncertainty caused by ongoing war in the Middle East region.

The Saudi Arabia Grand Prix earlier this year was scrapped following the outbreak of the United States and Israel's war with Iran, while the Bahrain race was delayed and moved to Malaysia.

- 'Down to the wire' -

Mercedes, with 652 points, has emphatically wrapped up the constructors' title, far ahead of Ferrari on 510 and Red Bull on 415.

Verstappen, who won last year's Las Vegas race, and Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar are ending the season in strong form. But their team could still be knocked off the podium by McLaren, spearheaded by Norris and Oscar Piastri.

The British outfit, which won the 2024 and 2025 titles, currently sits on 398 points and racing director Randy Singh has vowed to "do our best to make sure it goes down to the wire and in our favor."

Chasing third place, "we've got plenty of time to try and harvest as many points as we can," he said.

Saturday's 50-lap, 193-mile (310-km) race begins at 8:00pm local time (0400 GMT Sunday).

Piastri, who has had a lackluster season, faces a ten-place grid penalty after taking his fifth internal combustion engine of the season.

But McLaren will hope the Australian can make up ground on the very long 3.9-mile Las Vegas circuit, which features two lengthy straights up which cars have reached speeds above 220 miles per hour, as well as 17 corners.

In the third US Grand Prix of the year -- after Miami and Austin -- the Nevada desert night could provide the coldest conditions of the entire season, posing a challenge for getting tires up to the optimal operating temperatures.

World.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after dispute
World.content:
NEW YORK - A Vincent van Gogh masterpiece sold for a record-breaking $190.4 million Wednesday after a dispute between the seller and the heirs of a previous Jewish owner who sold it in the Nazi era, Sotheby's said.

"Chataigniers en fleurs" (Chestnut Trees in Blossom) painted in 1890 in Auvers-sur-Oise, France set a new record for the Dutch post-Impressionist and became the most expensive work auctioned off so far this season.

The previous auction record for a painting by Van Gogh was $117.2 million for the 1888 "Orchard with Cypresses" at Christie's in New York in November 2022.

An influential German publisher, Samuel Fischer, acquired the painting in Paris in 1909 and his family sold it in 1936.

His heirs had previously opposed the sale, saying Fischer's family parted with the painting only because of financial losses suffered under the Nazis.

The heirs' Berlin-based lawyer, Gunnar Schnabel, had called on Sotheby's to prove the painting was sold at its market value and that the family would have sold it regardless of the political context.

The Blaquier-Arrieta family acquired the painting in 1975 and has owned it for more than half a century, according to Sotheby's.

But on Tuesday, Sotheby's said "an agreement has been reached between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and all of the legal descendants of Hedwig and Samuel Fischer regarding the sale of Vincent van Gogh's Chataigniers en fleurs."

Schnabel did not respond to an AFP request for comment.

According to Sotheby's, the Fischer heirs said they were "grateful for the trusting and fair negotiation and collaboration with Sotheby's and the Blaquier-Arrieta family, which make it possible to acknowledge the suffering of the Fischer family during the Nazi era and honor Gisela Berman Fischer's history of seeking justice for her family."

World.title: Search for Anqobile Jiyela resumes after severe weather halts rescue efforts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The search for 11-year-old Anqobile Jiyela is expected to resume on Thursday after dangerous weather conditions forced emergency teams to suspend rescue operations on Wednesday.

Anqobile was swept away by a flash flood on Tuesday afternoon after her scholar transport dropped her off near a stream.

Emergency responders have been working to locate the young girl, but worsening weather conditions forced teams to temporarily halt their efforts.

Anqobile’s uncle, Tshepo Mokoena, said the family had been left heartbroken by the tragedy.

“We just want to find her body,” Mokoena said.

“Her father is really heartbroken; he can’t even speak. We hope, with the rescue teams here, the body can be found so we can bury my niece.”

Meanwhile, tragedy struck Dobsonville Extension 3, where the body of a man believed to be in his 40s was recovered on Tuesday.

The man reportedly drowned while attempting to cross a flooded stream.

World.title: Xi-Trump-Putin summit expected to be more symbol than substance
World.content:
WASHINGTON - The tightly choreographed talks between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to take place Thursday at a sprawling Chinese resort are expected to be heavy on images and light on concrete outcomes, experts said.

The historic three-president summit will happen just outside the bustle of central Shenzhen at the Kylin Villa, which has hosted foreign VIPs before, including one of North Korea's leaders.

But every detail of this summit will be closely scrutinised for meaning and indications of what happens behind the closed doors of the lakeside complex bordered by mountains.

"Typically, when Chinese leaders host meetings, every detail is nailed down and China's leader is positioned to project an air of serene authority and control," Ryan Hass at the Brookings Institution told AFP.

Chinese President Xi's staff "will do their utmost to minimise space for surprise or unexpected outcomes at the trilateral meeting", he said.

"Given the other leaders involved though, Trump and Putin, there is only so much choreography that can be done to eliminate unexpected moments."

Thursday's meeting, the first ever between the three powerful men, will be on the sidelines of the major annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering.

Opened in 1997, Kylin is an official reception venue for Chinese leaders and foreign dignitaries.

Behind its peaceful setting, the complex holds sprawling facilities: more than 20 meeting rooms with a total capacity of 1,600 people, around 20 restaurants and a hall that can host 480 guests.

Kylin Villa is said to have hosted Kim Jong Il, father of the current North Korean leader, during a visit in 2006, according to South Korean press reports.

- 'Direct and efficient' -

Some fear the leaders at Thursday's meeting may seek to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions on Ukraine's fate without consulting Kyiv or Europe.

China has said they will hold "in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations".

Efforts will probably be taken "to ensure the dialogue remains direct and efficient", said Wang Wen of Renmin University of China.

"Only a streamlined core group, comprising the heads of state, foreign ministers, national security officials, and a few other key personnel, will be present in the main meeting room," Wang said.

However, each nation "will bring a full delegation, with staff teams specialising in diplomacy, security, and economics standing by to provide policy support and coordinate text" for a potential joint statement.

Either way, optics are all-important at the lakeside villa, removed from central Shenzhen's tech-hub bustle, and surrounded by lush greenery and landscaped gardens.

- No breakthrough expected -

Media access will be carefully controlled to present the talks to the outside world in ways that show Xi is in control and that "limit any perception that events are going off script", Hass said.

The three leaders will likely want an image to come out of the meeting that shows them consulting together, not big teams meeting around a large, impersonal table.

"And they will want a communique of some sort to memorialise the occasion for posterity," Hass added.

Any such statement could be brief, and not highly binding, with possible broad commitments such as maintaining regular channels of communication and upholding nuclear stability.

Whether the leaders announce plans to meet again will also be a closely watched point.

"It isn't easy to organise such a meeting, but in this specific case, the three leaders' interests converged," Russian political analyst Konstantin Kalachev told AFP.

"Even if we shouldn't expect a geopolitical breakthrough, holding this meeting will help strengthen the image of each of the three participants," he said.

"In Russia, for example, it will be said after this meeting that Russia belongs to the key countries on the global stage and that the EU countries do not."

By Sam Davies And Katie Forster

World.title: Harry Styles, Cher to headline Glastonbury
World.content:
LONDON - The UK's iconic Glastonbury Festival on Wednesday unveiled its 2027 line-up with top names Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender, set to headline alongside veteran star Cher.

Tickets for the event next June sold out in 45 minutes last month with thousands rushing for sought-after places despite the hefty price tag.

Other big names on the bill include Massive Attack, Lily Allen, Lola Young, Kraftwerk, Texas and De La Soul, according to the line-up poster released on the festival's website.

Country star Kacey Musgraves, rising star FKA twigs and newcomer Adela also make the cut, with more acts still to be announced.

Cher, 80, will play the legend slot on Sunday. Aged 81 by the time she performs she will be the oldest artist to do so, taking the crown from Rod Stewart.

The festival held at Worthy Farm in southwest England has become a fixture of the international musical calendar, after first launching in 1970 inspired by British hippie and counterculture movements.

Prices have risen steadily in the last decade, with standard tickets costing £408 ($539) for the June 2027 iteration, which follows the "fallow year" of no festival in 2026.

"We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year," said organiser Emily Eavis on Instagram, describing the line-up as an "incredible" spread of artists.

World.title: 'Rockstar' climate expert urges world to defend science
World.content:
ANTALYA - He's briefed world leaders and business tycoons, appeared in a documentary with Leonardo DiCaprio, and amassed a cult following with his animated, no-nonsense warnings about the perils of climate change.

For a scientist, Johan Rockstrom is about as close to a rock star as it gets and at the United Nations climate conferences, the straight-talking Swede is in his element.

But this year, Rockstrom is on the offensive as science emerges as a key battleground at COP31 in Turkey.

Debates have dragged over the science of crossing the 1.5C temperature limit while a long-running standoff over the work of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has spilled into the talks.

Rockstrom, who is director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research in Germany, paused to speak with AFP after shaking hands with admirers in Antalya. This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Q: You've been warning for years that the 1.5C goal would be crossed without urgent cuts to planet-heating emissions. The UN says overshooting 1.5C is now imminent and unavoidable. Have we failed this goal?

A: "I think science clearly shows that we need to have a more nuanced way of describing this. The first is that we have to admit failure. We signed the Paris agreement 11 years ago and so far we've just added emissions. And now we will inevitably be crashing through the 1.5C limit. That is failure so far and that has to be admitted, because that's the key why we need to accelerate. For every year that we fail in bending the curve, the pathway to safety becomes steeper and steeper."

Q: Where are we heading?

A: "We're not following a pathway that brings us back to 1.5C. We're following a pathway that takes us to 2.8C, 2.9C, perhaps even 3C of warming within just 75 years... there's no evidence we can support the world as we know it at that level. It's a path to disaster."

Q: Does science have a solution?

A: "The best the science can offer is to limit warming, and peak warming, somewhere around 1.8C and then potentially bring it back to 1.5C. And that is what policy-wise is described as 'keeping 1.5C alive'. But that is an enormously heavy lift... and the first step is the most urgent one, which is to put a brake on warming."

Q: So by drastically and immediately reducing emissions, and then pulling carbon from the atmosphere, it might theoretically be possible in future to return to 1.5C?

A: "I think it is correct to say that 1.5C is theoretically still possible. We definitely need to hold on to it as the landing zone. That would be a big mistake to now compromise with 1.5C.

"Exceeding 1.5C brings us into danger in two ways. One is that it increases the frequency and severity of extreme events... but it's also pushing us closer to tipping points which if crossed, would bring us to irreversible changes that would push us forever into less and less liveable conditions on Earth."

Q: Some nations at COP31 have questioned recent studies into overshooting 1.5C -- is the science sound?

A: "This is obstruction, it's complete nonsense, and everybody knows that... these are robust, scientifically verified scenarios."

Q: There's also a separate spat involving the IPCC, with some nations pushing to delay the publication of its next major reports. Is science under attack here?

A: "We are seeing efforts of doing that -- to undermine the role of science as the basis for the whole policy regime around climate. This is highly frustrating... We have to stand up and defend science very, very clearly."

Q: Are you optimistic humanity will change course?

A: "That's the big question, isn't it? If you look at the world today, the answer would be -- I'm sceptical.

"We are in a world that is so fragmented and focusing entirely on geopolitics... In that sense I'm really, really nervous."

Q: Is there any light in the tunnel?

A: "We are on a journey. We're showing that solar, wind, biomass, hydro, efficiency of energy systems, are starting to scale in a way that almost exceeds our expectations.

"We are at this collision point. That is one reason why countries that feel threatened are digging in their heels even deeper. Because they see this is no longer a sideshow -- this is a main show. This is really the path toward not only solving the climate crisis, but it's also a pathway to competitiveness."

World.title: New Zealand, India lean on seam for first Test in Wellington
World.content:
WELLINGTON - New Zealand said Wednesday they would play four seamers in the first Test against India in Wellington, kicking off a hectic period of six matches in seven weeks for Tom Latham's side.

India under captain Shubman Gill will also field four pace bowlers for Thursday's opening match of the two-Test series on a Basin Reserve pitch expected to favour the seamers.

Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Nathan Smith and the returning Kyle Jamieson will lead New Zealand's attack, Latham told reporters.

The series sees the two nations clash in red-ball cricket for the first time since New Zealand's historic 3-0 Test series win in India in 2024.

Gill described having to choose which of his brigade of top-class bowlers to leave out as a "good kind of headache".

"All the fast bowlers did pretty well (in the ODI series) and we are still deciding on the final combination, which fast bowlers to go with," said Gill.

Quick bowling great Jasprit Bumrah is almost certain to lead the attack in what will be his first Test match for almost a year.

Bumrah played one warm-up match for India A against New Zealand A in Christchurch, bowling six wicketless overs before rain intervened.

"We know he's going to be a huge challenge especially on the surfaces that we have here," said Latham.

- Race to WTC final -

New Zealand's two Tests against India at home will be followed by four away in Australia, with all counting for the current World Test Championship cycle.

New Zealand top the WTC table after four wins in their first six matches as they seek to become the first team to win the competition twice.

The top two in the standings will progress to next year's final.

"What we focus on is the things that we can do and the things that we can control," Latham said when asked about the WTC.

"And we know if we do that, then hopefully we'll give ourselves a chance of being in the race for those top two positions come March."

Gill said the WTC was a priority for India, who sit fourth in the standings and will play a five-Test series at home against Australia beginning in January.

"I believe if we win these two Test matches we have a very good chance at playing the WTC final," he said.

"Even before coming here I knew these two Test matches are going to be really crucial."

Latham said his players would not be distracted by the launch of blockbuster video game Grand Theft Auto VI, which becomes available at midnight on the eve of the Test, with New Zealand the first country to receive it.

New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra told AFP he had agreed with coach Rob Walter to avoid late nights in "Vice City", where the game is set.

"Well, I'm not a gamer," Latham said, smiling.

"But there's obviously been a little bit of chat about it, that it comes out at midnight or whatever it is.

"But yeah, we certainly trust guys to prepare the best they can for the next couple of days."

The second Test in Christchurch begins on November 27.

World.title: Ruto lists measures to lower cost of living, put more money in Kenyans' pockets
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto during his State Of The Nation Address at Parliament, Nairobi. November 18th, 2026. [Elvis Ogina, Standard]

President William Ruto has outlined a raft of government interventions aimed at reducing the cost of living, increasing household incomes and creating more employment opportunities for Kenyans.

Addressing Parliament during the 2026 State of the Nation Address on Wednesday, Ruto said his administration had prioritised lowering the cost of essential goods and services while increasing earnings across key sectors of the economy.

“Our economic proposition was simple: Reduce the cost for families and increase the income from what they do,” he said.

On food prices, the President cited the government’s fertiliser subsidy programme, which has reduced the price of a 50-kilogramme bag of fertiliser from Sh7,500 in 2022 to Sh2,000 this year.

He said the government had distributed 38.5 million bags of subsidised fertiliser to farmers, contributing to an increase in maize production from 44.3 million bags in 2022 to 71 million bags last year.

Consequently, maize imports declined from 9.9 million bags to 3.3 million bags, while the average price of a two-kilogramme packet of sifted maize flour dropped from a high of Sh230 in September 2022 to Sh152 in September this year.

Ruto also highlighted gains in the tea, coffee, dairy and sugar industries, saying government interventions had helped improve production and increase farmers' earnings.

He said the Cherry Advance Revolving Fund had disbursed Sh15.07 billion to 684,000 coffee farmers, while tea export earnings increased from Sh163 billion in 2022 to Sh187 billion in 2025.

In the dairy sector, milk production rose from 4.5 billion litres to 5.52 billion litres, while average earnings for farmers increased from Sh32 to Sh60 per litre last month.

Sugar production, he added, increased by 60 per cent between January and October, with cane crushing rising by 57 per cent. The industry is projected to produce more than 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, with Sh1.2 billion in bonuses expected to be paid to sugarcane farmers.

On healthcare, Ruto said the Social Health Authority (SHA) was designed to ease the financial burden of medical expenses on households through a shared health financing system.

In education, he said the government had employed 100,000 teachers and was preparing to recruit an additional 20,000 to address staffing shortages and reduce the burden on parents who pay teachers hired through Boards of Management.

He added that 23,000 classrooms had been constructed, while 1,600 laboratories were being built and equipped.

The President said the annual education allocation had increased from Sh521 billion in the 2022/23 financial year to Sh784 billion in the current financial year.

"These investments improve the quality of education while progressively reducing the need for Kenyans to finance education," he said.

On affordable housing, Ruto said more than 313,000 homes were at different stages of construction across the 47 counties, with over 1.37 million Kenyans registered on the Boma Yangu platform and more than 18,000 homes already allocated.

He said households could work towards homeownership through monthly payments starting at Sh4,000, which he argued would help ease the burden of rent.

The housing programme, according to the President, had also generated more than 1.1 million employment opportunities and reserved orders worth over Sh61 billion for Jua Kali artisans.

On employment, Ruto said 350,000 Kenyans had secured jobs through the digital economy programme, while another 707,000 had obtained employment abroad through international labour mobility initiatives.

He also cited the Hustler Fund, saying more than seven million Kenyans had established credit records through the programme, with cumulative borrowing reaching Sh94 billion.

Under the NYOTA programme, more than 133,000 young entrepreneurs had received training, mentorship and Sh50,000 each in start-up capital, he said.

The President further announced proposed tax measures aimed at increasing disposable incomes, including exempting workers earning Sh32,333 or less per month from Pay As You Earn (PAYE).

Other proposals include scrapping stamp duty on land transactions valued at Sh1 million or less and removing the 25 per cent import duty on mobile phones.

On pending bills, Ruto said the government had approved the settlement of 28,726 verified claims amounting to Sh27.8 billion, covering debts of Sh50 million and below dating back to 2005.

He added that Sh18 billion owed to public universities and another Sh16 billion owed to public and private hospitals under the former National Hospital Insurance Fund (NHIF) had been approved for payment and were undergoing Treasury processing.

“These are not isolated interventions, but parts of one comprehensive undertaking,” Ruto said.

He maintained that the government's economic strategy was anchored on reducing household expenditure, increasing incomes and expanding opportunities for Kenyans.

World.title: After 22 years of waiting, woman welcomes quadruplet boys
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Samuel Langat speaks to journalists outside St Clare's Kaplong Mission hospital in Sotik Subcounty, Bomet county after his wife Lily Langat gave to quadruplets at the hospital. [Kiprono Kurgat, Standard]

After 22 years of waiting to become a mother, a woman has welcomed quadruplet boys in a rare and joyful birth that has brought immense happiness to her family.

Lily Langat delivered the quadruplets through a Caesarean section at St Clare’s Kaplong Mission Hospital in Sotik Sub-County on November 14, 2026.

The four boys arrived after more than two decades of waiting for a child in what the family described as a double blessing.

The 43-year-old mother could not hide her joy, saying the arrival of the four babies was an answer to years of prayer.

“I am very grateful to God for giving me four babies at once. This is a great blessing to my family. I thank the hospital staff for ensuring I got to see these bundles of joy,” she said.

“I have been praying and waiting upon God to give me double for the trouble. I have been childless for a long time, and God could not have given me a better gift than this,” she added.

She said she had been looking forward to the moment after doctors informed her early in the pregnancy that she could be carrying quadruplets.

Hospital staff celebrated the successful delivery, describing it as a rare occurrence at the facility.

A nurse who spoke with The Standard said the mother and her four newborns were in stable condition.

“We were delighted to deliver the babies. The mother faced some difficulties because of the combined weight of the four babies, but both she and the newborns are now stable,” she said.

The nurse said the babies had been placed in the nursery for observation and were doing well.

“This is a rare case in this hospital. We have had twins before, but this is different. None of the babies has developed complications so far, and we expect them to be discharged once they are fully stable,” she said.

She added that the mother was also recovering well and was expected to be discharged once doctors were satisfied with the condition of the newborns.

Lily's husband, Samuel Langat, appealed to well-wishers to support the family as they prepare to raise the four children.

“Raising four babies at once is no easy task. I am calling on well-wishers to lend a helping hand as we begin this extraordinary journey,” he said.

“Our four precious miracles have arrived safely, and while our hearts are overflowing with gratitude, the reality of caring for four newborns at once has brought challenges,” he added.

Naturally conceived quadruplets are extremely rare, although the likelihood varies depending on several factors, including maternal age and fertility treatment.

The birth marks a remarkable new beginning for the Langat family after 22 years of waiting for a child.

World.title: TSC picks Cheptumo Ayabei as new Chief Executive Officer
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Teachers Service Commission headquarters in Nairobi. [File, Standard]

The Teachers Service Commission (TSC) has picked Cheptumo Ayabei as its new Secretary and Chief Executive Officer, making him the first person with a disability to head the commission.

Ayabei emerged top in interviews conducted on Monday, beating four other candidates, including the commission’s acting chief executive, Dr Evaleen Jesang Mitei, to become the country’s top teachers’ employer.

His selection ends a prolonged search for a substantive head of the commission, which has operated under acting leadership since the departure of former CEO Nancy Macharia in June 2025.

Ayabei, who hails from Baringo County, is currently TSC’s Director of Finance, having served at the commission for more than two decades. He joined the institution in 1999 as a Finance Officer before rising through the ranks to become Director of Finance in 2009.

His elevation marks a significant milestone for the representation of persons with disabilities in the country’s public institutions.

Ayabei was the first candidate to face the selection panel at 9am at the commission’s headquarters in Upper Hill, Nairobi. He was followed by Mitei at 10am, Robert Odette at 11am, Lawrence Ngai Kaburu at noon and Farah Abdi Saman at 1pm.

The five candidates were shortlisted from 124 applicants who responded to a fresh  issued on September 29. Applications closed on October 30.

Ayabei holds a Bachelor of Education degree in Mathematics and Economics from Kenyatta University and a Master’s degree in Finance and Banking from the University of Stirling in the United Kingdom. He is also a Certified Public Accountant.

Before joining TSC, he worked at the Ministry of Education between 1990 and 1999.

He takes over at a critical time for the commission, which oversees the employment, deployment, promotion and discipline of teachers across the country. He will inherit mounting pressure over teacher shortages, recruitment, promotions, transfers and the management of the teaching workforce.

The recruitment process had faced legal challenges, with a petition filed at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Kisii seeking to halt the exercise.

The case, filed by Evans Morara Nyangongo under Cause E038 of 2026, challenged the fresh recruitment and raised questions about Mitei’s participation in the process while serving as acting CEO and seeking the substantive position.

Nyangongo sought to stop the commission from proceeding with the appointment until the issues raised in the petition were determined.

However, the court dismissed both the application and the suit, with no orders as to costs, clearing the way for the interviews.

In its defence, TSC maintained that the decision to advertise the position had been made collectively by the commission’s board and not by the acting CEO.

In a replying affidavit, TSC chairman Jamleck Muturi John maintained that Mitei had neither participated in the board’s deliberations on the recruitment nor influenced the process.

The fresh recruitment followed an earlier court decision that nullified the previous exercise over procedural irregularities, forcing the commission to restart the search for a substantive chief executive.

World.title: Thwake Dam project reaches 94pc completion
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Thwake Multipurpose Dam, which is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment.[File,Standard]

Thwake Dam is 94.2 per cent complete, with the government targeting April 2027 for water impoundment as residents seek a review of alleged construction-related damage claims.

Principal Secretary for Water and Sanitation Julius Korir told the National Assembly Departmental Committee on Blue Economy, Water and Irrigation that construction had reached 94.2 per cent.

The dam is being built at the confluence of the Athi and Thwake rivers along the Makueni-Kitui border. It is designed to provide water for domestic use, irrigation and electricity generation.

Martin Kimeu, a resident of Wote, said the project would improve access to water for farming in the region.

“Ukambani is fertile. Water has been the biggest impediment to the realization of our agricultural potential. Thwake Dam water is the clear solution to this,” he said.

Kimeu also defended the compensation process, saying he had followed the project since its inception and believed the exercise had been conducted properly.

Jacob Mwanzia, a resident of Madangi Village, said households in his area had been assessed and compensated. He argued that outstanding complaints should be addressed without delaying the project.

Mariam Mwikali, another resident, said assessments had been conducted on affected properties and residents given an opportunity to raise concerns.

However, some households have complained that construction-related blasting damaged their homes. Residents have reported cracks in walls, windows and foundations as well as dust, noise and ground vibrations.

In August 2026, residents from villages in Mavindini Ward, organised under the Thwake Dam Blasting-Affected Community Committee, sought an independent review by the African Development Bank (AfDB).

The residents alleged that some properties had been left out of assessments and compensation. They also sought access to assessment reports, photographs, measurements, valuation records and estimates for repairs or reconstruction.

A project official said the dam's safety department invited competitive bids for an independent assessment of properties potentially affected by blasting. Agile Consulting was selected to conduct the exercise.

The official said the consultant assessed 330 households within a two-kilometre radius of the construction site and submitted its report to the project implementation team. A large proportion of those assessed were satisfied with the exercise, the official added, without giving a breakdown.

Ben Mwongela, a director at Agile Consulting, said the assessment reviewed blasting records, vibration data and compliance with regulatory standards.

The exercise also involved documenting households, classifying structural defects and preparing bills of quantities and cost estimates for repairs or reconstruction, he said.

The AfDB conducted a field mission to the project between September 21 and 25, with its report published on October 21, 2026.

The bank's team, led by project task manager Nancy Ogal, met residents whose homes had been affected by blasting and identified outstanding health, safety, environmental and social issues, including homeowner grievances.

The bank called for timely compensation and continued monitoring of the project's environmental and social performance.

During a stakeholder engagement visit to Mavindini in October, Korir said the government had secured additional funding after the project experienced cash-flow constraints.

“When we ran short of cash, we engaged with our development partners, and they allocated additional funding, and this money will now go towards total completion of the project,” he said.

In June 2026, the AfDB approved additional financing of €68.39 million to support completion of the first phase, alongside funding from the Kenyan government.

The bank said the financing would support engineering refinements and safety works, including strengthening foundations, raising the dam and constructing two additional saddle dams.

The project has four phases. The first involves construction of the dam, while the subsequent phases cover hydropower generation, water supply and sanitation infrastructure, and irrigation.

The dam is approximately 80.5 metres high and has a planned storage capacity of 688 million cubic metres.

Once the water supply component is operational, the project is expected to provide 150,000 cubic metres of treated water daily to an estimated 1.3 million people in Makueni and Kitui counties and Konza Technopolis in Machakos County.

The irrigation scheme is designed to cover 40,000 hectares, equivalent to about 100,000 acres of agricultural land.

The project is also designed to generate 20 megawatts of hydropower.

The water supply, irrigation and hydropower components require infrastructure beyond the dam structure, including treatment and distribution networks and power generation facilities.

World.title: Love under watch: How technology is fuelling intimate partner abuse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Your enemy is closer than you think. For many Kenyan women, the person who demands a phone password, reads private messages and tracks their movements through a screen is not a faceless troll. He is the man they live with, or the one they used to.

That is the uncomfortable picture painted by the recently released 2025–2626 Kenya Mini Demographic and Health Survey (KMDHS), which measured technology-facilitated gender-based violence, abuse committed, assisted, aggravated or amplified through digital tools.

The most common form of abuse is online control, reported by 19 per cent of women, followed by hacking at 5 per cent and online sexual harassment or cyber sexual abuse at 3 per cent. Most of it happens on platforms women use every day.

“Sixty-seven per cent of women who experienced digital gender violence say it happened on social media, with Facebook cited by 59 per cent. Messaging apps follow at 47 per cent, with WhatsApp at 26 per cent. Among girls aged 15–19, 77 per cent reported abuse on social media.”

The report shows how widespread the abuse is. “Twenty-six percent of women age 15–49 have ever experienced technology-facilitated violence from any perpetrator,” the report says, and 21 per cent experienced it often or sometimes in the 12 months before the survey. Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced it at the hands of a current, most recent or previous partner.

The burden is not spread evenly, the report states that Nairobi City records the highest lifetime experience from any perpetrator at 33 per cent, followed by Murang’a and Baringo at 32 per cent each.

“For abuse by an intimate partner, Homa Bay 36 per cent and Baringo 35 per cent lead, while in the 12 months before the survey Trans Nzoia topped the list at 31 per cent. At the other end, Mandera and Wajir report just 3 per cent, a figure that may say as much about silence as about safety,” the report says

The picture is similar among young people. A 2024 rapid study by the Collaborative Centre for Gender and Development, working with the UNFPA and Women Economic Empowerment, found that nearly 90 per cent of young adults enrolled in three Nairobi tertiary institutions had witnessed TFGBV, and 39 per cent had experienced it personally.

Among women who have ever had a husband or intimate partner, 27 per cent have experienced gender violence committed by a current, most recent or previous partner, and 22 per cent did so in the past year. When women were asked who was responsible, the answer was blunt. Current husbands or intimate partners accounted for 61 per cent of perpetrators, former partners for 22 per cent and strangers for just 13 per cent.

Women who have never been married or had a partner face a different threat. For them, the most common perpetrators are strangers at 45 per cent, online attackers at 23 per cent and friends or acquaintances at 20 per cent.

Warning signs

Control is the common thread. The report describes such behaviours by a male partner as “important early warning signs that may escalate into violence within a relationship.”

Sixty-one per cent of ever-partnered women say their current or most recent partner has shown at least one controlling behaviour, and 27 per cent report three or more. Half say he has been jealous or angry when they spoke to other men, and 36 per cent say he insists on knowing where they are at all times. Others describe partners who demand passwords or read messages without consent.

Age and marital status matter. Technology-based gender violence is lowest among girls aged 15–19 at 10 per cent and highest among women aged 20–24 at 37 per cent. Forty-one per cent of divorced, separated or widowed women have experienced it, compared with 27 per cent of married women and 19 per cent of the never married.

Yet the digital rights advocate Cherie Oyier, a programmes officer at the Kenya ICT Action Network (KICTANet), says the low figures in some places should not be read as safety. Much of the abuse happens where nobody can see it.

“Closed applications, meaning like WhatsApp, those are the ones that most people, intimate partners will usually use,” she says. “Even as you are scrolling the internet to look for these instances, we may not be able to catch it. But it does not mean that it is not happening or that it is at a lower level.”

Culture also silences women. “Most women are told just endure, this is what marriage is about,” Oyier says. “Sometimes they don’t know, it’s so overt, like it doesn’t come out clearly that this is abuse. So most of the times, it is not reported.”

Online, abuse has been turned into entertainment. “It has become banter,” she says. “Even the people who are experiencing it have trivialised it. It’s now ingrained to you, like this is something that happens, you should expect it actually. If you post a picture, one of the things that you are thinking about is what kind of comments am I going to get.”

A 2023 report by KICTANet found that more than 30 per cent of Kenyans have experienced some form of TFGBV, while 90 per cent have witnessed it. In 2025, KICTANet and Equality Now released survivor testimonies showing how deceptive online job offers, grooming and image-based abuse leave women exposed, and how many had never received counselling despite years of trauma.

The stakes are not only digital. The 2025 Report of the Technical Working Group on GBV Including Femicide, cited in the KMDHS, indicated that many cases of homicide of women and girls, and of sexual and physical harm directed towards them, “are preceded by online and offline harassment using digital tools.”

For survivors, the law offers little comfort. “The technology is moving at a very fast pace compared to the laws,” Oyier says. In an attempt to bolster the gaps, Kenya has many fragmented laws. “You’ll have the Data Protection Act, the Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act, the Children’s Act, that to some extent touch on online issues, but they don’t really cohesively cover the different instances of TFGBV.”

The police, she says, often do not know either. “Just imagine you’re a woman who is in a village, for example, a village in Siaya, and you encounter violence. For you to even understand which law apply is very stressful.”

“You’re going through psychological stress and depression, and you’re also supposed to figure out which law applies in your situation. It causes even more problems for victims and survivors.”

Flagging abusive language

Artificial intelligence is adding a new layer. Even so, Oyier cautions against writing it off. “We should not vilify AI completely,” she says. KICTANet has built a lexicon to help flag abusive language and runs a tracker for online gender-based violence. “One person cannot sit down and look at everything on social media. When AI is able to pull every post that has this word, a human content moderator is able to look through it with local context and see is this TFGBV or not.”

The KMDHS findings further show that exposure to TFGBV varies across age groups and digital platforms.

“Younger women are particularly exposed on social media, with 77 per cent of women aged 15–19 and 72 per cent of those aged 20–24 who experienced TFGBV reporting abuse on social media platforms, compared with 50 per cent of women aged 40–49.”

However, messaging applications tell a different story. Women aged 40–49 reported the highest exposure through these platforms at 54 per cent, compared with 30 per cent among teenagers aged 15–19.

Wealth also influences where women encounter online abuse. Exposure on social media increases from 45 per cent among women in the lowest wealth quintile to 74 per cent among those in the highest. Conversely, women in the lowest wealth quintile report greater exposure through messaging applications, at 62 per cent, compared with 39 per cent among those in the highest wealth quintile.

These differences suggest that TFGBV cuts across age and economic backgrounds, although the platforms through which women experience it vary.

World.title: Not so fast: Court slams brake on ARA over wealth forfeiture
World.content:
Felix Mecha Nyakundi could not provide a plausible explanation for how he amassed his wealth.

The Court of Appeal has ruled that the government cannot go after a person’s wealth without prior investigations to establish reasonable grounds for suspecting that the property constitutes proceeds of crime.

In a landmark judgment, Justices Patrick Kiage, Jamila Mohammed and Nduma Nderi said that although it does not require a person to be charged for a crime for the Asset Recovery Agency (ARA) to come knocking, it bears the responsibility to link the wealth or cash to a crime.

World.title: Back to sender: Aisha Jumwa returns to UDA
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto welcome former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa has returned to President William Ruto’s United Democratic Alliance (UDA), ending a three-month political fallout with the ruling party that saw her join opposition outfit Wiper Patriotic Front and declare support for the one-term movement ahead of the 2027 General Election.

President Ruto welcomed Jumwa back into UDA at State House, Mombasa, on Thursday, November 12, 2026, in a political reunion that could reshape alignments in Kilifi County and the wider Coast region as parties position themselves for next year's elections.

The reunion comes barely three months after Jumwa dramatically announced her departure from UDA, accusing the party leadership of frustrating her political ambitions and failing to support her quest for the Kilifi gubernatorial seat.

On July 30, 2026, Jumwa announced her resignation during a press conference at her Kakuyuni home in Malindi, saying her attempts to have her grievances addressed by the President had repeatedly been unsuccessful.

Among her concerns was what she described as humiliation and rejection within the ruling party, including an alleged incident in which she was chased out of State House during a meeting between Ruto and Coast leaders.

She also accused sections of the ruling coalition of undermining her gubernatorial ambitions, claiming that the political arrangements being pursued in Kilifi were designed to deny her an opportunity to contest for the county's top seat.

President William Ruto recieve former Cabinet Secretary Aisha Jumwa back to the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA) on November 12, 2026. [PCS]

Jumwa, who was among UDA's founding members and one of Ruto's most vocal mobilisers at the Coast during the 2022 elections, said her loyalty to the people of Kilifi outweighed her allegiance to any political party.

"My loyalty to the people of Kilifi will always be greater than my loyalty to any political party. The voice of the people of Kilifi is louder than the voice of UDA," she declared during her exit announcement.

Her departure marked a significant political shift, particularly given her central role in mobilising support for Ruto in the Coast region.

In August, Jumwa turned to the opposition, where she was warmly received by Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka, who visited her at her Kakuyuni residence on August 14 alongside a delegation of party leaders, including Nyali MP Mohamed Ali, Kitui Senator Enoch Wambua and Wundanyi MP Danson Mwashako.

Kalonzo subsequently proposed Jumwa for the position of Wiper Deputy Party Leader, citing her political experience and influence, while also backing her ambition to contest the Kilifi governorship on a Wiper ticket.

Jumwa embraced the new political alliance, declaring support for the one-term movement and threatening to mobilise UDA supporters in Kilifi to deregister from the ruling party and join Wiper.

"We are the ones who registered UDA members in Kilifi, and we are embarking on a grassroots campaign to deregister them from UDA and join Wiper," she said at the time.

On September 8, she attended a meeting involving Wiper leaders and Coast gubernatorial aspirants, including Mohammed Ali and Danson Mwashako, as the party intensified efforts to expand its influence in the region.

However, the political alliance has now taken another turn, with Jumwa returning to the party she had accused of frustrating her ambitions.

Announcing her return, President Ruto welcomed the former Cabinet Secretary back into UDA, signalling renewed efforts to consolidate the ruling party's support in the Coast region.

"I look forward to working with her to advance the party’s transformation agenda at the Coast and across the country. We remain committed to uniting leaders and Kenyans around our shared vision of a united, inclusive and prosperous Kenya," the President said.

Her return comes as Ruto steps up political mobilisation in the Coast region ahead of the 2027 elections, with Kilifi emerging as an important battleground for competing political formations.

Jumwa's political journey has been characterised by shifting alliances. She previously served under the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM), representing Malindi in Parliament before becoming Kilifi's first Woman Representative between 2013 and 2017.

She later became one of Ruto's key political allies and served in his Cabinet.

World.title: Nvidia rules out Jensen Huang’s return as CEO, tells investors ‘we’ve got this’
World.content:
New York —
