Bustinduy adjetivó como “giro radical e histórico” el aprobado para el sistema de dependencia, con una dotación extra de 6.200 millones, una previsión para 2027 de 7.239 y una aportación del 50% por parte del Estado para acabar con las listas de espera el próximo año. Los socios de izquierda incidieron en la importancia de que esa financiación prometida esta vez llegue. Rocío de Meer, de Vox, no cree nada de un gobierno que entiende que lleva “ocho años robando y despilfarrando”. La popular Ana Isabel Alós acabó como había empezado la sesión el PP apelando a se vote el 29-N a Feijóo para que “haga verdad los cheques en blanco” que le deja en herencia el actual Gobierno de coalición de Pedro Sánchez.

World.title: Irene Montero y Vito Quiles o cómo una misma escena se convierte en dos vídeos antagónicos con millones de visitas
World.content:
El agitador ultra publica unas imágenes en redes que contrastan con las mismas que publica la candidata. “Él manda a un tipo a vigilarnos para saber siempre dónde estamos”, cuentan fuentes de Podemos

Vito Quiles subió hace unos días un vídeo a su perfil de X. El agitador ultra se fue hasta Alcalá de Henares para hacer unas preguntas por la calle a Irene Montero, que estaba de campaña electoral. La candidata de Podemos a la Presidencia del Gobierno había acudido a esta ciudad madrileña para hacer una declaración sobre el Plan Vive de la Comunidad de Madrid. Quiles subió la entrevista a su cuenta de X a las 12.51. Las imágenes se viralizaron de inmediato. Ya acumulan 2,5 millones de visualizaciones.

El montaje empieza con Quiles paseando con una chaqueta verde y unos vaqueros y un micrófono de Estado de Alarma, el canal de Javier Negre rebautizado como EdaTV y que es regado a menudo con dinero de administraciones del PP. Rastrear cuánto ha recibido Negre de administraciones públicas españolas es una tarea endemoniada porque no existe una web que centralice esa información. Un análisis del diario El Salto reveló que administraciones populares habían pagado a EdaTV entre 2020 y 2025 al menos 680.000 euros. En el vídeo con Montero, Quiles empieza así:

—Señora Montero, muy buenos días, ¿qué tal la resaca de la huelga?

—Yo le doy los buenos días a los que ayer la Policía pegó a porrazos.

—Eso le iba a decir. ¿Usted condena que acosaran a un anciano en una cafetería?

La conversación continúa. Casualidad o no, en ese mismo momento el equipo de Montero también contaba con una cámara e incluso ella misma lleva un micrófono incorporado. De hecho, la cuenta de la candidata de Podemos subió otro vídeo de 40 segundos cuatro horas después de Quiles. Ambos vídeos son el día y la noche. Dos versiones diferentes. Antagónicas. Es más, otro usuario colgó también un vídeo donde sucede lo contrario al publicado por el agitador: más respuestas de Montero y Quiles, entrecortado.

En el vídeo del exmiembro de la candidatura de Alvise Pérez en las pasadas elecciones europeas, Montero le pregunta por uno de los guardaespaldas que le acompaña a menudo en sus actos por España y que, según eldiario.es, ha sido detenido en Rumanía hace unos días acusado de tráfico de cocaína. Él responde: “¿Quién? Pues no sé, sería proveedor del Gobierno, porque si traficaba con coca…”.

Quiles continúa: “Vive en un chalé de un millón de euros; su escolta daba palizas a la gente. ¿Por qué vivienda se manifiesta?, ¿por el chalé de Galapagar o por las que tiene con Pablo Iglesias?”. E insiste: “Hoy no me pregunta por quién me paga y eso me ofende [...] A mí me paga mi jefe y no mi marido [...] Está mal en las encuestas, eh, se pone a entrevistarme a mí”. Montero responde: “Tú me acosas”. Él dice: “Eso no es acoso. Acoso es lo que hace Errejón, su compañero [Juan Carlos] Monedero…”.

La charla termina con Montero cuestionando las jornadas de más de ocho horas que supuestamente hace Quiles. “Así somos los currantes en este país”, responde él. “Soy autónomo. A mí lo que me pasa es que me gusta trabajar [...] Bueno, nos vamos”.

En la grabación publicada por el equipo de Montero, que lleva como título “A Vito Quiles, el PP y Vox le explotan”, se ve a la candidata de Podemos preguntando al agitador si sabe los motivos por los que existen las jornadas laborales de ocho horas. “¿Te explotan en tu trabajo?, ¿aparte de pagarte PP y Vox, son unos explotadores?, ¿te explotan? No, espera. Graba esto, que dice que hay días que trabaja más de ocho horas. ¿Al que está grabando también le explota laboralmente? [...] Preocúpate por la violencia policial [...] Los delincuentes son los que van contigo”. Y cierra: “Menudo paseo”.

Las respuestas de Irene Montero apenas se oyen en el montaje que sube Vito Quiles. Solo aparecen las preguntas que hace él. Se trata de una estrategia habitual en sus vídeos, en los que, para quedar bien, omite las respuestas de sus entrevistados. De hecho, en 2024, el presentador David Broncano se cruzó con él por una calle de Madrid y estuvo 15 minutos charlando. El resultado fue la publicación de un vídeo de solo dos minutos. El propio Broncano se lo afeó y le contestó en su perfil de X: “Vito, pero al menos sube los dos vídeos enteros, que me has tenido un cuarto de hora ahí de charla para esto. Jajajaja. Increíble edición, vaya fenómeno”. Quiles respondió entonces que si quería que se subiera entero, tenía que ir de invitado a La Revuelta. No hubo más vídeos.

“Él hace una estrategia de intimidación política”, cuentan ahora fuentes del entorno de Montero. “Y, frente a eso, creemos que tenemos que dar una respuesta muy clara: no nos van a callar. Lo mínimo que vamos a hacer cuando nos acosen es llamarles por su nombre. No hay que minimizar lo que implica el acoso fascista para nosotras, pero tampoco queremos que se salgan con la suya. Se trata de que la gente tampoco tenga miedo. Que cuando alguien escuche a un familiar o conocido repitiendo un bulo difundido por Vito Quiles, también tenga una respuesta”. Por eso, ya van siempre con una cámara. ¿Y cómo sabe Quiles dónde se encuentra Montero?

“A través de nuestra agenda pública”, responden fuentes de la candidata. “Y, para pillarnos por sorpresa y desprevenidas, él manda a un tipo a vigilarnos para saber siempre dónde estamos. Le dice: ‘Va por esta calle, van por aquí’. Y así pilla a Irene en situaciones que él considera comprometidas, como subiendo a un coche o entrando en algún sitio. A este tipo ya le tenemos identificado y ya no tenemos ese factor sorpresa, pero nos sigue y les va avisando para tratar de cogernos con la guardia baja”. El vídeo de Montero, eso sí, lleva 360.000 visualizaciones. 1,2 millones menos que el de Quiles.

World.title: Isak Andic tramó con la terapeuta un plan para apartar definitivamente a su hijo Jonathan de Mango
World.content:
Isak Andic trazó un plan para lograr que su hijo mayor, Jonathan Andic, abandonara definitivamente todas sus responsabilidades en Mango. Aprovechando la terapia familiar a la que padre e hijo se sometían desde hacía meses para mejorar sus relaciones, el empresario pidió ayuda a Julia Lüderwaldt, la terapeuta, para convencer a Jonathan de que se tomara un “año sabático”, paso previo para cerrarle de forma definitiva las puertas de la multinacional de la moda. Así consta en el auto de la Audiencia de Barcelona que avala las medidas cautelares impuestas por la jueza de Martorell (Barcelona) contra el primogénito, investigado por el homicidio de su padre. El análisis de los mensajes indica que Isak Andic ocultó deliberadamente el plan a su hijo.

“El padre había decidido apartar a su hijo de Mango y pretendía que la separación terminara siendo definitiva”, concluyen los magistrados tras examinar los centenares de mensajes que obran en el sumario del caso Andic. Uno de ellos lo envió Isak Andic el 19 de septiembre de 2024, tres meses antes de su inesperado fallecimiento, durante una excursión a la montaña de Montserrat, a los 71 años. El empresario pidió ayuda a la terapeuta para que lograra, cuanto antes, convencer a Jonathan de que debía tomarse un año sabático. Si después de esa temporada decidía regresar, se le comunicaría que la familia debía quedar fuera de la gestión de la empresa, según la estratagema que confió a la terapeuta. El emprendedor le dejó claro que lo importante era “apartarlo de la empresa” para siempre. La terapeuta le sugirió que el plan quedara oculto a ojos de Jonathan.

Funcionó, según se constata en los mensajes. La terapeuta comunicó a Isak Andic que había convencido al primogénito y que éste preveía comunicárselo en diciembre. El día 11 de ese mes, solo tres días antes del suceso, Julia le dijo que el hijo estaba “emocionado” y que había preparado un paseo por un camino de la montaña de Montserrat para explicarle su año sabático. La investigación ha constatado que lo preparó a conciencia: la matrícula de su coche fue captada dos días esa misma semana, el 7 y 10 de diciembre.

“No consta que Jonathan Andic conociera el designio final de impedir su regreso”, subraya la resolución, por lo que, en consecuencia, no puede afirmarse que esa salida de Mango constituya el móvil de un posible crimen. Sí sabía, en cambio, que su continuidad en la empresa estaba “comprometida” y se había dado cuenta de que había perdido funciones en la empresa, como aparece reflejado en las comunicaciones del proceso terapéutico. En su declaración ante la jueza el pasado mayo, sin embargo, Jonathan Andic explicó que había quedado a hablar con su padre del nuevo proyecto personal en que quería embarcarse, pero no mencionó el año sabático, una omisión que llama la atención de los magistrados.

La actividad profesional está en el origen de las tensiones entre padre e hijo. En 2014, Isak Andic decidió tomarse, también él, un año sabático para salir a navegar con su velero Nirvana alrededor del mundo. Dejó Mango en manos de su hijo y de un equipo de directivos, y la empresa perdió el rumbo y arrojó resultados negativos. El fundador tuvo que regresar para reflotarla. Y, con independencia de los muchos factores que pudieron influir en la caída de la empresa, Jonathan Andic quedó señalado como uno de sus responsables. Era herida nunca acabó de curarse.

Las tensiones profesionales y económicas entre padre e hijo se mantuvieron a lo largo del tiempo, también en los meses anteriores a la muerte del empresario. Hasta el punto de que, como subraya la resolución, “el dinero ocupó una posición central en el proceso terapéutico y en la relación entre padre e hijo”. Jonathan Andic estaba convencido de que solo lograría su libertad personal si conseguía la plena independencia económica respecto de su padre y por ese motivo le planteó, desde principios de 2024, “pretensiones” económicas “de elevada entidad”: asignaciones anuales, participación en el grupo empresarial, capital para proyectos personales y medios de transporte.

La terapeuta llegó a apoyar el propósito inicial del primogénito de lograr una “herencia en vida” por parte de su padre, de unos 40 millones de euros, para emprender proyectos propios, como una sastrería. Pero esa iniciativa no se contempló y, según ha declarado esta misma semana el notario de siempre de Isak Andic, éste llegó a hacer dos aportaciones (de un total de cuatro millones) a favor de su hijo. Tanto esas asignaciones como otras a sus hermanas (Judith y Sarah) se reequilibraban anualmente en el testamento, que en todas sus versiones repartía el imperio Mango, a partes iguales, entre los tres hermanos.

Los tres hermanos conocían la intención de su padre de constituir una fundación benéfica. En su oposición al recurso de la defensa, la Fiscalía ha revelado que constan mensajes de Isak Andic en los que plantea la posibilidad de dejar a esa iniciativa “hasta la mitad de su patrimonio”. En el momento de su muerte, la revista Forbes estimaba el patrimonio del empresario, primera fortuna de Cataluña, en 4.500 millones de euros. La resolución, sin embargo, no entra demasiado en ese detalle y concluye que “la fundación no posee actualmente fuerza como móvil autónomo” de un eventual crimen. Tampoco existía “una amenaza cierta de desheredación” por lo que el móvil económico pierde, también en ese punto, fuerza.

World.title: Una investigación independiente concluye que la actividad de Núcleo Nacional servía a los intereses de Rusia
World.content:
Una investigación independiente ha constatado la existencia de conexiones en 11 países europeos del grupo neonazi Núcleo Nacional (NN), 14 de cuyos dirigentes fueron detenidos el pasado 6 de noviembre, acusados de los delitos de incitación al odio, asociación ilegal y tenencia ilícita de armas. Seis días después, el Juzgado de Instrucción número 1 de Gijón ordenó suspender sus actividades y congelar sus cuentas. Un informe realizado por Golden Owl, una startup vinculada al Parque Científico de la Universidad de Alicante y especializada en el análisis de inteligencia de fuentes abiertas, concluye que, aunque el grupo neonazi no tenía una posición oficial sobre la guerra de Ucrania y varios de sus miembros acudieron el pasado verano al país invadido por Rusia para recibir instrucción militar, en su seno operaba un sector favorable al Kremlin, que era el gran beneficiado de su actividad política. Núcleo Nacional ha confirmado este miércoles el fallecimiento en Valladolid de Enrique Lemus, de 63 años, fundador y jefe del brazo político del grupo, quien sufrió un infarto el pasado viernes cuando salía del juzgado.

La red de relaciones internacionales de NN incluye a Alemania, Bulgaria, Hungría, Italia, Croacia, Rumania, Francia, Países Bajos, Portugal, Reino Unido y Ucrania, según el informe. No todas las relaciones tienen la misma intensidad. Con Die III Weg (La Tercera Vía), cuyo nombre evoca al Tercer Reich y al que el servicio de inteligencia interior alemán (BfV) califica de “claramente proucranio”, ha habido una cooperación estable y organizativa e intercambio de visitas. También mantiene relaciones con las juventudes de Die Heimat (La Patria), el antiguo partido neonazi NPD; Casa Pound, el movimiento fascista italiano; o los franceses Comité 9 de mayo o RED d’ Angers, en trámite de disolución por su peligrosidad.

En el seno del Núcleo Nacional ―una organización que nació al calor de las protestas ante la sede del PSOE en noviembre de 2023 y cuya ideología define como “nacionalsocialista, antidemocrática y abiertamente antisemita”― conviven una dirección proclive a Kiev y un sector prorruso. No obstante, constata el informe, ambas han acabado resultando igualmente útiles para la narrativa del Kremlin, interesado en desestabilizar a los países occidentales que apoyan a Ucrania y minar la confianza en la OTAN y la UE.

El documento recuerda que el Núcleo Nacional inauguró su sede en Madrid con una conferencia en la que intervinieron Koldo Salazar, que posa en su perfil en las redes sociales ante la bandera y el escudo de Rusia y cierra su biografía con la letra Z, símbolo de la invasión de Ucrania, y ha sido condecorado en la Embajada rusa en Madrid; o Carlos Paz, comentarista del canal oficial ruso RT e invitado también a las recepciones por el Día de Rusia en la representación diplomática de dicho país en España. Esta conferencia “no fue un episodio aislado”, según el informe, que cita también al concejal de Velilla de San Antonio (Madrid) Pedro Jesús Espada, quien clamó “¡No a la guerra contra Rusia!”; o al dirigente Carlos Areta, quien escribió que “Rusia es la verdadera esperanza de Europa” y acusó al opositor ruso Alexei Navalni, muerto en prisión, de ser “un espía contra Rusia, pagado por los servicios británicos”.

El informe también menciona al fallecido Lemus, exdirigente de Democracia Nacional. Este último partido forma parte de la Alianza por la Paz y la Libertad (APL), en la órbita del Kremlin, y su vicepresidente, Gonzalo Martín, asistió en septiembre de 2025 en San Petersburgo (Rusia) al congreso fundacional de Palandins, la red del oligarca ruso Konstantin Malofeev, en el que intervino Aleksandr Dugin, filósofo de cabecera de Putin. Tras la detención de los “compañeros” de NN, Democracia Nacional condenó su “persecución por motivos políticos e ideológicos” y puso a su disposición sus servicios jurídicos.

Por el contrario, el presidente de Núcleo Nacional, Iván Rico, evita mencionar a Moscú en sus publicaciones y sus contactos internacionales se encuadran en su mayoría en el ala proucrania de la extrema derecha europea. En agosto pasado, viajó a las ciudades de Kiev y Járkov, donde, según la investigación policial, militantes de NN recibieron instrucción militar con armas largas y mantuvieron contacto con la brigada especial Azov, que se formó como una unidad de voluntarios vinculada a movimientos ultranacionalistas y de extrema derecha durante la guerra de Donbás en 2014 y se integró luego en la Guardia Nacional. La Embajada de Ucrania en Madrid ha negado que los neonazis españoles recibieran formación militar por parte de dicha brigada.

Paradójicamente, las relaciones de NN con Ucrania han sido ampliamente explotadas por Rusia, que ha utilizado las noticias sobre su instrucción militar en dicho país para alimentar su discurso sobre el supuesto carácter nazi del gobierno de Zelenski. Ruptly, la agencia de vídeo de RT, propiedad del Kremlin, publicó el 1 de septiembre las imágenes de Iván Rico en la capital ucrania bajo el título “El líder de los nazis españoles llegó a Kiev y posó con una esvástica”. Menos de hora y media después, estos mensajes ya circulaban por cuentas prorrusas en español. Tras la detención de los ultras españoles, los medios próximos al Kremlin han lanzado una campaña para denunciar que “Ucrania exporta nazismo”. “Dos caras, un solo beneficiario”, concluye el informe. “La corriente prorrusa [de Núcleo Nacional] promueve posiciones alineadas con los intereses estratégicos de Moscú. La corriente proucrania proporciona material que los medios estatales rusos utilizan para desacreditar a Ucrania. Ambos resultados pueden servir a los objetivos informativos de Rusia”.

Los investigadores creen que “existe un canal de influencia conectado con Rusia que llega al interior de Núcleo Nacional a través de relaciones organizativas documentadas y de personas con vínculos acreditados con instituciones del Estado ruso”. Reconocen, no obstante, que no han podido acreditar “financiación rusa, ningún pago del extranjero ni control operativo” desde fuera de España. Varios dirigentes de NN han asegurado que les ofrecieron dinero a agentes de otros países y lo rechazaron, pero Iván Rico reconoció: “El dinero es necesario y nos da igual quién lo aporte mientras nadie meta mano en Núcleo”.

Este punto es crucial, pues, en menos de tres años, Núcleo Nacional ya contaba con delegaciones en media docena de ciudades españolas, incluido un piso de 400 metros cuadrados en un barrio de oficinas de Madrid, un partido legal inscrito bajo el nombre de Noviembre Nacional y una cuenta en X con 115.000 seguidores cuyas publicaciones, recopiladas por los investigadores, suman más de 170 millones de visualizaciones. Sus mensajes se dirigen contra Pedro Sánchez y el PSOE, pero también contra el PP e incluso Vox, al que acusan de actuar al servicio del primer ministro israelí en funciones, Benjamin Netanyahu. En política exterior, atacan a la UE, la OTAN, EE UU o Israel, lo que coincide con los objetivos de Rusia.

Hay un punto, según constata el informe, en el que coinciden los dos sectores de NN, tanto el favorable a Moscú como el inclinado a Kiev; su alineamiento incondicional con el régimen iraní. El día en que comenzaron los ataques de EE UU e Israel contra Irán, la cuenta oficial del grupo publicó el siguiente mensaje: “No más guerras por interés judío. Irán aplasta al sionismo”. Con casi medio millón de visualizaciones, fue uno de los mensajes del grupo más vistos del año.

World.title: Núcleo Nacional anuncia la muerte de su dirigente Enrique Lemus
World.content:
El grupo neonazi Núcleo Nacional ha confirmado este miércoles el fallecimiento de uno de sus líderes ideológicos y dirigente, Enrique Lemus, a los 63 años. Lemus fue detenido el pasado 6 de noviembre en una operación policial contra la formación de ultraderecha y posteriormente puesto en libertad con medidas cautelares. “Padre, amigo y camarada, luchador leal hasta el final. Que Dios le guarde. Descansa en paz”, ha publicado la organización de extrema derecha en su cuenta de X. Núcleo Nacional señala en su perfil en redes sociales que el veterano miembro de la organización ultra había sufrido un infarto hace cinco días, al que no ha sobrevivido, debido a “un profundo deterioro de su estado de salud” tras la operación policial.

Lemus, definido por Núcleo Nacional como “padre” y “amigo”, formaba parte de la cúpula de este movimiento recientemente investigado por un juez de Gijón a cuenta de sus movimientos de captación de menores, habiendo protagonizado también incidentes violentos frecuentes. Núcleo Nacional atribuye su muerte a una “clara operación del gobierno”. Lemus comandó fuerzas políticas como España 2000 o Democracia Nacional y era conocido por su peso más ideológico que violento.

Fuentes policiales habían informado a EL PAÍS de que Lemus había sufrido problemas de salud el viernes pasado, 13 de noviembre, por los que había sido ingresado en un hospital de Valladolid. Núcleo Nacional publicó el martes un mensaje en sus redes sociales informando del fallecimiento, pero fue retirado hasta este miércoles por la mañana, cuando lo han confirmado. El grupo neonazi ha criticado, en la publicación. la intervención policial en la vivienda vallisoletana en la que fue detenido y afirma que desde entonces “se encontraba profundamente afectado por todo lo sucedido, triste y abatido al contemplar cómo el Estado y sus fuerzas de seguridad nos trataban como criminales, y cómo los medios de comunicación, recurriendo a la mentira y a la manipulación proyectaban ante la opinión pública una imagen de nuestra organización y su persona que nada tenía que ver con la realidad, haciéndonos pasar por terroristas o maníacos”.

El mensaje precisa que el viernes por la tarde Lemus quedó con “Alberto”, en alusión a Alberto González de Juan, conocido como Pugilato, “y le confesó que se encontraba realmente mal y que estaba sufriendo mucho por todo”. Fue al despedirse cuando “sufrió un infarto y se desplomó en la vía pública”. Posteriormente, fue operado por el accidente cardiovascular.

El fallecimiento de Lemus supone que Núcleo Nacional pierda a una de sus figuras más experimentadas, sobre todo en el plano ideológico y de coordinación. El comunicado de redes muestra una foto del fallecido megáfono en mano, algo recurrente en él en manifestaciones, concentraciones o las algaradas ante la sede del PSOE en Madrid, en la calle de Ferraz, a finales de 2023.

Punto de encuentro

Imagen de 2019 tomada durante una visita policial al local en Valladolid.

Uno de los locales donde se reunían los miembros de Núcleo Nacional se encontraba en la calle de Renedo número 10 de Valladolid. EL PAÍS ha accedido a expedientes policiales del Ayuntamiento de Valladolid en los que constan varias visitas policiales entre 2019 y 2020 a este espacio, donde Lemus y otros compañeros aseguraban que tenía la sede Democracia Nacional, aunque oficialmente no está inscrito en ese local. Las quejas venían por vecinos ante los ruidos y se encontraron bebidas alcohólicas. Los agentes que acudieron en una de las ocasiones incorporaron fotografías del lugar, con abundante simbología fascista, banderas con la cruz celta nazi o bustos y fotografías enmarcadas de líderes fascistas.

World.title: Government struggling to reclaim €1.2bn in assets from criminals
World.content:
The Dutch government has an outstanding bill of €1.2 billion in unclaimed proceeds of crime and compensation payments, according to figures from the agency responsible for collecting the money.

The CJIB, the justice department’s debt collection service, said it was struggling to pursue criminals for amounts they owe under court orders designed to prevent them gaining financially.

Proceeds of crime account for two-thirds of the total amount, with 2% of the criminals responsible for 50% of the unpaid debts.

They include “Bolle Jos” Leijdekkers, the drugs baron who is believed to be hiding out in Sierra Leone and is the subject of a €2 million reward for information leading to his capture. He has been ordered to pay the Dutch state a total of €96 million.

“In general these are people who don’t want to pay,” Johan Bac, managing director of the CJIB, told Nieuwsuur. “Their fortune is often concealed by all kinds of international constructions. Tracking it down is very labour-intensive.”

Last year the CJIB managed to seize just €50 million in criminal assets, but the agency warns that the backlog will grow unless it is takes on staff, increases its expertise and can get its hands on criminal assets earlier.

The remaining €500 million consists of payments to victims of a wide range of crimes, €150 million of which has been paid out by the CJIB but still has to be reclaimed.

The agency says this amount is also likely to increase under plans to widen the range of offences for which the government covers the compensation payments, to include crimes such as arson and causing traffic deaths.

World.title: Groningen university continues Dead Sea Scrolls work with Israel
World.content:
The University of Groningen (RUG) is set to continue a research collaboration into the Dead Sea Scrolls with Israeli researchers, despite protests over the provenance of the scrolls and an appeal from 18 of its own professors, broadcaster NOS reported.

The Dead Sea Scrolls are considered one of the most important archaeological finds of the past century. They are ancient Jewish manuscripts, many of them biblical, that were discovered between 1947 and 1956 in various locations in the present-day West Bank, such as the caves at Qumran.

These locations were occupied by Israel during the 1967 war, and the manuscripts were transferred from the Palestine Archaeological Museum in East Jerusalem to the Israel Museum in West Jerusalem. Critics say Palestinians no longer have access to the collection.

Origins study

In June, RUG professor Mladen Popović was awarded €2.5 million by the European Research Council for a five-year study into the origins of the scrolls. The work is being done with the Israel Antiquities Authority (IAA), the state body that holds most of the collection. The team will use chemical analysis and AI to examine samples of parchment, papyrus and ink for clues about where the manuscripts were made.

In August, local protest groups wrote an open letter asking the RUG to stop the study because of the occupation and the ongoing violence throughout Palestine. They argue that working with the IAA legitimises the occupation.

The university’s executive board responded in late August that it would continue regardless, though it recognised the humanitarian situation in the region as “heartbreaking”. It said events there were not directly linked to the research.

Professors’ appeal

In October, 18 professors asked the board to reconsider. “By working together, the RUG gives the Israeli institution recognition, legitimacy, and prestige,” said Marcel Brus, emeritus professor of international public law and one of the signatories. “Anyone who remains neutral in a situation of injustice has sided with the oppressor.”

Critics are also concerned about a proposed Israeli law that would bring archaeology in the West Bank and Gaza under Israeli law, which they fear could help Israel lay claim to land.

In a statement on November 11, the board said the project has a clear scientific aim and needs direct access to manuscripts held by the IAA. The collaboration “does not constitute endorsement of government policy”, it said, and ancient Jewish history should be studied separately from the current conflict.

World.title: Amsterdam calls for immediate medical help for crack addicts
World.content:
Amsterdam council has called on the government to allow crack addicts to be treated with medication amid a nationwide crisis that is causing serious issues in many of the Netherlands’ major cities.

City health chief Alexander Scholtes told a parliamentary hearing on Wednesday that research into long-acting dexamphetamine, an ADHD drug, should be continued after the health inspectorate IGJ halted a trial.

The IGJ paused production of the drug in September, telling Dutch News that it was “concerned about the quality of the medicine”. Mayor Femke Halsema called on the cabinet to save the trial.

Amsterdam now wants a national guideline and funding for the treatment, and in the meantime it wants a related drug, lisdexamfetamine, to be used as a stopgap treatment.

There is currently no medication-based treatment for crack cocaine addiction in the Netherlands, leaving health services with little to offer, broadcaster NOS said.

Halsema called for national action in August, saying that major cities throughout the country are buckling under the pressure of rising homelessness, addiction and related public disorder.

The Trimbos addiction institute and fieldwork organisation Mainline estimated in 2023 that almost 28,000 people in the Netherlands are high-risk crack users. The city’s public health service GGD puts the number of regular crack users in Amsterdam at 3,000 to 9,000.

If you are concerned about your own or someone else’s use of alcohol, drugs, or gambling, the Jellinek addiction helpline can be reached on 088 505 1220 or at jellinek.nl. The line is staffed in Dutch and English on weekdays, 1pm to 5pm.

World.title: Woman who held séance at cemetery cleared of desecrating graves
World.content:
Four women who took part in a séance at a cemetery in Amersfoort have been cleared of desecrating the graves of adults and children.

The women, aged between 37 and 81, organised the event five years ago to try to detect paranormal activity using illuminated cat toys.

The prosecution service had sought sentences of up to 200 hours’ community service for taking part in the séance in September 2021, but the court said there was no conclusive evidence that the women acted illegally.

“In the judgment of the court, it cannot be proved that the suspects wilfully and knowingly intended to harm the memory of those who died or their familes’ sense of piety,” the court wrote in its judgment.

The investigation began after families of children who were buried in the cemetery found photographs of the séance that one of the participants left behind.

The ensuing uproar cost the cemetery’s director his job after he gave the women permission to conduct research into the “so-called energies of the deceased” after closing time.

At least 10 relatives have reburied their loved ones after their graves were used for the ceremony, but the court said that the women had behaved respectfully.

The court acknowledged in its judgment that the case had been distressing for some relatives.

“The court has seen the families’ feelings of disgust during the hearings,” the judges commented. “The judge in a criminal case does not decide on the issue of whether a suspect’s behaviour is socially acceptable.”

.

World.title: Russian embassy responds to NL role in Crimea bridge attack
World.content:

The Russian embassy in the Netherlands has responded to the announcement made by Dutch arms company Destinus that its weapons were used to attack the Crimea bridge. “Is The Hague openly joining the conflict?” it asked on social media.

The message comes hours after Destinus posted on LinkedIn that it was proud to support the attacks in allegiance with Ukraine. An expert told broadcaster NOS that the company was likely looking for publicity, which could carry risks of cyberattacks and other retaliations from Russia.

The Crimea bridge, which was built after Russia annexed the peninsula in 2014, is a symbol of Putin’s war on Ukraine and an important supply route for its munitions in the conflict.

Destinus’ headquarters are located in Valkenburg and the company has factories throughout Europe, including in Hengelo in Overijssel.

The company’s message, the first of its kind, also showed images of the damage caused to the bridge.

The Russian embassy also wrote: “Moscow has been duly informed of the NL involvement. The confession has been well noted.”

The Dutch foreign affairs ministry has not yet commented.

World.title: Far-right parties mentioned “remigration” 96 times in two years
World.content:
Far-right parties such as Forum voor Democratie and PVV used the term “remigration” nearly 100 times in the Dutch parliament in the last two years, a dramatic escalation that followed the PVV’s success in the 2023 election.

Figures obtained by Nieuwsuur showed remigratie appeared 115 times in the parliamentary records in the last decade, 96 of them since 2024.

In 53 cases the speaker was an FVD MP, while on 19 occasions they represented the PVV. FVD MPs were also most likely to use omvolking, the Dutch word used to describe the replacement of native populations by migrants.

The intelligence service AIVD and the anti-terrorism co-ordinator (NCTV) have warned in a report earlier this year that far-right organisations and their associated political parties are trying to normalise terms such as remigratie as part of a wider strategy to bring about “the breakdown of the democratic rule of law and the foundation of a white ethno-state”.

Sarah de Lange, professor of Dutch politics at Leiden University, told Nieuwsuur: “When far-right activists and movements refer to remigration, what they actually mean is the deportation of people with a migrant background who live in the Netherlands.”

“Wrong and inappropriate”

The PVV stopped using the term omvolking in 2024 when it joined Dick Schoof’s cabinet. Marjolein Faber, who represented the party as minister for asylum, said she accepted it was “wrong and inappropriate” at her ministerial vetting hearing.

But Ralf Dekker, interim parliamentary leader for FVD, told Nieuwsuur he saw remigratie and omvolking as “normal words” and his party had “legitimate political views” about them.

“The population of today has a different make-up than 40 or 50 years ago,” he said. “You can argue about the question of how much it was brought about by deliberate policies.”

Other right-wing parties also used the term remigratie in their manifestos for the 2025 election, including JA21, whose leader Joost Eerdmans said: “We think stimulating voluntary remigration is fine, but deporting people on grounds of origin, religion or race is abhorrent and we obviously reject it.”

World.title: Netherlands has widest gender pay gap in EU despite improvements
World.content:
The Netherlands has the widest gender pay gap in the European Union, with low-paid workers and single parents particularly disadvantaged, new figures have found.

Median earnings for women were 68.8% of men’s earnings last year, while women in couples earned 65% of their partner’s salary. The gap has narrowed in the last 12 months, but both figures remain the widest in the EU.

The annual study by the European Institute for Gender Equality (EIGIE) found that the Netherlands had made progress on all measures, which also include health, political power, knowledge and how men and women spend their time.

Overall the country ranks fifth out of the 26 EU nations, performing relatively strongly on knowledge and political and economic power. The gender gap is closing faster than across the EU, but not as fast as its nearest competitors Spain, Belgium and Ireland.

Sixty percent of Dutch women have a graduate qualification, compared to an EU average of 51%, while 40% of members of parliament and 44% of board members of the largest companies are female, both above the average.

But further down the socio-economic scale the gap is wider, the report found. Women hold 30% of managerial positions, below the EU average, and account for 44% of low paid workers, a relatively high share.

Segregation in education

The researchers found that Dutch women were more likely to work in low-paid sectors such as healthcare, cleaning, and catering.

EIGE said segregation in education remained a concern, with women making up three-quarters of graduates in arts and humanities subjects but only one-third of science, technology and maths graduates.

Mara Yerkes, professor of social policy at Utrecht University, said the trend showed that women’s opportunities were still held back by stereotyped domestic roles.

“Education and healthcare are sectors where it’s often easier to work part-time and have flexible work arrangements,” she told broadcaster NOS.

“As long as women are seen as primarily responsible for children, they will tend to keep working in those sectors.”

Nearly half of mothers of children under 12 spent at least 35 hours a week on childcare, as do 26% of men. Both figures are among the highest in the EU. The report noted that parents have to wait four years after the end of well-paid parental leave for a nursery place.

World.title: Van Gogh sale goes ahead after deal with Jewish family’s heirs
World.content:
The owners of a Van Gogh painting expected to fetch around $180 million at auction in New York on Wednesday have reached a deal with the heirs of a Jewish family, who say the work was sold through an Amsterdam gallery in 1936 amid the threat of Nazi persecution.

Sotheby’s said in a statement on Tuesday that the Blaquier-Arrieta family, which has owned Châtaigniers en fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees) since 1975, had come to an agreement with all the legal descendants of the Berlin publisher Samuel Fischer and his wife Hedwig.

“In recognition of the painting’s complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution,” the auction house said. The terms have not been made public.

The US-based heirs asked Sotheby’s last week to withdraw the painting from sale. In a letter to the auction house on November 12, their lawyer asked it to prove that the work had been sold at market value and that the family would have sold it even without Nazi rule, according to the New York Times.

The heirs said the agreement made it “possible to acknowledge the suffering of the Fischer family during the Nazi era”.

Fischer, who founded the publishing house S. Fischer Verlag, bought the painting in 1909. According to Sotheby’s lot notes, it was deposited with the Paul Cassirer gallery in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933, passed to his widow Hedwig when he died in 1934, and was sold through the gallery to a Paris couple in 1936.

Sotheby’s had said its research had not shown that the painting was sold under duress.

If the painting sells at its estimate, it will break Van Gogh’s auction record of $117.2 million, set at Christie’s in 2022.

World.title: Disputed Polish constitutional court announces chief justice stripped of immunity to face charges
World.content: Why are you seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This is a breaking news story and may be updated as further information becomes available. The government-backed judges who recently took control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have announced that the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, has been stripped of legal immunity in order to face criminal charges. Święczkowski, who was appointed to the TK under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government, has condemned their takeover as an illegal “coup d’état” and says that any decisions issued by them have no validity. In a further development, the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) announced yesterday that it has rejected a request by Święczkowski for an emergency order to suspend all proceedings against him at the TK. Trybunał Konstytucyjny zdecydował. Prokuratura może teraz stawiać zarzuty. Nikt nie stoi ponad prawem.https://t.co/trIEqa8Mh1 — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 18, 2026 A statement published on Wednesday evening on the tribunal’s website announced that motions from the prosecutor general, Waldemar Żurek, to strip Swięczkowski and the deputy head of the court, Bartłomiej Sochański, of immunity had been approved. The decision was made by the group of eight judges who dramatically took control of the TK on 30 October as riot police held back protesters outside. All of them were chosen by the government’s parliamentary majority this year, but opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of them. After taking over the tribunal, they declared that Święczkowski and Sochański had been suspended for their failure to properly fulfil their duties. They also launched internal disciplinary proceedings against the pair, with hearings in those cases due to take place later this week. Separately, Żurek, who serves as justice minister in addition to being prosecutor general, filed multiple requests to the TK for Święczkowski and Sochański to be stripped of their immunity in order to face criminal charges. Most of those were approved today. Among the alleged crimes prosecutors wish to charge Święczkowski with are abuse of power and failure to fulfil duties for his refusal to allow five judges chosen by parliament this year to take up their seats on the court. Sochański is accused of the same offences. Święczkowski has argued that he cannot admit those judges because, under Polish law, they are obliged to first swear an “oath before the president” and have not done so. Prosecutors also allege that Święczkowski used violence against those five judges to physically prevent them from entering the judges’ chambers at the TK. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 Further allegations against Święczkowski relate to his time serving as national prosecutor under the former PiS government. Prosecutors say that he abused his powers by making unauthorised use of material gathered from surveillance. They also accuse him of abusing his power by “maliciously” reassigning prosecutors to different locations as a form of punishment, despite there being no legal basis for doing so. However, although the TK today approved the lifting of Święczkowski and Sochański’s immunities, it did not consent to them being arrested and held in pretrial detention. It also rejected two additional requests from Żurek to lift Święczkowski’s immunity for other alleged crimes. The TK found the motions contained “formal deficiencies”. Skierowałem do Trybunału Konstytucyjnego kolejny, szósty już wniosek o uchylenie immunitetu Bogdanowi Święczkowskiemu, dołączając go do pięciu wniosków przekazanych w piątek. Dzisiejsza sprawa dotyczy zakupu systemu szpiegowskiego Hermes w czasie, gdy pełnił funkcję Prokuratora… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 3, 2026 Święczkowski immediately rejected today’s decisions, saying that they had no legal validity. He describes the eight judges who have taken control as “usurpers”. However, on Tuesday, Święczkowski suffered another setback in his struggle to retain control over the TK after the European Court of Human Rights announced that it had rejected a request from him and Sochański for an interim measure ordering that all proceedings against them be suspended. The ECHR found that “the applicants had failed to demonstrate an imminent risk of irreparable harm to the core of their rights”. The decision stands in contrast to one made in May this year by the ECHR, when it ordered that the five judges Nawrocki has refused to swear in be admitted to the TK. Święczkowski ignored that order, arguing that the ECHR did not have the authority to issue it. European Court rejects request for interim measure in case concerning Constitutional Court of Poland. 🔗 https://t.co/I15bGXeeKF — ECHR CEDH (@ECHR_CEDH) November 17, 2026 Święczkowski has received backing from some other Polish institutions. President Nawrocki continues to recognise Święczkowski as the chief justice of the TK and has condemned the government-backed judges’ takeover of the court. The chief justice of the Supreme Court (a separate body from the TK), Zbigniew Kapiński, has also sided with Święczkowski and Nawrocki. Speaking to broadcaster RMF on Wednesday morning, Kapiński said that any decisions made by the eight judges who have taken over the TK “have no legal force”. Kapiński’s own status has also been subject to dispute. He was appointed to the Supreme Court under the PiS government through a judicial body overhauled in a manner that rendered it illegitimate, according to various European and Polish court rulings. On Monday, the central bank, whose governor is a longstanding associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński, announced that it was suspending all outgoing payments from the TK’s bank accounts due to uncertainty over who holds legitimate control over the court. Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal, citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a takeover by a group of judges backed by the government https://t.co/ZYkzoneojO — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 17, 2026 The recent dramatic events at the TK follow a decade-long crisis around the Polish judiciary, triggered by the contested judicial reforms and appointments made by the former PiS government and PiS-aligned former President Andrzej Duda. The current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk that came to power in 2023 – has refused to recognise the legitimacy of the TK due to the presence of unlawfully appointed judges. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. The eight judges it has appointed now have a majority on the 15-person court, although five of them have not been sworn in by Nawrocki. The remaining seven judges, including Święczkowski and Sochański, were appointed when PiS was in power. World.title: New Kraków mayor withdraws from metro plans and seeks to shrink clean transport zone
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The administration of Kraków’s new mayor, Łukasz Gibała, has signalled that the city will withdraw from plans to build a metro system and will seek to shrink the size of the recently introduced Clean Transport Zone, which imposes additional costs on older, more polluting cars. “We won’t, like the previous administrations, make any promises regarding the metro,” deputy mayor Karol Wałachowski told local news service LoveKrakow. “We’re withdrawing from this project until central [government] or European funding becomes available.” The draft municipal budget for next year presented by Gibała allocates no funds towards preparation work for the metro, notes LoveKrakow. Instead, the new administration wants to establish seven new tram routes. For decades, Kraków has discussed the possibility of building a metro system, which would be just the second in Poland after Warsaw’s. In 2014, 55% of residents who took part in a referendum voted in favour of the idea. However, only in 2024 did the then-mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, who came to office that year, announce plans to build a metro. The city unveiled the planned route in 2025 and then, in July this year, it launched a 188 million zloty (€43 million) tender for “pre-design” of the project. Kraków has announced a €43 million tender for pre-design work on a planned new metro system, which would be only the second in Poland. The plans include a feasibility study, environmental report and assessment of the impact on existing buildings https://t.co/mB24RcVY96 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 But the idea now looks set to be abandoned after Miszalski was dismissed in a recall referendum earlier this year and Gibała was elected last month to replace him. While Gibała has often said that he would, in theory, like Kraków to have a metro system akin to Warsaw’s, he has argued that it would be impossible to build without significant funds from the European Union or Polish government. During this year’s election campaign, Gibała told news service Wirtualna Polska that he wanted to “honestly tell Kraków residents that, regardless of whether [Monika] Piątkowska [his opponent] or I win, there won’t be a metro anytime soon. We won’t build it without government funding”. Gibała said that, if elected, he would ask the government for a written guarantee of funding. “In my opinion, they won’t [give one], and the metro issue will die. I won’t spend millions more zloty on more expert teams and analyses [to prepare for the metro].” The issue has become tied up in national politics. Gibała is an independent while Piątkowska, his defeated rival, was from Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO) party. LoveKrakow reports, based on sources, that, if Tusk loses power at next year’s parliamentary elections, a new national government may be more willing to provide funds for the metro project. In one of his first announcements since being elected, the new mayor of Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, has declared that he will withdraw official patronage of the annual LGBT+ equality march. He argues that the event has become too "partisan" https://t.co/SS2EbRy6Ob — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 This week’s announcement of withdrawal from the metro plans was criticised by one of Miszalski’s former deputy mayors, Stanisław Mazur, who told Radio Kraków that the project should have been seen as “an investment that would significantly support the development of Kraków’s economy”. Two former rectors of Kraków’s AGH University, Antoni Tajduś and Tadeusz Słomka, also told LoveKrakow that it was vital to continue with the preparatory work for the metro system because otherwise, if funding does become available, the city would not be ready to implement the project. Separately, Gibała’s new administration has also presented draft plans to reduce the size of Kraków’s Clean Transport Zone, which was introduced at the start of this year and levies additional costs on drivers of old, more polluting cars. The project has long caused controversy. It was initially meant to go into force in 2024, but was blocked by a court ruling. There have also been legal challenges to the measures finally introduced this year. Many local politicians and officials have argued that the zone unfairly burdens drivers from outside Kraków who need to enter the city, in particular people with lower incomes, who are more likely to drive older cars and are hit harder by the new costs. A court has rejected an attempt to overturn the Clean Transport Zone that was introduced at the start of this year in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, and which places restrictions on driving older, more polluting cars https://t.co/NoAKsDgUus — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 26, 2026 During his election campaign, Gibała said that he wanted to reduce the size of the Clean Transport Zone, so that it covered only the city centre rather than the whole city. He also pledged to put any final decision about the zone to a public referendum. This week, another of his deputy mayors, Jan Hoffman, confirmed that city hall had presented draft plans to reduce the size of the zone. However, he noted that any change would have to be approved by the city council and also suggested that any final decision should be made in a referendum. Those plans were criticised by Kraków Smog Alarm, an NGO that fights for cleaner air. They said that reducing the scope of the Clean Transport Zone would harm residents’ health and result in tens of millions of zloty in fees being lost to the city budget. World.title: Polish government seeks to introduce maximum gas prices for consumers
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s government has announced plans to introduce a maximum price for natural gas to protect households from the continued impact of the US and Israel’s attacks on Iran earlier this year. The measure would be funded by a new special levy on certain energy companies. To enter into force, the bill must still be approved by parliament, where the government has a majority, and signed into law by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki, who has vetoed a record amount of legislation. Speaking ahead of a cabinet meeting on Tuesday, Prime Minister Donald Tusk noted that gas prices have been at elevated levels due to the ongoing crisis around the Strait of Hormuz in the Middle East, which is normally a major conduit for both oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG). Tusk pointed out that the European gas benchmark price recently surpassed €100 per megawatt-hour (MWh), which was its highest level in four years. The figure has since fallen to around €85/MWh, though that is still more than double the level in January and February, before the US and Israel attacked Iran. Such costs are “unacceptable for any Polish family”, said the prime minister. “We can’t allow people to suffer because of decisions made abroad… about war in the Middle East. We don’t want Polish families to pay for it.” The government therefore wants to introduce a maximum price of 197.29 zloty (€44.15) per MWh (which is the level of the current state-regulated gas tariff) for the whole of 2027. The energy ministry estimates that this will save households that use gas for heating up to 1,863 zloty over the year. As well as individual households and housing cooperatives, the maximum price will also apply to entities providing important public services, such as schools, nurseries, hospitals and shelters. Companies selling gas to such consumers will then receive compensation from the state to cover the difference if the maximum price is below what the level of gas tariffs would normally be at that time. The costs of this compensation “will be largely covered by a new monthly gas levy” charged to “energy companies holding licences to trade natural gas with foreign countries and selling high-methane natural gas on the domestic market”, says the government. The levy would amount to 10% of net revenues from domestic sales of high-methane natural gas in 2027. Companies holding capacity rights amounting to less than 10% of the total capacity at entry points to Poland’s gas-transmission system would be exempt. While the legislation is unlikely to face obstacles in parliament, it remains unknown what Nawrocki’s position will be. The president has previously pushed for the government to lower energy prices. However, he also blocked a windfall tax on energy companies to subsidise fuel-price cuts, before eventually relenting. President @NawrockiKn has backed down and signed into law the government's proposed windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits, which he had previously blocked. In response, the government has reintroduced measures to lower prices at petrol stations https://t.co/icGEST8NAo — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Earlier this year, analysis by Allianz, the world’s largest insurance company, found that Poland was among a group of 11 countries “most at risk” from a prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Poland has become a growing consumer of gas in recent years. As the country has moved away from its traditional reliance on coal, gas has increasingly been used for both electricity generation and home heating. Last year, gas accounted for a record 13.2% of electricity production, up from just 2.7% in 2015. The latest figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that in 2024 almost 21% of households use gas for heating, up from 10% in 2015. Gas consumption reached its highest ever level in Poland this week – breaking a record set in 2021 – amid freezing winter temperatures and as the fuel continues to play a bigger role in the country's energy mix https://t.co/2wEWLPCV9l — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 10, 2026 The majority of gas consumed in Poland is imported – around 82% last year, according to the energy ministry. Around 43% of imports arrive in the form of LNG, delivered to a terminal at Świnoujście on Poland’s northern Baltic Sea coast. Last year, most of that LNG came from the United States (accounting for 30.7% of Poland’s total gas imports) and Qatar (11.2%). However, LNG exports from Qatar have been severely impacted by the difficulties around the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier this month, Polish state energy giant Orlen exercised its right to terminate one of its two long-term LNG contracts with QatarEnergy, citing “the ongoing force majeure”. However, Orlen insisted that the decision “does not affect the security of gas supplies”. Most of Poland’s remaining gas imports come via the Baltic Pipe, which opened in 2022 and brings gas from Norway via Denmark. World.title: Poland’s central bank freezes constitutional court’s accounts amid leadership dispute
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a disputed takeover by a group of judges backed by the government. The National Bank of Poland (NBP), which holds the tribunal’s accounts and is headed by a governor appointed under the former government, said it was not the bank’s role to determine which side was legally entitled to represent the institution. Narodowy Bank Polski wstrzymał realizację zleceń płatniczych Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. Powodem jest spór o to, kto jest uprawniony do reprezentowania TK i dysponowania środkami zgromadzonymi na jego rachunkach bankowych – poinformował NBP.https://t.co/KXwEBL6j9k pic.twitter.com/0h90bPdTLO — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) November 16, 2026 Last month, eight judges elected to the TK this year by the government’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom the opposition-aligned president, Karol Nawrocki, has refused to swear in – took control of the court. They declared that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański, both of whom were appointed to the TK under the former government, had been suspended for failing to fulfil their duties and launched disciplinary proceedings against them. Święczkowski denounced the move as an illegal “coup d’état”. He has been backed by the court’s other six judges, also appointed under the former government. A few days later, Święczkowski submitted a statement to the NBP identifying himself as the sole person authorised to manage the TK’s accounts. Later that week, after the newly elected judges held their first meeting and made several key decisions, the NBP said it had also received documents “indicating, in principle, other persons authorised to dispose of the funds held in the Constitutional Tribunal’s bank accounts”. Meanwhile, Święczkowski also issued a legal challenge against the TK takeover at the Supreme Court, which on 10 November issued a ruling revoking the order to suspend Święczkowski and Sochański. However, the validity of that ruling is disputed. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, the judge who has claimed leadership of the TK, said that only the tribunal itself can decide on the issue. Disciplinary hearings for Święczkowski and Sochański are due to begin later this week. Święczkowski, nevertheless, sent the Supreme Court ruling to the national bank as evidence that he remained the person legally entitled to manage the tribunal. The dispute around Poland's constitutional court risks entrenching a system of legal dualism in which judicial authority depends on political allegiance rather than broad constitutional consent, writes @AleksSzczerbiak https://t.co/mtgutqSTQh — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 The NBP’s governor by Adam Glapiński, who was appointed under the former Law and Justice (PiS) government and is a longtime associate of PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński. On Monday, the NBP announced that it would suspend all payment orders relating to funds held in the TK’s accounts, citing “a set of documents, which mutually cancel each other out”. “This means that payment orders are not executed, regardless of who initiates them,” the NBP said in a statement. “The National Bank of Poland has no authority to decide who is legally entitled to control the Constitutional Tribunal.” Finance minister Andrzej Domański criticised the decision, accusing the central bank of becoming embroiled in the political dispute. “The National Bank of Poland should safeguard its independence, including its political independence,” Domański said. He added that the government would “explore all available options” to secure funding for the TK and ensure that it can continue functioning. Justice minister Waldemar Żurek also condemned the NBP’s move, saying its “invocation of a non-existent document [the disputed Supreme Court ruling] to block funding for a constitutional body is…an attempt to protect an entrenched system”. Święczkowski expressed satisfaction that the NBP had denied access to the “usurpers” trying to take over the court but argued that he, as the legitimate chief justice, should be given control over the accounts, reports news website Onet. Prezes Narodowego Banku Polskiego próbuje paraliżować Trybunał Konstytucyjny, powołując się na rzekome orzeczenie Sądu Najwyższego z 10.11.2026 r.. Problem w tym, że ten papier wygląda jak wydany z pieczątką z ziemniaka, a w obiegu są już jego trzy różne wersje. Najpierw Bogdan… pic.twitter.com/7rWELZFIF0 — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 16, 2026 Recent events follow a decade-long crisis surrounding the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative PiS government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. However, Nawrocki has refused to accept the oath of most of those judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. World.title: Kraków church holds mass for perpetrator of deadly attack just metres from where he shot victims
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The historic St Mary’s Basilica in Kraków has hosted a holy mass for Michał Oksiński, the man who carried out the recent attack in the city and later died of injuries sustained in a shootout with police. The six people who died in the attack and more than a dozen who were injured were shot by Oksiński on the square where the church stands, some of them just a few metres from its doors. St Mary’s Basilica says that the mass is “an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime”. On the afternoon of 7 November, Oksiński launched his attack on Kraków’s famous market square, which was packed with locals and tourists. He shot at random from his car while driving through the square and surrounding streets before police managed to bring his rampage to an end. Later that same day, the dead bodies of Oksiński’s parents and sister were found in his home. They had each been shot in the head while sleeping. Two days after the attack, Oksiński himself died in hospital. On Sunday, Łukasz Wantuch, a former city councillor, shared a photograph of an announcement that there would be “a holy mass for the late Michał Oksiński and the deceased members of his family” at the Roman Catholic St Mary’s Basilica on Monday morning. The church, built in the 14th century, is one of the most famous in Poland and dominates the skyline in Kraków’s historic, UNESCO-listed city centre. It stands on one corner of the market square, just a few steps from where some of Oksiński’s victims were shot. “I won’t hide the fact that I find this somewhat shocking,” wrote Wantuch. He noted that the announcement referred to the “blessed memory” (świętej pamięci) of Oksiński. However, that phrase is standard usage in Polish to refer to someone who has died (the equivalent ot the English “late”). “But perhaps that is what faith is about: praying even for a murderer,” added Wantuch. Among the more than 1,000 comments under his Facebook post, many agreed with that sentiment. “The whole of Christianity is based on forgiving the unforgivable,” wrote one. “I don’t think anyone needs God’s mercy more [than Oksiński],” said another. However, some others were critical of the fact that the mass was being held in that particular church among the dozens in Kraków. “It is the height of impudence that they’ll celebrate mass for him in the very church he murdered in front of,” wrote one commenter. Later on Sunday, St Mary’s Basilica issued a statement, signed by parish administrator Father Mariusz Słonina, saying that the holy mass “is a private initiative of one of the priests, not of St Mary’s Parish”. However, Słonina added that “praying for the deceased is an expression of the Christian faith in God’s mercy” and “in no way indicates justification for the crime, a lessening of the perpetrator’s responsibility, or a trivialisation of the suffering of the victims”. Local news service KR24 reported that uniformed police officers were posted outside the church for today’s mass while plainclothes officers were inside, with one of them right next to the altar. Three priests were present, including Słonina, who presided over the mass. Only around a dozen faithful were in attendance, with KR24 suggesting that many did not even seem aware for whom mass was being held. Separate private funeral ceremonies will take place for Oksiński, his parents and sister, who lived in the town of Ostrowiec Świętokrzyski, about 160 km from Krakow. On Sunday, their family issued a statement asking the media to “respect the privacy, dignity and mourning of our family and loved ones”. Meanwhile, police and prosecutors continue to investigate the possible motive behind Oksiński’s attack, which they are treating as a terrorist offence. Last week, the justice minister said that there were “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the perpetrator’s online activity. Two police officers, Jakub Kulik and Artur Morański, who were seriously injured in the shootout that debilitated Okisński, have been recovering in hospital after undergoing emergency surgery. World.title: Poland detains neo-Nazi teens accused of terrorist plot
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has detained and charged three teenagers who are allegedly linked to “an international neo-Nazi network” and had been planning terrorist attacks, including with the use of homemade explosives. The arrests were announced on Monday morning by Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, who revealed that the suspects are Polish citizens. Two are aged 17 and one is 16. “The teenagers not only promoted Nazi and fascist ideology but had also already taken steps toward committing terrorist offences,” wrote Siemoniak. Funkcjonariusze @ABW_GOV_PL zatrzymali 3 obywateli RP, 16-latka i dwóch 17-latków, związanych z międzynarodowym środowiskiem neonazistowskim. ▶️ Nastolatkowie nie tylko propagowali ideologię nazistowską i faszystowską, ale podejmowali już działania zmierzające do popełniania… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) November 16, 2026 The National Prosecutor’s Office revealed that the trio were “fascinated by the activities of an international neo-Nazi terrorist organisation…[that] has an ideology based on hatred against people of Jewish descent, immigrants, black people, the LGBT community, politicians and state security officials”. Though prosecutors did not name the organisation, they said that members of it have been involved in planning terrorist attacks in the United States, Germany and the United Kingdom. In some countries, including the UK, Canada and Australia, it has been outlawed and designated a terrorist group. Poland’s Internal Security Agency (ABW) had found that the three suspects’ online communication indicated “an interest in constructing explosive devices, modifying weapons and using such items to carry out terrorist activities”. During a search of the home of one of the 17-year-olds (named only as “suspect 1”), officers found chemicals that are precursors for the production of explosives. That suspect has also been charged with possession of a so-called pipe bomb, which prosecutors say he wanted to “transfer to a neo-Nazi terrorist group”. Suspect 1 was found to have discussed with the other 17-year-old, named as suspect 2, how to construct an explosive device and detonate it in a specific residential building where someone they knew lived. Suspect 1 had also “incited extremist behaviour and hate-motivated violence” in his online activity, while the 16-year-old, named as suspect 3, had “promoted fascist content” (a crime in Poland) and encouraged someone to assault another person based on their race. Each suspect has been charged with three crimes, relating variously to terrorist offences, possession or attempted production of explosives and weapons, promoting Nazism, fascism and racial hatred, and inciting others to commit violence based on racial differences. Prosecutors note that Polish law generally allows people to face full criminal liability from the age of 17. The two 17-year-olds have therefore been placed in adult pretrial detention, while the 16-year-old is being held in a juvenile facility. Śledztwo w sprawie neonazistów i planowanych aktów terroru kryminalnego Szczegóły w komunikacie: ⬇️https://t.co/dQpdgiTYJD — Prokuratura Regionalna w Gdańsku (@Prok_Regio_GDA) November 16, 2026 The arrests come in the context of recent concerns over radicalisation of young people in Poland. Earlier this month, a 24-year-old carried out a terrorist attack in the city of Kraków, killing six people by firing a rifle from his car. He had earlier killed his parents and sister in their home. In the aftermath of the attack, justice minister Waldemar Żurek revealed that investigators had found “very strong traces of right-wing extremism” in the attacker’s online activity, though he emphasised that the motive was yet to be determined. In the space of a few days last month, three knife attacks took place in Polish schools, resulting in one case in the death of a member of staff. Dozens of young people were arrested in the aftermath for making threats and/or possessing weapons. In September, the security services detained three teenagers accused of being part of online groups promoting neo-Nazism and violence. One of them has been charged with planning terrorist attacks on targets including a mosque and a school.
