World.title: Three Months After the Omiš Fire – Still No Real Answers
World.content:
November the 18th, 2026 – Over three months have now passed since the devastating Omiš fire, yet the public and more importantly those directly affected are still waiting for actual answers.

The catastrophic fire that engulfed the Omiš area on the night of August the 13th to the 14th remains fresh in most people’s minds, particularly for those who were near it. Index reports that six people lost their lives as a result of that specific fire, homes were destroyed, and residents fled directly into the sea to escape the flames. Survivors described the dramatic moments, escaping from blocked roads, and boat rescues for HTV. Three months after the tragedy, they are still seeking answers regarding accountability, the warning system, and reconstruction aid.

fleeing from the flames

For the residents of Omiš and surrounding towns, the night of the fire began with the flames rapidly spreading toward their houses. Goran Lović from Lokva Rogoznica recounted how his wife called him to return urgently because the fire had already caught their building. When he arrived, the fire had spread so much that they could no longer reach their other house, about three hundred meters away, where a minor child was located.

Dubravka Marunčić from Stanići was putting her children to bed when her daughter noticed that the tree in front of the house was red. When she turned around, she realized the fire had already reached them and decided to leave immediately with the children. Gabrijela Baučić from Borak also tried to escape by car with her family, but traffic had almost come to a standstill. “My younger one, David, when he saw the flames in the rearview mirror, turned around and saw it coming close to us. ‘Mum, drive faster, we’re going to burn!’ And you’re just standing still. It’s horrendous.”

Julija Hrstić tried to protect her house by hosing it down with water, but when they lost electricity and water, the family decided to leave. They grabbed their dog and put him in the car, but soon got stuck in a line of vehicles that was barely moving.

clogged roads and an escape into the sea

Marunčić described how cars drove between flames while the wind carried embers. “It was burning on both the upper and lower sides of the road. A rain of embers was falling and it was horribly hot,” she said. When she saw that cars were also burning and people were fleeing from them, she turned toward the sea. There, she got out of the vehicle with her three children and ran toward the shore, where many people were already in the shallows. “We couldn’t breathe. Thick black smoke came down, embers were falling around us,” she recalled.

She also recounted how a young man approached them in the sea and began splashing them with seawater to protect them from the heat. “Just by him being close to me, I felt safe. I calmed down because I knew I could count on him,” she recalled. Soon, boats arrived and began transporting people to safety.

“we could hear people screaming”

Among the people who set out in their boats to help with the rescue was Mario Popovac from Omiš. With a friend, he sailed toward the endangered areas despite extremely poor visibility due to smoke. “We heard screams. We simply drove the boat right in among the people. At 200 or 300 metres from the shore, we couldn’t stand the heat,” he described. They found the first people about three hundred metres from the shore. Popovac says the smoke was so thick he couldn’t even see the bow of his own boat. During one trip, his friend warned him to stop, and in the sea they spotted an elderly man keeping himself afloat by holding onto two empty fuel cans.

“We came across him by chance. It is fortunate, in my opinion, that citizens spontaneously went out to sea,” he said. The evacuation lasted until roughly 04:30 in the morning. Marunčić also mentioned Milan Balić, who came by boat to pick up people on the shore of Mala Luka and, according to her, refused to leave until he had boarded everyone who needed help.

three months since absolute tragedy…

Six people lost their lives in the fire. Among the deceased were two female workers from the same hotel, a retired fire commander, and three members of the same family. Julija Hrstić admits that she is still overwhelmed by emotion today. “A life that is lost cannot be brought back. Neither life nor health for the people who will suffer consequences. When I think about it today, I often feel like crying,” she said. Even three months after the tragedy, residents are raising questions about how the warning system functioned. Baučić claims they did not receive timely evacuation instructions. “No siren sounded, we received no instructions. It was chaos. Nobody knew where to go or what to do,” she said.

Julija Hrstić also wonders why the SRUUK early warning system was not activated. “Could there have been a reaction to alert people? Better a false alarm than for this to happen,” she stated. Residents also pointed out neglected firebreaks and the unavailability of water. Goran Lović claims there were not enough hydrants.

left with no answers

The danger did not end when the fire was extinguished, because landslides are now threatening the area. Baučić, whose apartment burned down, described how her family lost everything in a single night. “In one night, you simply lose everything you’ve built for years. Without a home, a family nest,” she said. She warns about rocks that began falling after the fire and the danger of larger landslides due to destroyed vegetation. Goran Lović warns of the same issue, believing that urgent coastal remediation and state aid are needed because the local community lacks sufficient funds. He also adds that residents estimate the total damage to be higher than the amount mentioned by the government.

Three months after the tragedy, residents are still waiting for answers about the causes of the fire and possible accountability. “There is no information whatsoever about the investigation, accountability, and handling of the situation. We want something to be set in motion so that Omiš never happens to anyone again,” said Julija Hrstić. Lović also demands that authorities explain what happened. “We just want to know what happened, why people lost their lives, why our property is gone,” he stated. He emphasizes that residents feel forgotten and expect concrete help.

World.title: Vukovar Procession to Carry the Names of the Missing
World.content:
November the 18th, 2026 – The Vukovar procession will have thousands of people wearing the names of those still categorised as missing on their clothing.

Today marks the 35th anniversary of the fall of Vukovar, one of the defining moments of the Homeland War and the place of the type of massacre unseen since WWII. Index reports that in this year’s Column of Remembrance, thousands of young people will participate wearing T-shirts with the names of missing persons. This is part of the “Instead of Them” (Umjesto njih) initiative, organised for the third consecutive year by the Student Catholic Centre (SKAC) from Osijek. As part of the project, an application was also designed to permanently preserve the memories and personal stories of the people in whose name the youth will walk the streets of Vukovar.

a tribute to those still missing – all 1,725 of them

In this way, young people want to pay tribute to the 1,725 people who are still being searched for. Their message is that the memory of fallen, missing, and suffering Croatian defenders and civilians must be preserved. Many of the participants will set out on foot from Osijek toward Vukovar during the night.

“It’s a big responsibility and a very honourable role to be able to wear the name of someone who gave their life for the homeland,” said Ana Pešikan, a member of Osijek’s SKAC. Vlatka Ivančičević, head of the SKAC office, shared what motivated her to participate. “When I looked from the side and saw the faces of people searching for the name of one of their own on a T-shirt, in that moment it became very real to me,” she said.

passing on the truth about the war

Although many of those planning to march wearing the names of Vukovar’s missing were not even born during the Homeland War, today they want to pass on the truth about the events of that time. “This year on our T-shirts we’re wearing the names of missing defenders, and by wearing white T-shirts with a universal message we will pay tribute to all civilians from the Homeland War,” explained Domagoj Galić, coordinator of the “Instead of Them” initiative.

So that participants can learn more about the people whose names they wear, the organizers are recording their life stories in a special web application. “We’re aware of how grateful we should be to those people who made it possible for us to live today in a free Croatia and enjoy freedom. This is the least we can do to show them respect and gratitude,” said Ivan Galić from the organising team.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: Iraq aims to raise non-oil revenues to 19% in 2027 budget
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s draft 2027 federal budget aims to raise non-oil revenues to at least 19 percent of total government revenues, marking the highest proportion in the country’s history.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi government, Haider al-Aboudi, announced the target on Tuesday, noting that non-oil income had never exceeded 11 percent before 2026.

According to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the government plans to achieve this increase and insulate the economy from oil shocks through several structural changes.

Authorities are automating customs procedures at border crossings, digitizing government operations, and strengthening tax collection.

The plan relies on tightening financial oversight to cut off sources of corruption and revenue leakage.

The bill introduces elements of program and performance-based budgeting, tying public spending to measurable goals rather than strictly to payroll and operational categories.

While the ministries of finance and planning have completed the draft, the bill has not yet been formally published or approved by the Iraqi cabinet.

The Iraqi government aims to spend 217 trillion Iraqi dinars (around $166 billion) in 2027, assuming an oil price of $58 per barrel, according to parliamentarians familiar with the draft budget.

The measures would result in a fiscal deficit of around 40 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $30.6 billion).

Members of the parliamentary finance committee told Reuters that the draft budget anticipates crude oil exports of around four million barrels per day, including shipments from Iraqi Kurdistan.

Oil exports generate the majority of the Iraqi government’s revenue, accounting for roughly 80 percent of the general budget’s resources.

The 2027 budget represents a structural transformation by allocating 150 trillion ($114.5 billion) for traditional line items and 50 trillion Iraqi dinar ($38.2 billion) for a new World Bank-coordinated program-and-performance model to measure expenditure efficiency.

World.title: Baghdad Court sentences six more French ISIS members to life in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Al-Karkh Criminal Court in Baghdad sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, for membership in the Islamic State (ISIS) terrorist organization, raising the total number of French citizens convicted in the ongoing mass transfer case to 16.

According to a statement from the Supreme Judicial Council’s Media Center, the verdicts were pronounced in the presence of the defendants’ legal counsel and diplomatic representatives from the French Embassy in Baghdad.

The court issued the rulings under Article 4 (Paragraph 1)—read in conjunction with Article 2 (Paragraphs 1 and 3)—of Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law No.13 of 2005, applying discretionary sentence mitigation pursuant to Article 132 (Paragraph 1) of the Iraqi Penal Code to commute potential capital punishments to life sentences (equivalent to 20 years under Iraqi statutory law, subject to automatic Court of Cassation review).

The six convicts belong to a group of 47 French detainees transferred into Iraqi custody from detention facilities in northeastern Syria.

Initial inquiries were conducted by the First Al-Karkh Investigation Court with evidentiary and archival verification provided by the National Center for International Judicial Cooperation, before referring the suspects for trial.

Judicial proceedings for the group began on September 20, 2026, under tight security and without media access.

Today’s rulings mark the third wave of convictions handed down by the Al-Karkh Criminal Court in this case: on October 27, 2026, the court sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment and a seventh defendant to 15 years in prison;two days later, on October 29, it issued life sentences to three additional French suspects, bringing the cumulative tally to 16 convicted individuals following Wednesday’s verdicts.

World.title: Fourth Arab SME Summit opens in Baghdad as CBI reveals 16.3 trillion dinar financing milestone
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) The fourth edition of the Arab Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Summit kicked off at the Baghdad International Fairground on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, running through November 20 under the patronage of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi and co-organized by Iraq’s Ministry of Planning and the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia (ESCWA).

Participating as a strategic partner and sponsor, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) established a dedicated pavilion within the summit’s accompanying exhibition alongside commercial banks, corporations, and economic institutions.

Through informational publications and technical briefings, the CBI pavilion highlighted the banking sector’s role in executing national development financing initiatives and walked attendees through the application procedures for accessing SME loans—which carry a financing ceiling of 20 million Iraqi dinars per project through participating banks.

During the exhibition, the Central Bank unveiled updated cumulative figures detailing the scope of its developmental lending programs since their inception in 2015 through the end of October 2026.

Over that 11-year span, total CBI-backed financing reached 16.3 trillion Iraqi dinars, supporting the launch and expansion of more than 10,000 projects across Iraq’s private sector.

World.title: Iran-backed militia torture Iraqi environmentalist who refuses to abandon marshes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Jassim al-Asadi, an Iraqi environmentalist, has returned to safeguarding the country’s southern marshlands after being kidnaped and tortured by an Iran-backed militia in 2023, according to a November 18 article by NPR correspondent Jane Arraf.

Al-Asadi, 69, co-founded the environmental organization Nature Iraq in 2004 and has spent decades fighting to restore the marshes, which were mainly drained under Saddam Hussein and were designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2016.

Nature Iraq is an Iraqi-registered non-governmental organization accredited to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and also Iraq’s first and only affiliate of BirdLife International, an international conservation partnership.

Speaking with NPR, al-Asadi reported that armed men kidnapped him while he was traveling from Baghdad to his village of Chibayish in February 2023.

His captors accused him of spying for Israel and using his environmental expertise to aid foreign intelligence activities.

He said he was kept for two weeks, assaulted, shocked, and brutally suffocated during questioning.

When he was asked to confess or face death, he refused and instead composed a goodbye letter to his family.

According to NPR, al-Asadi was finally released due to pressure from his Bani Asad tribe, who mobilized hundreds of armed tribesmen to demand his liberation.

He denied an offer of refuge in Europe, preferring to stay in Iraq and continue his environmental efforts.

His homecoming comes as Iraq’s marshlands begin to recover after five years of severe drought.

Recent rains have boosted water levels, enabling some displaced buffalo herders to return, but pollution, water scarcity, and diminishing fish populations remain major concerns.

Despite threats against him, Al-Asadi continues to monitor water levels, help local people, and lobby for improved environmental protection.

The NPR investigation also highlighted the dangers confronting Iraqi environmental activists, especially those working with foreign organizations in regions where Iran-backed armed groups hold significant power.

Despite his suffering, al-Asadi remains determined to preserve the marshlands and its centuries-old way of life.

Nature Iraq organization focuses on conserving and rehabilitating Iraq’s ecosystems while safeguarding the cultural traditions and heritage connected to them.

World.title: CBI rules out dropping zeros from Iraqi dinar and favors banknote redesign
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) Spokesperson Mahmoud Dagher announced on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, that dropping zeros from the Iraqi dinar requires formal parliamentary legislation to overhaul financial transactions alongside large-scale currency printing, stating that under current economic conditions, the central bank views redesigning the physical appearance of banknotes as the most practical option.

Speaking during a televised interview with journalist Lana Al-Zahawi on Al-Nahrain TV, Dagher explained that redenominating the currency goes far beyond issuing replacement banknotes.

While passing enabling legislation through the Council of Representatives is legally feasible, he emphasized that re-indexing financial obligations, corporate shares, and market valuations introduces complex structural adjustments.

Citing the Iraq Stock Exchange as a practical example, Dagher questioned how shares currently priced at a nominal value of 1 dinar would be recalibrated without a comprehensive legal and accounting framework governing equity stakes and financial contracts.

Highlighting the industrial scale required for any currency overhaul, Dagher noted that replacing 10 million circulating banknotes requires printing an equal volume of new notes—a process contracted to premier international security printers such as “Theron,” which he ranked among the top four currency printing houses globally.

He underscored that banknote production is a specialized technical operation rather than a routine commodity order.

Instead of pursuing currency redenomination at this stage, the CBI favors updating the physical design and security features of existing denominations without altering their nominal face value or purchasing power.

According to Dagher, refreshing the banknote series delivers immediate economic and security advantages: it strengthens anti-counterfeiting protections, extends the physical lifespan of circulating notes, and incentivizes the return of hoarded cash back into the formal banking system.

World.title: Major KFC franchisee files for bankruptcy protection, may shut more outlets
World.content:
A major KFC franchisee in the US has filed for bankruptcy protection, citing rising costs and declining sales, after shutting dozens of restaurants this year. The company has warned that more outlets could close as it seeks to restructure its operations and exit additional leases.

Tasty Chickân LLC, which operates 75 KFC outlets and nine restaurants co-branded with Taco Bell across 10 US states, including Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, filed for bankruptcy on Monday. Court documents show that it owes about $16 million in unpaid royalties to Yum Brands Inc, KFCâs parent company.

The franchisee said it sought Chapter 11 protection to prevent Yum from immediately terminating its franchise agreement.



It has shut 44 locations since the beginning of 2026 and plans to use the bankruptcy process to exit more leases, according to court filings, Bloomberg reported.

Chapter 11 is a form of bankruptcy in the United States that allows a struggling business, or, less commonly, an individual, to reorganise its debts and operations while continuing to stay open and operate

In a Tuesday filing, a Yum affiliate said it had been working with Tasty Chickân for several months.





However, it alleged that the franchiseeâs sudden restaurant closures had significantly damaged the KFC brand, leaving it absent from some markets and weakening its presence and consumer confidence in those communities.

Tasty Chickân is at least the third major restaurant franchisee to seek bankruptcy protection in recent weeks. An operator of Outback Steakhouse restaurants filed for Chapter 11 earlier this month, also citing rising costs.

World.title: Health of states: Bihar per capita spend lowest, Sikkim's highest
World.content:
Poorer northern states spend less than half of what Northeast spends per person

Expenditure sheet

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There are wide regional disparities on what govt spends on healthcare. Govt health expenditure per person in the four poorer northern states - Bihar, UP, MP and Jharkhand - averages around Rs 1,651, less than half the Rs 3,501 recorded in the northeastern states and nearly a fourth of the Rs 7,209 average for UTs, according to the National Health Accounts (NHA) Estimates for 2023-24.At the national level, govt health expenditure stood at Rs 4.1 lakh crore in 2023-24, translating into Rs 2,959 per person. It accounted for 43.5% of total health expenditure and 1.43% of GDP.Southern states recorded a population-weighted average govt health spending of around Rs 2,960 per person, almost matching the national average of Rs 2,959. Kerala and Andhra Pradesh were above this level at Rs 3,396 and Rs 3,347, respectively, while Telangana spent Rs 3,125. Tamil Nadu's per capita spending stood at Rs 2,860 and Karnataka's at Rs 2,446, showing considerable variation even within the region."The differences and disparities in per capita govt health expenditure reflect differences in states' fiscal capacity, population size, historical investment in healthcare infrastructure and political priorities. Economically weaker, populous states face greater resource constraints and higher investment by govts, while northeastern states incur higher service delivery costs and higher per capita investment due to difficult terrain and dispersed populations," health policy specialist Dr Chandrakant Lahariya said."We need to remember some of the fixed costs such as capital investment, infrastructure cost remain relatively high even if people using those services are limited."The disparity is particularly stark in Bihar and UP, where govt health spending was Rs 1,126 and Rs 1,399 per person, respectively. In comparison, Sikkim spent Rs 16,026 per person, the highest among states, while Chandigarh led among UTs at Rs 24,187. The population-weighted average for the four poorer states worked out to Rs 1,651.The eight NE states show considerable variation. While Assam spends Rs 2,282 per person and Tripura Rs 3,360, spending is substantially higher in Sikkim (Rs 16,026), Mizoram (Rs 9,320), Arunachal (Rs 8,885) and Meghalaya (Rs 7,533). Manipur and Nagaland reported per capita spending of Rs 5,507 and Rs 4,585, respectively. The population-weighted regional average works out to around Rs 3,501.Among UTs, Puducherry spent Rs 11,165, Lakshadweep Rs 9,643, Andaman and Nicobar Islands at Rs 8,947 and Delhi at Rs 8,611. J&K reported Rs 3,339, while Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu recorded Rs 2,293. The population-weighted average across the seven UTs covered in the report was around Rs 7,209.The figures underline substantial geographical differences in public health financing, although per capita spending alone does not measure the quality, accessibility or outcomes of services.

World.title: 'If oppn stops participating, Indian democracy would end': Rahul Gandhi in US rules out poll boycott
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader

on Wednesday said the opposition was ânot ready to accept a non-democratic Indiaâ. He said opposition parties would continue to contest elections and expose alleged electoral irregularities, arguing that boycotting polls would undermine the legitimacy of the electoral process.

Speaking at an event titled âThe Iran War & India's Role in the Worldâ at the University of Chicago in Illinois, Rahul expressed confidence that the alleged discrepancies in the electoral system would eventually come to light.

âWhat happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't contest elections'? If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that very minute. And we do not want to end the structure of Indian democracy,â Lok Sabha leader of opposition said.



He said the opposition's strategy was to bring alleged irregularities to light and take the issue to the people rather than abandon elections.

âOur strategy is to expose what is going on and take the meeting...until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished. But we do not want to break the electoral structure. Because once the opposition says that we are not going to fight elections, in the minds of the Indian people, that process becomes illegitimate.





We do not want that. We are purposely not taking that step and we are confident,â Rahul said.

He also made a big claim that the opposition was receiving information from within the

and suggested that the alleged irregularities would eventually lead to changes within the institution.

"The Election Commission itself is now giving us information from inside. So it is only a question of time before that structure collapses.

Senior people in the Election Commission are now saying, 'Look, we cannot do this anymore.' So it has been a long journey," the Raebareli MP added.

Asserting that the opposition would not accept âa non-democratic Indiaâ, Rahul said the parties were fighting to restore people's ability to express themselves without fear.

âWe are fighting that battle, and I am quite happy to say that we are winning that battle. It is only a question of time before those structures begin to give way. We are not ready to accept a non-democratic India. And it is not just the

. It is the vast majority of Indians. We are going to ensure that our biggest strength, the ability of our people to express themselves without fear, is revived once again and remains our biggest strength,â Rahul said.

Rahul questions 2024 poll legitimacy

The Congress leader also questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 general elections, citing the example of a Brazilian woman who, he claimed, had never visited India but voted 23 times in a state assembly election.

"If the voters were illegitimate in the 2024 election, if they did not exist, were fake voters or should not have voted, then how is that election legal? I will tell you again that a Brazilian woman who has never visited India voted 23 times in a state election in India," Rahul said.

He further claimed that the Congress had suspected irregularities in the electoral process as far back as the 2014 general elections, pointing to what he described as politically inexplicable margins.

"Even in the 2014 election, we already believed that there was something wrong because the margins were just unexplainable politically," he said.

Rahul said that even after obtaining what he considered proof of irregularities and presenting it to senior Congress leaders, they had advised him against making the allegations publicly.

"Even when I got the proof and demonstrated it to our political leaders in the Congress party, they said to me, 'Please don't say this.' For us, Indian democracy is sacred. For me, even to say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200 or 300 per cent proof," he said.

Rahul's 'economic disaster' remark in New York

A day before his Chicago interaction, Rahul, while addressing students and faculty members at Columbia University in New York, described India as being on the brink of an economic crisis, citing unemployment and problems in the education system.

"The blunt thing is that India is sitting on an economic disaster. That's the reality. One can brush it aside, the media can brush it aside, but India's got a massive unemployment problem. India's got a massive problem with its education system," former Congress chief said, as quoted by news agency ANI.

BJP fires back at Rahul

His remarks drew a sharp response from the BJP, which accused the Congress leader of attacking India's image abroad and described him as a "leader of anti-India propaganda".

BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari took to X and criticised Rahul's comments at Columbia University.

World.title: CJI averts 'potential religious row', pulls cases from SC judge
World.content:
NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant's decision to withdraw two cases from the bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, which had expanded individual incidents of lapses on the part of authorities into pan-India judicial drives against similar illegalities, averted a potential religious controversy.

The bench's Aug 4 order directing all states and UTs to remove stray animals from public places created a controversy as it is known that the majority of strays comprise cows and calves. A UP resident filed an application before the bench apprehending that the order was "capable of being implemented in a manner that may result in cows and their progeny being rounded up, transported or disposed of without regard to the special constitutional protection they are entitled to".



Also Read|

'Wasn't permissible for that particular bench to create PIL jurisdiction'

The applicant said, "Cows have been worshipped and revered in Indian society since ancient times as 'gaumata', and religious sentiments of the public..., particularly the Hindu community, are gravely hurt whenever cows are slaughtered or otherwise ill-treated."

He said a blanket order for the removal of strays by SC ran "the real risk of stray cattle being pushed across state borders, herded into inadequate holding pounds, or otherwise subjected to conditions violative of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960...





instead of being rehabilitated through properly funded and regulated gaushalas".

The CJI's decision to withdraw the cases, backed by the four most senior SC judges, was taken after they felt it was impermissible for a bench, not assigned the PIL roster, to create PIL jurisdiction for itself by expanding individual cases into pan-India exercises in violation of case-distribution discipline, which falls in the CJI's domain.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

SC sources said the CJI informed the senior judges there would be a general survey of cases before other benches to identify matters where the ambit had been expanded to give these a pan-India texture by converting them into PILs. A decision on allocation to appropriate benches would be taken after that, they said.

One such case - Loganathan vs State of Tamil Nadu - started from the illegal construction of a ground plus one floor without a sanction plan and the failure of authorities to even notice it. The bench led by Justice Amanullah on March 25 said, "It is evident there are apparent widespread and blatant violations of building bylaws and land-use regulations. In view of the above, we deem it appropriate to examine the issue on a pan-India basis.

" It impleaded municipal corporations and municipalities of capital cities of all states and UTs.

World.title: US court to Delhi courts: Help serve summons to R&AW ex-chief, Doval
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A US district court has ordered alternative delivery of summons through Indian courts on NSA

and former Research and Analysis Wing chief Samant Goel. However, sources said the summons was not binding.

The Clerk of the US Court has been directed to send the necessary judicial documents via international mail or courier to three district courts in Delhi - Patiala House, Dwarka and Tis Hazari district courts.

The order was issued by Judge Katherine Polk Failla of the court of Southern District of New York in a civil lawsuit filed by Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, founder of pro-Khalistan outfit Sikhs for Justice (SFJ).

US court move a 'procedural, routine' step

âThe court respectfully requests the assistance of receiving Indian courts in effecting service of process upon the defendants in this civil action pending before this court,â says an order by a US district court, seeking to serve summons on Ajit Doval and Samant Goel.



The order states that standard service through India's central authority under the Hague Convention was attempted but rejected. The court then authorised alternative service under Article 19 of the Hague Convention and India's Code of Civil Procedure.

World.title: Heritage walk at Bengaluru’s Someshwara temple celebrates local history
World.content:
“This temple is literally the entrance to Bengaluru,” announces public archaeologist Lathashree KS, pointing to the Someshwara Swamy Temple in Ulsoor, where we have gathered on a pleasant Saturday morning. Over the chants wafting from the temple, which is adorned with a sky-grazing Vijayanagara-style gopuram, she explains why the area is important: “The highway to Kolar and Chintamani is here, and traders coming from there to go to the city market beyond have to pass through here. This is the first area you enter when you come to the city after trading with your ox carts and camels,” she says.

It wasn’t just traders and their animals who stopped here to rest after an arduous journey, says Lathashree, who founded Chai with History, an informal archaeology and history group in Bengaluru, in 2013. “It is not surprising that the Madras Sappers came and set up a cantonment here,” she elaborates as we begin our heritage walk through the centuries-old temple.

Over the next couple of hours, we traverse the temple’s impressive open mantapa with its carved pillars and its beautiful sculpted panels, peaceful inner sanctum and surrounding shrines, learning about its mythologies and histories along the way.

For instance, a sculpture of a Shuka Bhashini, a lady conversing with a parrot, bears a tiny signature of the sculptor: a little squirrel. “He didn’t have to do that, but we can see how the artist observed nature, although he was carving for a temple, under strictures,” she says. Other interesting learnings include how Lord Cornwallis, who led the British troops in the final Anglo-Mysorean War, camped here with them; why the oldest part of the temple lies at its very centre; how the interconnectedness of nature and human beings, apparent in some of the sculptures, is a crucial aspect of Shavisim; and that the entire temple was built out of local granite. “It is a people’s temple,” says Lathashree.

The walk through this people’s temple, one of the two events regularly conducted as part of a recent collaboration with Yellow Veranda Experiences — the other is a Brahmi script workshop, ending with a Mauryan meal — is the latest offering of Chai with History, which has evolved considerably since its genesis 13 years ago.

“It started randomly,” says Lathashree, pointing out that since she holds an MA in archaeology and indology from Deccan College, Pune, people started reaching out to her on Facebook with questions. “I started providing information,” she says. Soon, a member of a Facebook group suggested meeting regularly to discuss history. “I agreed to meet up once every month.”

A motley bunch of people began meeting every month, congregating around the benches at the Government Museum on Kasturba Road. “We made it our adda. And a small canteen made better tea than coffee, so we called it Chai with History,” she recalls.

Gradually, generic history conversations became more specific, focusing on a variety of topics, including the Mauryan Dynasty, epigraphy, how to read sculptures, the Jataka Tales and stratigraphy. Even during the pandemic, Chai with History continued in an online format, with sessions continuing until 2023, when Lathashree took a step back for personal reasons, she says.

Earlier this year, however, she restarted it, with Chai with History now conducted in four major formats: Shared Space, for discussions about the history behind a particular hobby such as pottery, philately or poetry; Cosy Conversations, for curated conversations with a small group; Idea Lounge, for interaction on books and other readings, especially for those new to history; and Walks and Workshops, for heritage walks and focused workshops, like the one we are currently attending, as part of the collaboration with Yellow Veranda Experiences.

According to Soumya Jayaraj, the founder of Yellow Veranda Experiences, which is located in Sthala, a heritage space in Ulsoor, “We thought we would curate unique experiences around these spaces that are rich in history and heritage,” she says. This led to collaborations with experts such as Lathashree. “We were interested in the Someshwara Temple for its history and its iconography. We enjoy incorporating such subjects into our heritage experiences,” she says of the walk, which ended with a hot South Indian breakfast and excellent coffee, throughly enjoyed by the small, ecclectic group of people who attended the experience.

One of them is senior plant biologist R. Ganesan. This walk, he says, made him think about how the city’s botanical history is tied to historical events, whether it was Kempe Gowda, the Mughals, Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan or the British. “It was a learning to hear about the development of Bangalore and how the temples store the information and chronicle it,” says Ganesan, an adjunct fellow at Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE),

Another participant, Meghana Laxman Patgar, a city-based content creator who runs the Instagram page Yo Bengaluru, is also impressed with Lathashree’s knowledge and patience. “She explained everything beautifully, answering every question and doubt, and also allowed people to share their stories,” she says.

Besides helping spread awareness about history, Lathashree feels these sessions also nudge us to think about who we are and where we came from. She recalls a moment as a student when she held a million-year-old hand axe and realised how that object connected her to someone, not even a modern human, who inhabited this world all those years ago. “It was a moment when the past became sacred. That is what I want them to understand.”

For more details or to collaborate with Chai with History, visit its Instagram page, chaiwithhistory

World.title: As three-year mark nears, Bhajan Lal Sharma seeks to shed ‘Parchi CM’ tag
World.content:
When Bhajan Lal Sharma, a first-time MLA who had largely remained in the background of the BJP’s Rajasthan unit, was named Chief Minister in December 2023, Congress State president Govind Singh Dotasara dismissed him as the “Parchi CM”, a leader chosen by the party’s central leadership rather than one who had built a political base of his own.

Nearly three years later, Mr. Dotasara has changed his line of attack. He now accuses the Mr. Sharma of being a leader “jisne poori BJP ko Rajasthan me khatam kar dala” (who has finished off the entire BJP in Rajasthan).

World.title: Keralam’s 15th Five-Year-Plan: Govt to explore possibilities in small modular reactors in the ‘longer-term’
World.content:
Keralam will explore, among other options, the possibilities offered by nuclear energy for energy security in the longer-term, according to the Approach Paper to the 15th Five Year Plan (for the 2027-2032 period) published on Wednesday.

“For the longer term, the State will assess small modular reactors (SMR) for feasibility, safety, siting and grid implications,” the Approach Paper drafted by the State Planning Board said. Elsewhere, the paper observed that systematic investment in local battery energy storage systems (BESS), large BESS, pumped storage and modular reactors is the way forward given that Keralam generates only 25% of its electricity demand internally.

The Approach Paper said Keralam will aim for an “informed decision” on the subject, “with the option kept open.” “This is a Union subject, and the State’s role covers siting, grid readiness and engagement,” it said. Green hydrogen and offshore wind will be assessed on the same basis. Alongside energy storage, the Plan also will promote household and decentralised generation.

SMRs are an evolving technology. According to the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) definition, they are nuclear reactors with a power capacity of up to 300 MWe, about one-third the capacity of conventional nuclear reactors. In India, under the Nuclear Energy Mission announced in the 2025-26 Union Budget, ₹20,000 crore has been earmarked for research, design, development and deployment of SMRs. According to the Union government, the Department of Atomic Energy is working on the 220 MWe Bharat Small Modular Reactor (BSMR-200), the 55 MWe Small Modular Reactor (SMR-55) and a high-temperature gas-cooled reactor for hydrogen generation.

Proposals for establishing a nuclear power plant in Keralam in the 1980s had been met with a public outcry regarding safety, prompting successive State governments to be wary of the subject.

As Keralam draws up its 15th Plan, its power sector is in sharp focus. In recent months, the sector has been in the news over peak-hour electricity shortages and controversies over power purchase deals. At the same time, the State’s renewable capacity has risen from 572.42 MW in 2020-21 to 2382.34 MW in December 2025. Most of it is solar power, and much of that generated through household rooftop systems.

Energy, alongside higher education and employment generation form critical areas of the 15th Plan, Planning Board Vice-Chairman K.M. Chandrasekhar had said in a recent interview to The Hindu. Electricity is one area where the State will have to find large-scale investment, he said. According to the Approach Paper, the State’s ‘growth engine’ needs reliable power and preparations for ensuring long-term energy security should start now, since it would take more than five years to deliver results.

World.title: Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting LIVE: Leaders meet with nuclear arms and two wars on table
World.content:
When President Donald Trump meets on Thursday (November 19, 2026) with China’s Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, it could mark a pivot in world history — or become a quickly forgotten photo op.

Mr. Trump, who will test his reputation as an expert dealmaker in the trilateral meeting, has promoted his time with Mr. Xi and Mr. Putin — two of America’s leading rivals — as a chance to hash out rules for controlling nuclear arms and to start resolving the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Experts have kept expectations low for major breakthroughs.

Mr. Trump plans to have a separate one-on-one meeting with Mr. Xi — his third substantial meeting with him this year — right before the trilateral. He also added a separate sit-down with Mr. Putin to his schedule, marking the first time that the leaders have held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year that failed to broker a deal to ease Russia’s war in Ukraine.

U.S. officials said the three leaders will likely discuss, among other issues, the war in Ukraine, the situation in Iran, global energy stability, and nuclear arms control.

Officials have described the rare trilateral leaders’ summit as more of an exploratory and symbolic meeting, playing down the likelihood of substantive outcomes, either with regard to a possible Russia-Ukraine deal or on the West Asian crisis. Whether they can see eye-to-eye on nuclear disarmament also remains to be seen.

World.title: Dual reporting structures built into the new police system in Bengaluru, raise concerns
World.content:
The restructuring of Bengaluru City Police into five commissionerates with a Chief Commissioner has several dual reporting structures built into it, which could potentially cause administrative issues, several senior police officials have flagged, on Wednesday following the government order on the restructuring. They have pointed out that hierarchy and chain of command was key in the police and that was not clear in the new organisational structure, even as roles are also yet to be defined properly.

For instance, the five police commissioners will directly report to the Director-General and Inspector-General of Police (DG&IGP), Karnataka, the order says, but while defining the role of the Chief Commissioner it said he would supervise the five commissioners. The order even acknowledges the confusion and says any clarification about mutual powers and functions of the Chief Commissioner of Police and Commissioners of Police of the five commissionerates will be clarified by the government for their smooth functioning. While the chain of command for the Law and Order functions of the police in the city remains clear, both traffic and crime seem to be marred by dual reporting structures that can cause confusion and put the lower bureaucracy under stress over conflicting orders and hamper a coherent strategy.

For the traffic police, the additional layer has created confusion for Deputy Commissioners of Police (DCPs), as they will now have to report to both the local commissioners and the Commissioner of Police (Traffic). Speaking to The Hindu, senior officers who have previously held the position of Traffic DCPs in the city said the new hierarchy could create complications in obtaining approvals, planning, and coordinating with civic bodies.

Currently, all planning functions of the Bengaluru Traffic Police fall under the ambit of the Joint Commissioner of Police. However, while the new order places the responsibility for planning city traffic with the Commissioner of Police (Traffic), there is no clarity on which aspects the Traffic DCPs will have to report to the local commissioners.

While each commissionerate has a DCP (Crime), there is also an Additional Commissioner (Anti-Rowdy Squad) at the city level, both of which are expected to replace the erstwhile Central Crime Branch. Hemanth M. Nimbalkar has also been tasked with “supervising crime control” across the city. This has also created a dual reporting structure for crime.

A senior police officer said the hierarchy could create pressure, with its effects cascading down to inspectors and lower-ranking officers.“For instance, if we have a case in hand and one officer suggests one method of investigation and another suggests a different one, which of the two should the DCP choose? This could further percolate down to the inspector if the pressure mounts on the DCP,” the officer explained.

Even local-level planning, including crime monitoring and patrolling strategies, could be affected by such conflicts, leading to a substantial burden on officers and delays in implementing plans, the officer said.

World.title: Tamil Nadu Police launch e-CSR facility to enable online filing of complaints
World.content:
The Tamil Nadu Director-General of Police and Head of Police Force, Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal, on Wednesday launched the e-CSR (electronic Community Service Register) facility at the State Police Headquarters here.

The initiative, aimed at making it easier for the public, particularly senior citizens and women, to lodge complaints online without having to visit police stations, is another step towards ensuring transparency in the police system, Dr. Aggarwal said.

“People are unhappy when their complaints are not acknowledged through the issuance of a CSR at police stations. They can now lodge complaints relating to minor offences online and receive an e-CSR on their mobile phones through SMS,” he said.

Complainants can approach the jurisdictional police station with the e-CSR and other relevant documents to obtain a regular CSR or have an FIR registered, as applicable, within three days.

Senior police officers would monitor the progress of e-CSR complaints and the number of cases subsequently converted into regular CSRs or FIRs. The e-FIR facility, introduced last month exclusively for cybercrime offences, had received a good response, he said.

e-FIR for mobile phone, two-wheeler thefts soon

Dr. Aggarwal said the e-FIR facility would soon be extended to cases involving missing or stolen mobile phones and two-wheelers.

Responding to a question on the possibility of misuse of the e-CSR facility, he said any such initiative could be misused. However, the police would proceed with further action only after establishing a prima facie case.

Zero tolerance towards custodial violence

Dr. Aggarwal said the Tamil Nadu Police had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards custodial violence. The recent custodial death reported at the Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai district had been handed over to the Crime Branch-CID for investigation.

“We have instructed officials to ensure that people visiting police stations are covered by CCTV cameras at all times. Firm action will be taken wherever any lapse on the part of the police is established,” he said.

“Law and Order is being maintained well in the State. The average number of murders reported between January and November over the past five years stood at 1,421, while the figure had declined to 1,306 during the corresponding period this year,” he said.

Most murders were attributed to family disputes, illicit relationships and petty or verbal quarrels. Only 1% of the cases were linked to previous enmity involving rowdy elements, he said.

There had also been a significant increase in the registration of drug-related offences, seizure of contraband substances and the arrest of accused persons, he added.

Though the number of political agitations in Tamil Nadu increased by 35% compared with the previous year, there was no untoward incident since adequate bandobust arrangements were being made despite vacancies at various levels in the police force.

The Tamil Nadu Uniformed Services Recruitment Board had recently completed the recruitment of 3,000 police constables. The process of recruiting 1,200 Sub-Inspectors would also be completed soon. About 29,000 additional posts had been sanctioned to the police force by the Chief Minister, he said.

World.title: Jayaprakash Narayan’s private secretary T. Abraham passes away
World.content:
T. Abraham, who served as private secretary to Socialist stalwart Jayaprakash Narayan, passed away on Wednesday. He was 93. Abraham breathed his last at his residence at Mavelikkara.

He had also served as public relations officer with the Tata group.

He is survived by his wife Ammini Abraham and children Mini Jacob, Prakash, and Prabhash. The funeral prayers will be conducted at his residence at 10 a.m. on Friday, followed by the funeral service at 11 a.m. at St. Mary’s Orthodox Church (Muttel Church), Kuttamperoor.

Condoling his death, Varughese George, secretary general of RJD, remembered that Abraham had served as private secretary to JP from the Sarvodaya period to the post-Emergency days.

Abraham’s biography titled Jayaprakash Narayanante Nizhalayi Oraal by Fr. Abraham Koshy Kunnumpurath, was released a few years ago.

World.title: Abdul Shukkoor murder case: CBI court to pronounce verdict today
World.content:
A Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) Special Court will pronounce a verdict in the case relating to the murder of Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) worker Abdul Shukkoor on Thursday (November 19, 2026).

The case assumed political significance after former Kannur district secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) P. Jayarajan and former MLA and then Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) State secretary T.V. Rajesh were arraigned as accused numbers 32 and 33. The court had earlier refused to quash the trial proceedings against them. Of the 33 accused in the case, two have since died.

Shukkoor, 21, a native of Ariyil near Taliparamba, was hacked to death by a group of assailants at Keezhara under the Kannapuram police station limits on February 20, 2012. The murder was allegedly carried out in retaliation for an attack on Mr. Jayarajan and Mr. Rajesh during their visit to tension-hit Ariyil earlier that morning. Shukkoor and four other youths, who had taken refuge in a house at Keezhara, were allegedly forced to leave the premises after a group of CPI(M) workers intimidated the house owners.

The police said their captors photographed them using mobile phones and verified their identities with party workers. Following the purported verification, three of them were released. Shukkoor and Zakaria were then taken to a nearby field and stabbed. While Shukkoor succumbed to his injuries, Zakaria, who also sustained stab injuries, managed to escape

Mr. Jayarajan and Mr. Rajesh were charged under Section 118 of the Indian Penal Code after investigators found that they allegedly had prior knowledge of the conspiracy to kill Shukkoor. The conspiracy was purportedly hatched in a room at the Taliparamba Co-operative Hospital, where they had been admitted on February 20 following an attack on Mr. Jayarajan’s convoy by alleged IUML workers earlier the same day.

The Kerala High Court ordered a CBI probe into the incident while allowing a writ petition filed by Shukkoor’s mother, A.C. Aathikka, in 2016.

World.title: Suparco warns of worsening smog across Punjab
World.content:
LAHORE: The Pakistan Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (Suparco) has warned of worsening smog conditions across Punjab over the next three days, with satellite observations detecting 690 active fire incidents in Punjab and adjoining transboundary areas, while Lahore on Wednesday topped the list of the world’s most polluted major cities.

According to Suparco’s smog assessment for Nov 17, satellite observations recorded 386 active fire detections in Punjab and 304 in the transboundary region during the preceding 24 hours. The assessment covered 36 districts and used VIIRS and MODIS satellite observations to identify fire incidents.

The bulletin identified seven districts – Jhang, Narowal, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Gujranwala and Dera Ghazi Khan – as having high or severe smog conditions.

The mean aerosol optical depth (AOD), an indicator of atmospheric aerosol concentration, was recorded at 0.25, with the highest levels over Chiniot, Jhang and Faisalabad. Tropospheric nitrogen dioxide (NO2), however, was 21pc below the 2019-2025 average for this time of the year.

Jhang, Narowal, Sheikhupura, Sialkot, Hafizabad, Gujranwala and DGK to have high or severe smog conditions in coming days

Despite the lower NO2 levels compared with the historical average, the satellite assessment warned that atmospheric conditions were likely to deteriorate over the following three days.

The Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS) model projected PM2.5 concentrations of around 51 to 71 micrograms per cubic metre.

Suparco cautioned that model estimates were generally lower than ground-based monitoring readings during winter. Atmospheric dispersion was also assessed as very poor, indicating that pollutants were likely to remain trapped close to the ground.

The satellite-based monitoring is intended to track the geographical spread of smog, identify fire hotspots and provide an assessment of atmospheric conditions across Punjab.

Meanwhile, Lahore remained at the top of IQAir’s global major city pollution ranking on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) of 339 during the 10am-11am period.

The city’s air quality subsequently improved, with the AQI falling to 167 at 5pm, but began deteriorating again, reaching 178 at 6pm.

In the global ranking, Lahore was followed by Dhaka with an AQI of 221, Baghdad 199, Tashkent 182 and Kolkata 178. Karachi ranked sixth with an AQI of 174.

The real-time Pakistan city ranking showed hazardous pollution levels in several other Punjab cities. Faisalabad topped the national list with an AQI of 686, followed by Gujranwala at 550, Kahna Nau at 516, Multan at 437, Kasur at 371 and Lahore at 339. Khanewal recorded an AQI of 327, Sargodha 314, Sahiwal 253 and Dera Ghazi Khan 238. Readings above 300 fall in the hazardous category.

The Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) also forecast fog and smog at isolated places in Lahore, Sialkot, Narowal, Sheikhupura, Okara, Kasur, Faisalabad, Jhang, Khanewal, Multan and surrounding areas during morning and night over the next 48 hours. Dry weather is expected across most districts, with no significant rainfall forecast.

Meanwhile, the Punjab Environment Protection Agency (EPA) deployed five senior directors from its headquarters across different divisions to supervise anti-stubble burning operations and coordinate with agriculture officials and district administrations.

EPA Director General Abdullah Nayyer Sheikh said the deployment was aimed at ensuring direct supervision of field operations, verifying reported fire incidents and ensuring timely action against crop-residue burning.

In Multan, the district administration has received two modern anti-smog gun vehicles on the directives of Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.

Deputy Commissioner Dr Faisal Saleem said the vehicles would operate round the clock and spray water in different parts of the city during morning and evening hours. He said the administration was also taking action against people burning crop residues and garbage.

Published in Dawn, November 19th, 2026

World.title: PTI’s legal eagles ‘shake and make up’
World.content:
• Raja, Khosa deny internal rifts; Gohar maintains all decisions taken on Imran’s directions

• PTI warns Adiala authorities against violating SC orders on ex-PM’s medical treatment

• IHC directs proper medical care, hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules

ISLAMABAD: PTI Sec­r­e­tary General Salman Akram Raja and senior lawyer Sardar Latif Khosa — who were reportedly divided over the question of engaging with the establishment — appea­r­ed to have resolved their beef on Wednesday, as both leaders shook hands and declared that there was no discord within the party.

Speaking to the media outside the Islamabad High Court, both leaders maintained there was complete discipline and cohesion within the party.

Mr Raja said attempts to create divisions within the PTI would not succeed. He stepped forward and shook hands with Mr Kho­sa. In response, Mr Khosa smiled and said Mr Raja is his junior (barkhurdar).

It may be recalled that rumours had been circulating within the party that Mr Khosa and his group favoured holding negotiations and increasing engagement with the establishment. Mr Raja’s group, however, was said to favour maintaining a hard line against the establishment and avoiding any gesture that could suggest the PTI had weakened and was left with no option but to hold talks.

Earlier, Mr Raja had acknowledged differences with Mr Khosa and Salman Safdar after their meeting with Imran Khan, amid speculation that the PTI founder wanted major changes within the party.

But on Wednesday, Mr Raja said that Imran Khan’s letter, conveyed by Mr Safdar, was intended to awaken the conscience of the judiciary and the nati­­on and prompt them to act.

“As a party, we will play the role that is our duty. The health of Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi is very important to us,” he said.

Mr Safdar said the case against the PTI founder was controversial, adding that several questions had been raised about the decision in the Al-Qadir case. He said it was concerning that the media had already predicted the outcome of the case.

PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said he was unaware of the purpose behind PPP chief Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s recent press conference. However, he described it as a positive development that everyone had finally accepted the PTI’s position.

He also said the PTI did not believe in power-sharing and that all decisions were taken in accordance with Imran Khan’s directions. He said the PTI would not make any irresponsible statements on the issue of new provinces and would keep its cards close to its chest.

PTI letter to Adiala jail admin

Meanwhile, the PTI on Wednesday sent a letter to the Adiala jail administration, warning it against violating Supreme Court orders on the provision of medical treatment to incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan and urging his transfer to Shifa International Hospital.

Advocate Khalid Yousuf Chaudhry told Dawn that the PTI had learnt through the media that the jail administration had taken Imran Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for treatment.

“It is nothing but contempt of the Supreme Court. We urge that he [Imran] should be immediately shifted to Shifa International Hospital in accordance with the Supreme Court’s orders and provided proper treatment. That is what I have written in the letter,” he said.

The letter comprises 44 pages, including the SC order of Aug 18, directing Mr Khan’s transfer to Shifa International Hospital, the Islamabad High Court order of Aug 6 regarding facilities, Barrister Salman Safdar’s open letter on behalf of the PTI founder and his amicus curiae report submitted to the SC.

The letter, dated Nov 12 but sent to the Adiala jail administration and several other relevant offices on Wednesday, states that the jail administration must ensure implementation of the binding judicial directives issued by the Supreme Court.

Medical care for Bushra Bibi

Meanwhile on Wednesday, the Islamabad High Court directed prison authorities to ensure medical care and hygienic living conditions for Bushra Bibi as per prison rules, while adjourning for seven days the appeals filed by her and her husband against their convictions in the £190 million case.

The couple is serving prison sentences in the Al-Qadir Trust case. On Jan 17, 2025, an accountability court in Islamabad sentenced Imran Khan to 14 years in prison and Bushra Bibi to seven years in the case. Both subsequently challenged their convictions before the IHC.

An IHC division bench comprising Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and Justice Muhammad Asif granted Barrister Salman Safdar, counsel for the PTI founder, seven days to prepare arguments on the appeals.

During proceedings, the court also took up a fresh miscellaneous application filed on behalf of Bushra Bibi, raising concerns about her deteriorating eyesight, need for surgery, possible post-operative complications and the medical facilities available to her in prison.

After hearing arguments from her counsel, Sardar Latif Khosa, the bench directed the prison authorities to ensure cleanliness in her cell, arrange an examination by a specialist doctor from a hospital and provide all necessary medical facilities in accordance with jail rules.

The court further directed Islamabad Advocate General Naveed Hayat Malik to ensure that its order was implemented through the relevant prison authorities.

Published in Dawn, November 19th, 2026

World.title: Petrol and diesel prices reduced by Rs3 per litre each
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the prices of both petrol and diesel by Rs3 per litre, marking the twelfth consecutive decrease in the rate of petrol.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs322 per litre, while HSD will remain at Rs355 on Nov 19 (Thursday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

Following Tuesday’s reduction of the petrol price to Rs325 per litre, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar highlighted the government’s “proactive measures including policy changes and structural reforms in petroleum policy” that had brought prices back down from their April 3 peak and provided relief through a fuel subsidy scheme.

“The government of Pakistan remains committed to continue making all possible efforts to ease the financial burden on the common man amid global challenges,” he said.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Nov 2, for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This allows a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

On Sept 17, the government rolled out the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme across the country to ease the public’s burden amid rising fuel prices due to the Middle East situation.

The subsidy scheme applies to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

Since July 17 , the government has been revising fuel prices on a near-daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the conflict. The federal government had also announced targeted relief measures in April to provide subsidised fuel.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: FBR unveils proposed rules for faceless tax appeals
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) unveiled draft rules on Wednesday for its faceless income tax appeals system, eliminating the need for physical interaction between taxpayers and appellate authorities.

The new system will also conceal the identity of officers responsible for deciding tax disputes. The rules are expected to be finalised this week, following feedback from stakeholders.

Under the proposed system, the Commissioner (Appeals) will not be identified during hearings via video link, and their voice will be electronically modified to prevent disclosure of identity.

The draft rules were notified through SRO 2136 of 2026 to amend the Income Tax Rules, 2002, by inserting a separate chapter on faceless appeals.

The entire appeal process, from filing and submission of evidence to hearings and issuance of final orders, will be conducted electronically through FBR’s Iris portal, or any other designated automated system.

A separate appeals wing/centre will be established in Islamabad, comprising appellate units, each headed by a Commissioner (Appeals). The wing will function under the administrative control of the FBR’s Member (Legal) Inland Revenue.

However, the director general, chief commissioner or any other authority will not be allowed to exercise control over, or issue directions, to a Commissioner (Appeals) regarding the hearing or decision of an appeal.

FBR or the Centre may also transfer pending appeals from one appellate unit to another through the automated system to ensure equitable workload distribution, efficiency and impartiality.

All notices, requisitions, written submissions, arguments and evidence will be exchanged exclusively through the electronic portal. Neither taxpayers nor tax officials or their authorised representatives will be allowed to appear physically before the appellate authority.

Taxpayers will, however, have the option of seeking a decision on their appeals based solely on written submissions. In such cases, the respondent tax authorities will be allowed to submit written comments, while taxpayers will retain the right to reply.

All virtual hearings will be recorded and digitally archived as part of the electronic record of the appeal.

World.title: FBISE introduces on-the-spot printing of question papers
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (FBISE) has taken a major step towards preventing question paper leaks by introducing an on-the-spot printing system at examination centres, which will also reduce transportation and bank storage costs.

During the ongoing second annual examinations, the FBISE has introduced the facility at 35 examination centres and plans to phase out the manual, bank-based distribution of question papers across all centres within the next year.

“We are receiving very good feedback from 35 centres where we share question papers online just 15 minutes before the start of the examination. Only the superintendent and head of the school, through their separate passwords, can access the question papers. They can then print the required number of copies using their printers,” FBISE Chairman Dr Ikram Ali Malik told Dawn.

He said the board would pay the respective schools for the number of question papers printed.

“This online paper distribution system has been successfully operating at our foreign examination centres since 2018. A few years ago, it was also introduced at local examination centres but was later discontinued. However, we have now decided to introduce the system gradually. Our target is to implement it at all 1,000 centres within a year,” he said.

He added that schools and colleges were being consulted about the availability of internet facilities at their examination centres.

“Online paper distribution is a very good experience. It is a cost-effective and time-saving initiative,” he said.

The FBISE chairman said the board was also planning to introduce a computer-based testing system for the multiple-choice questions (MCQs) portion of examinations.

“We are in talks with schools and colleges to complete arrangements for alternative energy sources to ensure uninterrupted functioning of computer laboratories,” Dr Malik said. He added that, under the proposed system, examinations would comprise 50pc descriptive questions and 50pc MCQs.

“We want to introduce this system in the annual examinations of Class 9 and first-year students in 2027,” he said, adding that computer-based testing would initially cover MCQs in five subjects, including Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Mathematics and Computer Science.

“Through this system, human involvement in checking MCQs will be eliminated, and students will receive their results on the same day through the system,” he said.

He added that one major computer laboratory shared by a cluster of four to five schools would be sufficient to conduct computer-based tests. Talks with schools and colleges in this regard were under way.

Meanwhile, the Higher Education Commission (HEC), through its Education Testing Council (ETC), successfully conducted the 35th Law Admission Test (LAT) to ensure standardised, transparent and merit-based admission testing across the country, according to a press release issued by the commission.

As many as 42,547 candidates registered for the examination, while more than 35,523 appeared at 103 examination centres in 28 cities across the country, the statement said.
